p1.en: To confess or accept that something is true, often unwillingly.
p1.ex1: He admitted feeling nervous before the exam.
p1.ex2: They admitted the plan had some serious flaws.
p1.example: She finally admitted that she had made a mistake.

p1.en: In opposition to someone or something.
p1.ex1: Are you for or against the new policy?
p1.ex2: She voted against the proposal at the meeting.
p1.example: He was against the idea of moving to another city.

p1.en: Feeling relaxed and comfortable in a situation.
p1.ex1: She felt completely at ease with her new colleagues.
p1.ex2: He put the nervous guest at ease with a warm smile.
p1.example: The teacher made the students feel at ease during the test.

p1.en: To be very easy to do.
p1.ex1: Don't worry — fixing this bug will be a piece of cake.
p1.ex2: He said the job interview was a piece of cake.
p1.example: The final exam was a piece of cake for her.

p1.en: To support or agree with something.
p1.ex1: The manager is in favour of flexible working hours.
p1.ex2: Are you in favour of the new environmental policy?
p1.example: Most students are in favour of shorter school days.

p1.ru: быть на седьмом небе от счастья
p1.en: To be extremely happy and excited.
p1.ex1: He was over the moon after his team won the championship.
p1.ex2: They were over the moon to hear the good news.
p1.example: She was over the moon when she got the scholarship.

p1.en: To be in a stressful situation where you must perform or decide quickly.
p1.ex1: He works best when he is under pressure.
p1.ex2: She felt under pressure to finish the project on time.
p1.example: Teachers are often under pressure to improve test scores.

p1.en: A plan showing how much money you have and how you will spend it.
p1.ex1: They had to cut costs to stay within the budget.
p1.ex2: Planning a budget helps you avoid unnecessary spending.
p1.example: The school has a limited budget for extracurricular activities.

p1.en: To become exciting, active, or interesting.
p1.ex1: Her novel really comes to life in the final chapters.
p1.ex2: The classroom came to life when the teacher started the experiment.
p1.example: The city comes to life during the festival season.

p1.en: To think of or produce a new idea or plan.
p1.ex1: Can you come up with a better title for the essay?
p1.ex2: The team came up with an innovative marketing strategy.
p1.example: She came up with a brilliant solution to the problem.

p1.en: The ability to share information clearly and effectively with others.
p1.ex1: She improved her communication skills by joining a debate club.
p1.ex2: Employers often value strong communication skills in candidates.
p1.example: Good communication skills are essential in any workplace.

p1.en: To have power over something and manage how it works.
p1.ex1: The government aims to control inflation.
p1.ex2: You need to control the speed of the machine carefully.
p1.example: He struggled to control his emotions during the argument.

p1.en: To handle, manage, or take action regarding something.
p1.ex1: We need to deal with this issue before it gets worse.
p1.ex2: He had to deal with a lot of stress at work.
p1.example: She knows how to deal with difficult customers professionally.

p1.en: To become smaller in size, amount, or number; the act of reducing.
p1.ex1: There has been a decrease in air pollution this year.
p1.ex2: Sales decreased sharply during the economic crisis.
p1.example: The number of students decreased after the holidays.

p1.en: Requiring a lot of effort, skill, or patience.
p1.ex1: The training programme was physically demanding.
p1.ex2: She found the new role extremely demanding but rewarding.
p1.example: Being a doctor is one of the most demanding jobs in the world.

p1.en: To feel or go through something directly.
p1.ex1: He experienced a sense of achievement after completing the marathon.
p1.ex2: Many people experience stress during exam periods.
p1.example: Travellers often experience culture shock in new countries.

p1.en: Comments or reactions from others about your work or behaviour.
p1.ex1: He welcomed feedback from his colleagues to improve his performance.
p1.ex2: Please share your feedback after using the new app.
p1.example: The teacher gave the students detailed feedback on their essays.

p1.en: A sum of money saved or collected for a particular purpose.
p1.ex1: They raised a large fund to support local charities.
p1.ex2: The government allocated a special fund for education reform.
p1.example: The school set up a fund to help students buy textbooks.

p1.en: The process of increasing or developing over time.
p1.ex1: Personal growth often comes from facing challenges.
p1.ex2: Economic growth has slowed down in recent months.
p1.example: The company showed impressive growth in just one year.

p1.en: A strong effect or influence that something has on another.
p1.ex1: The new law had a positive impact on air quality.
p1.ex2: The teacher's words had a lasting impact on his students.
p1.example: Social media has had a huge impact on modern communication.

p1.en: To become or make greater in number, amount, or degree.
p1.ex1: There has been a sharp increase in online learning.
p1.ex2: Exercise can increase your energy levels significantly.
p1.example: The school fees will increase by 10% next year.

p1.en: To have an effect on how someone thinks or acts.
p1.ex1: Her parents greatly influenced her career choices.
p1.ex2: Music has the power to influence your mood.
p1.example: Advertising can strongly influence consumer behaviour.

p1.en: A feeling of excitement that gives you new ideas or motivation.
p1.ex1: She found inspiration in her grandmother's stories.
p1.ex2: The speech gave the volunteers a great deal of inspiration.
p1.example: Nature was the main inspiration behind the artist's work.

p1.en: Used to say that something is not important.
p1.ex1: 'I forgot to bring the book.' 'It doesn't matter, we have a copy.'
p1.ex2: It doesn't matter how long it takes, as long as you do it well.
p1.example: It doesn't matter if you make a mistake — just keep trying.

p1.en: Small in amount or restricted in some way.
p1.ex1: Access to clean water is still limited in some regions.
p1.ex2: The library has a limited number of books on this topic.
p1.example: We have limited time, so let's focus on the key points.

p1.en: More than half of a group.
p1.ex1: A large majority voted in favour of the new rule.
p1.ex2: The majority of people prefer to shop online these days.
p1.example: The majority of students passed the final exam.

p1.en: To move forward or improve over time.
p1.ex1: The team is making good progress on the new project.
p1.ex2: You need to make progress every day to reach your goals.
p1.example: She has made excellent progress in her English studies.

p1.en: Done by hand rather than by machine.
p1.ex1: This car has a manual gearbox.
p1.ex2: He prefers manual tools to electric ones.
p1.example: Many factories are replacing manual work with automation.

p1.en: Relating to the mind or thinking.
p1.ex1: Solving puzzles is a great mental workout.
p1.ex2: Mental strength is just as important as physical ability.
p1.example: Physical exercise can also improve your mental health.

p1.en: Less than half of a group; a small group that differs from the majority.
p1.ex1: Minority languages deserve protection and support.
p1.ex2: A small minority of people still doubt climate change.
p1.example: Only a minority of students disagreed with the new timetable.

p1.en: Used to say something is (or is not) true or factual.
p1.ex1: It's not the case that all teenagers are lazy.
p1.ex2: Many assume success is only about talent, but that's rarely the case.
p1.example: People think learning a language is difficult, but that's not always the case.

p1.en: Relating to the body rather than the mind.
p1.ex1: The job requires a lot of physical effort.
p1.ex2: She enjoys physical challenges like rock climbing.
p1.example: Physical activity is essential for a healthy lifestyle.

p1.en: To be an important part of something.
p1.ex1: Technology plays a significant role in modern healthcare.
p1.ex2: Volunteers play an important role in disaster relief efforts.
p1.word: play an important / a significant role
p1.example: Parents play an important role in their children's education.

p1.en: The ability or capacity to develop or succeed in the future.
p1.ex1: This project has great potential for growth.
p1.ex2: The teacher saw potential in even the weakest students.
p1.example: Every student has the potential to achieve great things.

p1.en: To a certain degree; more precisely.
p1.ex1: I'd rather stay home tonight than go to the party.
p1.ex2: The weather is rather cold for this time of year.
p1.example: The exam was rather difficult, but most students passed.

p1.en: To suggest that someone should do or use something.
p1.ex1: The doctor recommended that she rest for a week.
p1.ex2: Can you recommend a good restaurant nearby?
p1.example: I would recommend this book to anyone interested in history.

p1.en: To refuse to accept or approve something.
p1.ex1: His application was rejected because of missing documents.
p1.ex2: She rejected the offer and decided to start her own business.
p1.example: The committee rejected the proposal due to lack of funding.

p1.en: To write something again in a different or improved way.
p1.ex1: He decided to rewrite the entire report from scratch.
p1.ex2: After feedback, she rewrote the first paragraph completely.
p1.example: The teacher asked the student to rewrite the essay more clearly.

p1.en: The state of being protected from harm or danger.
p1.ex1: The company prioritises the safety of its employees.
p1.ex2: Wearing a helmet is important for your safety while cycling.
p1.example: Road safety is a major concern in urban areas.

p1.en: Pleased or content with something.
p1.ex1: Are you satisfied with the service you received?
p1.ex2: He was not fully satisfied with his performance.
p1.example: She was satisfied with the results of her hard work.

p1.en: A plan that shows when things will happen.
p1.ex1: She manages a very busy schedule every week.
p1.ex2: We need to adjust the schedule to meet the deadline.
p1.example: The train schedule has been updated due to roadworks.

p1.en: Important or large enough to have a noticeable effect.
p1.ex1: The discovery made a significant contribution to science.
p1.ex2: His absence had a significant impact on the team's performance.
p1.example: There has been a significant improvement in air quality.

p1.en: The place, person, or thing that something comes from.
p1.ex1: Please cite your sources at the end of the essay.
p1.ex2: Sunlight is the primary source of energy for plants.
p1.example: The internet is a major source of information today.

p1.en: To agree with and help promote an idea or person.
p1.ex1: Do you support the new school policy?
p1.ex2: She publicly supported the campaign for better public transport.
p1.example: Most of the class supported the idea of a class trip.

p1.en: To stop thinking about something by doing something else.
p1.ex1: He watched a film to take his mind off the stressful week.
p1.ex2: Listening to music helps me take my mind off worries.
p1.example: A short walk can help you take your mind off problems.

p1.en: To think in a creative and unconventional way.
p1.ex1: The project requires students to think outside the box.
p1.ex2: She always thinks outside the box when solving problems.
p1.example: Good entrepreneurs know how to think outside the box.

p1.en: During the whole period of something.
p1.ex1: She remained loyal to her team throughout the project.
p1.ex2: Throughout history, people have faced and overcome challenges.
p1.example: The company has grown significantly throughout the years.

p1.en: At any time or every time that something happens.
p1.ex1: You can call me whenever you need help.
p1.ex2: Whenever she sings, the whole room falls silent.
p1.example: Whenever I feel stressed, I go for a walk.

p1.en: Used to strongly agree with what someone has said.
p1.ex1: When she said teamwork is essential, he said he couldn't agree more.
p1.ex2: I couldn't agree more with your point about the importance of reading.
p1.example: 'Learning a second language opens many doors.' 'I couldn't agree more.'

p2.en: To plan or organise something in advance.
p2.ex1: Can you arrange a meeting for next Tuesday?
p2.ex2: He arranged all the books on the shelf alphabetically.
p2.example: She arranged a surprise party for her friend's birthday.

p2.en: To increase or improve something.
p2.ex1: The new campaign boosted sales by 30%.
p2.ex2: Positive feedback can boost a student's confidence significantly.
p2.example: Exercise can boost your energy and mood.

p2.en: To work together with others towards a shared goal.
p2.ex1: The two countries agreed to cooperate on environmental issues.
p2.ex2: Students cooperated well during the group presentation.
p2.example: All team members must cooperate to finish the project on time.

p2.en: The ability to analyse information carefully and make reasoned judgements.
p2.ex1: The course is designed to develop students' critical thinking skills.
p2.ex2: She used her critical thinking skills to evaluate the data.
p2.example: Critical thinking skills are vital for success in higher education.

p2.en: Not harmful to the environment.
p2.ex1: The new packaging is eco-friendly and fully recyclable.
p2.ex2: They switched to eco-friendly transport to cut emissions.
p2.example: More people are choosing eco-friendly products to reduce pollution.

p2.en: Providing useful knowledge or information.
p2.ex1: The museum offers a range of educational programmes for children.
p2.ex2: She prefers educational games over simple entertainment apps.
p2.example: The documentary was both entertaining and educational.

p2.en: Interesting and enjoyable to watch, listen to, or take part in.
p2.ex1: He is known for his entertaining lectures.
p2.ex2: The evening was entertaining thanks to the live music.
p2.example: The film was entertaining from start to finish.

p2.en: To create or develop something, or to come together as a group.
p2.ex1: Ice forms when water temperature drops below zero.
p2.ex2: She helped form a new environmental club at school.
p2.example: The students formed a study group before the exams.

p2.en: To communicate or work together with others.
p2.ex1: The app allows users to interact with each other in real time.
p2.ex2: She interacts confidently with both students and colleagues.
p2.example: Children learn social skills when they interact with their peers.

p2.en: Things you are required or expected to do.
p2.ex1: He took his obligations to his team very seriously.
p2.ex2: Students must be aware of their obligations regarding attendance.
p2.example: As a citizen, you have certain rights and obligations.

p2.en: More than usual; especially.
p2.ex1: I particularly enjoyed the last chapter of the book.
p2.ex2: The weather was particularly cold this January.
p2.example: She is particularly good at maths and science.

p2.en: To make something smaller or less in size, amount, or degree.
p2.ex1: Regular exercise helps to reduce the risk of heart disease.
p2.ex2: The company reduced its prices to attract more customers.
p2.example: We should reduce the amount of plastic we use every day.

p2.en: Giving a sense of pleasure or fulfilment.
p2.ex1: It is satisfying to finish a project you have worked hard on.
p2.ex2: She found her new job far more satisfying than the previous one.
p2.example: Helping others can be one of the most satisfying experiences.

p2.en: To spend time with other people in a friendly and relaxed way.
p2.ex1: She loves to socialise with her colleagues after work.
p2.ex2: Moving to a new city can make it harder to socialise at first.
p2.example: It's important to socialise regularly to maintain good mental health.

p2.en: For a particular purpose or in a precise way.
p2.ex1: I specifically asked for a window seat on the flight.
p2.ex2: The rules apply specifically to students in Year 10 and above.
p2.example: The course is designed specifically for advanced learners.

p2.en: Something interests or attracts you.
p2.ex1: Outdoor adventures appeal to him more than indoor activities.
p2.ex2: The design of the new phone appeals to young consumers.
p2.example: The idea of studying abroad really appeals to me.

p2.en: Used to give an example of what you have just said.
p2.ex1: There are many benefits to learning English. For instance, it improves job prospects.
p2.ex2: You can improve your health in simple ways. For instance, drink more water every day.
p2.example: Many cities have reduced pollution. For instance, Oslo banned diesel cars.

p1.en: To help someone do something.
p1.ex1: Volunteers assisted victims of the flood.
p1.ex2: He assisted his colleague with the presentation.
p1.example: She assisted the teacher in setting up the classroom.

p1.en: To think something is true without having proof.
p1.ex1: He assumed she was angry, but she was just tired.
p1.ex2: We assumed the meeting would be cancelled due to rain.
p1.example: Don't assume that everyone thinks the same way as you.

p1.en: To keep things in equal or fair proportions.
p1.ex1: She balanced her studies with part-time work.
p1.ex2: You need to balance your diet with regular exercise.
p1.example: It's hard to balance work and family life.

p1.en: To be dedicated and willing to put in effort for something.
p1.ex1: The team is committed to delivering the project on time.
p1.ex2: He is committed to helping young people in his community.
p1.example: She is committed to improving her English every day.

p1.en: Having a positive or helpful effect.
p1.ex1: Exercise is beneficial for both physical and mental health.
p1.ex2: The new policy proved beneficial for small businesses.
p1.example: Regular reading is beneficial for vocabulary development.

p1.en: A close connection or relationship between people.
p1.ex1: She felt an instant bond with her new classmates.
p1.ex2: The shared experience created a lasting bond among the team.
p1.example: There is a strong bond between twins.

p1.en: Showing kindness and concern for others.
p1.ex1: She is one of the most caring people I have ever met.
p1.ex2: He raised his children in a warm and caring environment.
p1.example: A good nurse should be patient and caring.

p1.en: To be thought of or remembered.
p1.ex1: Several solutions came to mind during the meeting.
p1.ex2: No better word comes to mind to describe the situation.
p1.example: When I think of courage, her name immediately comes to mind.

p1.en: To give or add something that helps achieve a goal.
p1.ex1: She contributed a great deal to the success of the project.
p1.ex2: Volunteers contributed their time and skills to the campaign.
p1.example: Everyone can contribute to making the world a better place.

p1.en: A strong will to achieve something despite difficulties.
p1.ex1: He finished the race through sheer determination.
p1.ex2: Success often comes down to hard work and determination.
p1.example: Her determination helped her become a top student.

p1.en: To be unlike something or someone else.
p1.ex1: Our opinions differ on this subject.
p1.ex2: The two systems differ significantly in how they operate.
p1.example: People differ in the way they deal with stress.

p1.en: The ability to control your behaviour and follow rules.
p1.ex1: The school has strict rules to maintain discipline.
p1.ex2: Learning a musical instrument requires a lot of discipline.
p1.example: Self-discipline is key to achieving long-term goals.

p1.en: To take part in or become involved in an activity.
p1.ex1: He engages in volunteer work every weekend.
p1.ex2: She engaged in a lively debate with her classmates.
p1.example: Students are encouraged to engage in extracurricular activities.

p1.en: A person who is confident and enjoys being around others.
p1.ex1: He is a natural extrovert who loves public speaking.
p1.ex2: Extroverts tend to recharge by spending time with people.
p1.example: As an extrovert, she thrives in social situations.

p1.en: The fact of not achieving what was expected or hoped for.
p1.ex1: The launch of the product was considered a failure.
p1.ex2: Every failure brings you one step closer to success.
p1.example: Don't be afraid of failure — it's how we learn and grow.

p1.en: To do the same job or live in the same way as someone before you.
p1.ex1: He followed in his father's footsteps and joined the family business.
p1.ex2: Many young athletes follow in the footsteps of their heroes.
p1.example: She followed in her mother's footsteps and became a doctor.

p1.en: To make someone do something they don't want to do.
p1.ex1: The storm forced them to cancel the trip.
p1.ex2: He was forced to resign due to the scandal.
p1.example: You shouldn't force children to eat food they dislike.

p1.en: A difference or empty space between two things.
p1.ex1: She noticed a gap in the market for affordable language apps.
p1.ex2: The generation gap can make communication between parents and teens difficult.
p1.example: There is a large gap between the rich and the poor.

p1.en: To feel a connection with or similarity to someone.
p1.ex1: She identified with the struggles of the young entrepreneur.
p1.ex2: He couldn't identify with the values shown in the film.
p1.example: Many readers identify with the main character in the novel.

p1.en: Feeling admiration or respect for something.
p1.ex1: The judges were impressed with the student's project.
p1.ex2: I'm always impressed by how calmly she handles problems.
p1.example: She was very impressed by his knowledge of history.

p1.en: As a response or reward for something.
p1.ex1: He asked for nothing in return for his kindness.
p1.ex2: In return for your hard work, you'll receive a bonus.
p1.example: She helped him with the essay and in return he taught her coding.

p1.en: To form an opinion about someone or something.
p1.ex1: It's hard to judge someone's character in a short time.
p1.ex2: The competition will be judged by a panel of experts.
p1.example: Don't judge people by the way they look.

p1.en: To decide something is true without enough evidence.
p1.ex1: She jumped to conclusions and accused him wrongly.
p1.ex2: It's easy to jump to conclusions when you're stressed.
p1.example: Don't jump to conclusions before you hear both sides of the story.

p1.en: To continue for a period of time.
p1.ex1: How long will the battery last?
p1.ex2: The friendship lasted a lifetime.
p1.example: The lecture lasted for two hours.

p1.en: To cause something to happen as a result.
p1.ex1: His hard work led to a promotion.
p1.ex2: Ignoring small problems can lead to bigger ones later.
p1.example: Lack of sleep can lead to poor concentration.

p1.en: To admire and respect someone.
p1.ex1: She looks up to her mentor for guidance.
p1.ex2: He is the kind of leader others naturally look up to.
p1.example: Children often look up to their parents as role models.

p1.en: Behaving in a sensible, adult way; fully developed.
p1.ex1: A mature approach to conflict is to listen before responding.
p1.ex2: He showed a mature attitude during the difficult situation.
p1.example: She is very mature for her age.

p1.en: Having real importance or a positive purpose.
p1.ex1: He wanted a meaningful conversation, not small talk.
p1.ex2: Building meaningful relationships takes time and effort.
p1.example: Volunteering gave her a more meaningful daily routine.

p1.en: A school for young children before they start primary school.
p1.ex1: The nursery school has a safe outdoor play area.
p1.ex2: Many children develop social skills at nursery school.
p1.example: She started nursery school at the age of three.

p1.en: Strange or unusual.
p1.ex1: He has some odd habits, like talking to his plants.
p1.ex2: She gave me an odd look when I suggested the idea.
p1.example: It seemed odd that the shop was closed on a Monday.

p1.en: Used to say the opposite is true.
p1.ex1: She didn't fail — on the contrary, she scored top marks.
p1.ex2: The plan wasn't a disaster; on the contrary, it was a great success.
p1.example: He wasn't tired; on the contrary, he was full of energy.

p1.en: In a sequence, with each one following the previous.
p1.ex1: Problems seemed to appear one after the other that week.
p1.ex2: She read the books one after the other over the summer.
p1.example: The students gave their presentations one after the other.

p1.en: A person who competes against or disagrees with you.
p1.ex1: His main opponent in the debate made strong arguments.
p1.ex2: A good leader respects their opponents.
p1.example: She shook hands with her opponent after the match.

p1.en: To do better than someone else.
p1.ex1: She outdid herself with the quality of her presentation.
p1.ex2: The new restaurant outdid all the others in the area.
p1.example: He always tries to outdo his classmates in exams.

p1.en: To rest and recover your energy.
p1.ex1: A short holiday helped her recharge completely.
p1.ex2: He went for a walk to recharge during his lunch break.
p1.example: Introverts need time alone to recharge after socialising.

p1.en: Connected to something or someone.
p1.ex1: Is this question related to the topic we studied last week?
p1.ex2: All the problems were related to a single software bug.
p1.example: The two events are closely related to each other.

p1.en: Slow to show emotions or talk to others; quiet.
p1.ex1: She gave a reserved smile and said nothing.
p1.ex2: Reserved people often prefer small groups to large parties.
p1.example: He is quite reserved at first, but very warm once you know him.

p1.en: To treat someone with consideration; a feeling of admiration.
p1.ex1: She earned the respect of all her colleagues.
p1.ex2: Mutual respect is the foundation of any healthy relationship.
p1.example: We should respect people's different opinions.

p1.en: A duty or obligation to do something or care for someone.
p1.ex1: It is your responsibility to submit the work on time.
p1.ex2: She took full responsibility for the mistake.
p1.example: Looking after younger siblings teaches responsibility.

p1.en: A person who others admire and try to copy.
p1.ex1: Her teacher was her biggest role model growing up.
p1.ex2: Parents are often the first role models in a child's life.
p1.example: Athletes can be powerful role models for young people.

p1.en: To arrive or be present somewhere.
p1.ex1: He promised to come but never showed up.
p1.ex2: She showed up late but still gave an excellent speech.
p1.example: Only half the students showed up to the optional lecture.

p1.en: A brother or sister.
p1.ex1: Do you have any siblings?
p1.ex2: Growing up with siblings teaches you how to share.
p1.example: She is very close to her siblings.

p1.en: An amount of something available for use.
p1.ex1: Food supplies were running low after the storm.
p1.ex2: There is a growing supply of online courses available.
p1.example: The school has a limited supply of textbooks this year.

p1.en: An idea or opinion produced by thinking.
p1.ex1: The thought of moving abroad both excited and scared him.
p1.ex2: Give it some thought before making a final decision.
p1.example: She shared her thoughts on the topic in the essay.

p1.en: Used when something unexpected happens.
p1.ex1: To my surprise, the exam was much easier than I expected.
p1.ex2: He turned up to my surprise, as I thought he was abroad.
p1.example: To my surprise, she already knew the answer.

p1.en: To behave towards someone in a particular way.
p1.ex1: She treated all her students with equal respect.
p1.ex2: He felt he was being treated unfairly by his employer.
p1.example: You should treat others the way you wish to be treated.

p1.en: Without any doubt; certainly.
p1.ex1: This is undoubtedly one of the best films of the year.
p1.ex2: The project was undoubtedly a great success.
p1.example: She is undoubtedly the most talented student in the class.

p1.en: Not known or recognised; strange.
p1.ex1: He felt unfamiliar with the new software.
p1.ex2: Some students struggle with unfamiliar vocabulary in exams.
p1.example: The city was unfamiliar to her at first.

p1.en: Not probable or expected.
p1.ex1: She came from an unlikely background to become a scientist.
p1.ex2: An unlikely friendship formed between the two rivals.
p1.example: It's unlikely that the event will be cancelled.

p1.en: Having no restrictions or limits.
p1.ex1: She seemed to have unlimited energy during the project.
p1.ex2: Students have unlimited attempts at the practice quiz.
p1.example: The subscription gives you unlimited access to the platform.

p1.en: Strange and unusual in a way that is hard to explain.
p1.ex1: He has a weird sense of humour, but people love it.
p1.ex2: There was a weird atmosphere in the room that nobody could explain.
p1.example: It felt weird to go back to school after such a long break.

p1.en: Much wiser or more mature than expected for their age.
p1.ex1: His advice was surprisingly good — he's wise beyond his years.
p1.ex2: People often say she's wise beyond her years because of her thoughtful decisions.
p1.example: Even as a child, she was wise beyond her years.

p1.en: Extremely tired or used up.
p1.ex1: He looked worn out after working three shifts in a row.
p1.ex2: The worn-out shoes needed to be replaced.
p1.example: After the long journey, they were completely worn out.

p2.en: A person you know slightly but not closely.
p2.ex1: He has many acquaintances through his work in business.
p2.ex2: We became acquaintances at the conference last year.
p2.example: She is just an acquaintance, not a close friend.

p2.en: Informal word for your best friend.
p2.ex1: He called his bestie to share the exciting news.
p2.ex2: My bestie always knows how to cheer me up.
p2.example: She and her bestie have been inseparable since primary school.

p2.en: Someone you work with.
p2.ex1: He discussed the project with a colleague over lunch.
p2.ex2: My colleagues and I often share ideas after meetings.
p2.example: She gets along very well with all her colleagues.

p2.en: Someone you know, especially useful for professional purposes.
p2.ex1: He reached out to his contacts for help with the project.
p2.ex2: Keep in contact with former classmates — you never know when it helps.
p2.example: She has a wide network of contacts in the industry.

p2.en: A person who works in the same place as you.
p2.ex1: She asked her co-worker for help with the report.
p2.ex2: A good co-worker supports others during busy periods.
p2.example: He gets on well with all his co-workers.

p2.en: The latest time or date by which something must be completed.
p2.ex1: Missing a deadline can have serious consequences.
p2.ex2: The team worked hard to finish before the deadline.
p2.example: She stayed up late to meet the deadline.

p2.en: Having a strong will to do or achieve something.
p2.ex1: He was determined to change his unhealthy habits.
p2.ex2: Despite the difficulties, she remained determined.
p2.example: She was determined to pass the exam no matter what.

p2.en: A person or company that pays others to work for them.
p2.ex1: A good employer values and supports their staff.
p2.ex2: He was praised by his employer for his dedication.
p2.example: Her employer offered flexible working hours.

p2.en: The same in size, amount, or value.
p2.ex1: The pay should be equal for the same work, regardless of gender.
p2.ex2: The teams were equal in skill, making the match exciting.
p2.example: Everyone deserves equal opportunities in education.

p2.en: Able to change or adapt easily to different situations.
p2.ex1: You need to be flexible when plans change unexpectedly.
p2.ex2: A flexible approach to problem-solving is very useful.
p2.example: She appreciates her job because of the flexible schedule.

p2.en: A relative by marriage.
p2.ex1: His mother-in-law visits every Sunday.
p2.ex2: Building a good relationship with in-laws takes time.
p2.example: She gets on very well with her in-laws.

p2.en: Feeling unhappy because someone has something you want.
p2.ex1: She was jealous of her sister's success at first.
p2.ex2: Being jealous of others stops you from appreciating what you have.
p2.example: He felt jealous when his friend got the promotion.

p2.en: To improve or reach a higher level in a skill or situation.
p2.ex1: He is constantly looking for ways to level up his career.
p2.ex2: The new training programme helped employees level up quickly.
p2.example: She decided to level up her English by taking an advanced course.

p2.en: To focus on the positive aspects of a bad situation.
p2.ex1: She always looks on the bright side, which makes her great company.
p2.ex2: Look on the bright side — at least you learned something from the experience.
p2.example: Even when things go wrong, try to look on the bright side.

p2.en: A friend or companion, often used informally.
p2.ex1: She is a good mate — always there when you need her.
p2.ex2: We have been mates since our first day at university.
p2.example: He went to the match with his mates.

p2.en: The mother of your husband or wife.
p2.ex1: His mother-in-law is a very warm and generous person.
p2.ex2: Building a good relationship with your mother-in-law takes patience.
p2.example: She cooks dinner for her mother-in-law every Sunday.

p2.en: Each other; used to show a mutual relationship.
p2.ex1: They respected one another's opinions during the discussion.
p2.ex2: Good friends listen to one another without judgement.
p2.example: The students helped one another prepare for the exam.

p2.en: An informal word for a friend.
p2.ex1: She is a great pal — funny, loyal and supportive.
p2.ex2: We were pals from the moment we met.
p2.example: He spent the weekend with his old pals.

p2.en: A person who is the same age or has the same status as you.
p2.ex1: Peer pressure can influence teenagers' decisions significantly.
p2.ex2: He performed much better than his peers in the science test.
p2.example: She is well respected among her peers.

p2.en: To stop someone from doing something.
p2.ex1: She couldn't prevent her brother from making a big mistake.
p2.ex2: Rules are there to prevent people from acting unsafely.
p2.example: The bad weather prevented us from going on the trip.

p2.en: To depend on someone or something for support.
p2.ex1: The project relies on good teamwork.
p2.ex2: She relies on public transport to get to work every day.
p2.example: You can always rely on a true friend.

p2.en: To think carefully about a factor when making a decision.
p2.ex1: The teacher took the student's personal situation into consideration.
p2.ex2: All options should be taken into consideration before deciding.
p2.example: Please take the deadline into consideration when planning your work.

p2.en: To usually do or be something.
p2.ex1: Introverts tend to prefer smaller social gatherings.
p2.ex2: He tends to overthink things before making a decision.
p2.example: She tends to arrive early for important meetings.

p2.en: Having a very close and strong relationship.
p2.ex1: Our group of friends is very tight.
p2.ex2: She and her cousin are tight — they talk every day.
p2.example: They've been tight since childhood and tell each other everything.

p2.en: To offer to do something without being paid or asked.
p2.ex1: He volunteered to help organise the school event.
p2.ex2: Volunteering is a great way to develop new skills.
p2.example: She volunteers at the local animal shelter every Saturday.

p2.en: Willing to work with others and be helpful.
p2.ex1: The students were cooperative during the group project.
p2.ex2: She was cooperative and always willing to share ideas.
p2.example: A cooperative team member makes everyone's work easier.

p2.en: Showing keen interest or enthusiasm.
p2.ex1: He was eager to impress his new employer.
p2.ex2: The students were eager to start the new project.
p2.example: She was eager to learn as much as possible.

p2.en: Confident, outgoing, and energised by social interaction.
p2.ex1: She is very extroverted and loves meeting new people.
p2.ex2: An extroverted personality is often an advantage in sales roles.
p2.example: Extroverted people tend to enjoy group activities.

p2.en: Shy and preferring to focus on inner thoughts rather than social life.
p2.ex1: Introverted people often need quiet time to recharge.
p2.ex2: Being introverted doesn't mean you can't be confident.
p2.example: He is introverted but very thoughtful and creative.

p2.en: Hopeful and confident about the future.
p2.ex1: Try to stay optimistic — things will improve.
p2.ex2: An optimistic attitude helps you recover from setbacks faster.
p2.example: She remained optimistic even when things went wrong.

p2.en: Expecting bad things to happen.
p2.ex1: Don't be pessimistic — you have prepared well.
p2.ex2: A pessimistic view can hold you back from trying new things.
p2.example: He was pessimistic about his chances of passing the exam.

p2.en: Consistently dependable and trustworthy.
p2.ex1: A reliable friend always keeps their promises.
p2.ex2: Is this source reliable enough to use in the essay?
p2.example: She is one of the most reliable members of the team.

p2.en: Caring only about yourself and not about others.
p2.ex1: A selfish attitude damages teamwork.
p2.ex2: She regretted being selfish and apologised to her friend.
p2.example: It was selfish of him to take the last portion without asking.

p2.en: Refusing to change your opinion or behaviour.
p2.ex1: She was stubborn about her decision to study abroad.
p2.ex2: A stubborn approach can sometimes lead to conflict.
p2.example: He was too stubborn to admit he was wrong.

p2.en: Giving help and encouragement to others.
p2.ex1: A supportive team makes difficult tasks much easier.
p2.ex2: He is always supportive when his friends are going through hard times.
p2.example: Her parents were very supportive of her career choice.

p2.en: Ready or happy to do something.
p2.ex1: Are you willing to take on extra responsibilities?
p2.ex2: He is always willing to help others without being asked.
p2.example: She was willing to stay late to finish the project.

p3.en: Used to emphasise the truth of something, especially when it is surprising.
p3.ex1: She actually finished the marathon despite her injury.
p3.ex2: Actually, I think you might be wrong about that.
p3.example: I thought the film would be boring, but it was actually brilliant.

p3.en: The way you communicate through physical movements and gestures.
p3.ex1: Good speakers use confident body language.
p3.ex2: He crossed his arms, which his body language revealed his discomfort.
p3.example: Her body language showed she was nervous during the interview.

p3.en: To talk and share news with someone you haven't seen in a while.
p3.ex1: I need to catch up on the lessons I missed.
p3.ex2: Let's catch up soon — I have so much to tell you!
p3.example: We met for coffee to catch up after months apart.

p3.en: To communicate with someone by phone, email, or in person.
p3.ex1: She contacted her doctor as soon as she felt unwell.
p3.ex2: He contacted several companies before finding a job.
p3.example: Please contact us if you have any questions.

p3.en: To make someone believe something or agree to do something.
p3.ex1: He couldn't convince the manager to change the deadline.
p3.ex2: The evidence convinced the jury of his innocence.
p3.example: She convinced her parents to let her study abroad.

p3.en: In a way that produces the desired result.
p3.ex1: The new system works more effectively than the old one.
p3.ex2: You need to manage your time effectively to meet the deadline.
p3.example: She communicates effectively in both English and Uzbek.

p3.en: The look on someone's face that shows how they feel.
p3.ex1: A genuine smile involves the whole face, not just the lips.
p3.ex2: He tried to hide his emotions, but his facial expression gave him away.
p3.example: Her facial expression made it clear she was disappointed.

p3.en: To give someone information they have missed.
p3.ex1: She filled her colleague in on the latest developments.
p3.ex2: He asked his friend to fill him in after missing the lecture.
p3.example: Can you fill me in on what happened at the meeting?

p3.en: A method or way of sharing information with others.
p3.ex1: Writing letters is a more personal form of communication.
p3.ex2: Gesture is an important non-verbal form of communication.
p3.example: Social media has become a major form of communication.

p3.en: A movement of your body to express or emphasise something.
p3.ex1: He made a gesture to signal that everything was fine.
p3.ex2: Different cultures interpret the same gesture in different ways.
p3.example: A thumbs up is a common gesture for approval.

p3.en: To have a friendly relationship with someone.
p3.ex1: Do you get along with your neighbours?
p3.ex2: They didn't get along at first, but grew to be great friends.
p3.example: She gets along with everyone at work.

p3.en: To contact someone or obtain something.
p3.ex1: Can you get hold of the report before the meeting?
p3.ex2: It's hard to get hold of tickets for the concert.
p3.example: I tried to get hold of her all morning but she didn't answer.

p3.en: To have a short, often serious, conversation with someone.
p3.ex1: Could I have a word with you in private?
p3.ex2: She had a word with her manager about the workload.
p3.example: The teacher asked to have a word with him after class.

p3.en: Meeting or doing something physically rather than remotely.
p3.ex1: She applied for the job in person rather than online.
p3.ex2: Meeting in person helps build stronger relationships.
p3.example: It's much better to discuss this in person.

p3.en: Away from others; not in public.
p3.ex1: Let's discuss this in private so others don't hear.
p3.ex2: He preferred to deal with sensitive matters in private.
p3.example: She asked to speak with the manager in private.

p3.en: Communication or direct involvement with others.
p3.ex1: The app encourages interaction between students.
p3.ex2: Positive interaction with customers is essential in retail.
p3.example: Regular interaction with native speakers improves fluency.

p3.en: To stop someone from speaking or doing something.
p3.ex1: He interrupted the meeting with an urgent announcement.
p3.ex2: Please don't interrupt — let me finish my point.
p3.example: It is rude to interrupt someone while they are speaking.

p3.en: The quality of being friendly, generous, and considerate.
p3.ex1: She showed great kindness to the new student.
p3.ex2: Kindness costs nothing but means everything.
p3.example: A small act of kindness can make a big difference.

p3.en: To no longer have contact with someone.
p3.ex1: I lost touch with many school friends over the years.
p3.ex2: It's easy to lose touch when everyone gets busy.
p3.example: They lost touch after moving to different cities.

p3.en: Being faithful and committed to someone or something.
p3.ex1: She showed great loyalty to her team during the crisis.
p3.ex2: Customer loyalty is built through trust and quality service.
p3.example: Loyalty is one of the most important qualities in a friendship.

p3.en: To keep something in good condition or continue something.
p3.ex1: She works hard to maintain a healthy lifestyle.
p3.ex2: The company maintains high standards in all its products.
p3.example: It takes effort to maintain a long-distance friendship.

p3.en: A method used to communicate or convey information.
p3.ex1: Social media is a powerful means of communication today.
p3.ex2: Face-to-face conversation is still the most effective means of communication.
p3.example: Email is a widely used means of communication in business.

p3.en: Worth remembering because it is special or unusual.
p3.ex1: She gave a memorable performance that the audience loved.
p3.ex2: That holiday was one of the most memorable of my life.
p3.example: The graduation ceremony was a truly memorable event.

p3.en: A failure to understand something correctly.
p3.ex1: A misunderstanding in communication can cause serious problems.
p3.ex2: They cleared up the misunderstanding quickly and moved on.
p3.example: The argument was the result of a simple misunderstanding.

p3.en: A child with no brothers or sisters.
p3.ex1: Being an only child taught him to be independent.
p3.ex2: Some only children find it hard to share at first.
p3.example: As an only child, she was very close to her parents.

p3.en: The qualities and traits that make someone who they are.
p3.ex1: He has a strong character and never gives up.
p3.ex2: Personality and character develop through experiences.
p3.example: Her cheerful personality makes her easy to be around.

p3.en: A particular quality or feature of someone's personality.
p3.ex1: Patience is a trait that many great teachers share.
p3.ex2: Her most noticeable trait is her incredible determination.
p3.example: Honesty is one of his most admirable traits.

p3.en: A feature or characteristic, especially a good one.
p3.ex1: She has many qualities that make her an excellent teacher.
p3.ex2: Reliability is a quality that employers look for in candidates.
p3.example: Leadership is a quality valued in many jobs.

p3.en: To contact or communicate with someone.
p3.ex1: She tried to reach her friend but got no answer.
p3.ex2: The best way to reach customers is through social media.
p3.example: You can reach me by email at any time.

p3.en: To call someone again after they have called you.
p3.ex1: She asked him to ring her back when he was free.
p3.ex2: He forgot to ring back and apologised the next day.
p3.example: I'm busy right now — I'll ring you back in an hour.

p3.en: To represent or mean something.
p3.ex1: What does this symbol stand for?
p3.ex2: The flag stands for the values of the country.
p3.example: 'UN' stands for United Nations.

p3.en: To stop listening or paying attention; to turn something off.
p3.ex1: He switched off his phone during the lecture.
p3.ex2: You need to switch off and relax over the weekend.
p3.example: She finds it hard to switch off from work in the evenings.

p3.en: Having the usual qualities expected of something or someone.
p3.ex1: A typical school day starts at eight o'clock.
p3.ex2: This is a typical example of miscommunication.
p3.example: It's typical of him to arrive late.

p3.en: Showing sympathy and awareness of others' feelings.
p3.ex1: He appreciated having such an understanding partner.
p3.ex2: An understanding approach helps resolve conflicts peacefully.
p3.example: Her teacher was very understanding when she explained the situation.

p3.en: To give the latest information; or the information itself.
p3.ex1: The app needs a software update to run properly.
p3.ex2: She sent a quick update to let everyone know the news.
p3.example: Please update me on any changes to the plan.

p3.en: Used to partially agree with a point.
p3.ex1: I agree to a certain extent — social media can be useful, but also harmful.
p3.ex2: She said she agreed to a certain extent but had some reservations.
p3.word: I agree to a certain extent.
p3.example: I agree to a certain extent, but I think there are other factors too.

p3.en: Used to say you partially agree, but not completely.
p3.ex1: He agreed up to a point but felt the policy went too far.
p3.ex2: I agree up to a point — exercise helps, but diet matters more.
p3.word: I agree up to a point.
p3.example: I agree up to a point, but the situation is more complex than that.

p3.en: Used to introduce a personal opinion.
p3.ex1: To my mind, students learn best when they feel safe.
p3.ex2: To my mind, the solution is simpler than people think.
p3.example: To my mind, communication is the key to a successful relationship.

p3.en: Used to clarify or explain what you are trying to say.
p3.ex1: I wasn't criticising you. What I mean is, we could do it differently.
p3.ex2: What I mean is that everyone deserves a second chance.
p3.example: What I mean is, we should think carefully before deciding.

p4.en: A variety of different things.
p4.ex1: She has a range of skills that make her very employable.
p4.ex2: The museum has a range of exhibitions for all ages.
p4.example: The school offers a range of after-school activities.

p4.en: Something bought at a lower price than usual.
p4.ex1: This coat was a real bargain — half the original price.
p4.ex2: Shoppers look for bargains during the sales period.
p4.example: She found a great bargain at the market.

p4.en: An agreement or arrangement, often involving money.
p4.ex1: The company signed a new deal with a major supplier.
p4.ex2: That's a great deal — you should take it!
p4.example: They made a deal to share the cost of the trip.

p4.en: A public display of art, objects, or information.
p4.ex1: The science museum is hosting an interactive exhibition.
p4.ex2: The photography exhibition attracted thousands of visitors.
p4.example: She visited an exhibition of modern art at the gallery.

p4.en: To have a very enjoyable time.
p4.ex1: She had a blast on her trip to Istanbul.
p4.ex2: The kids had a blast at the theme park.
p4.example: We had a blast at the end-of-year school party.

p4.en: Involving communication between people or between people and technology.
p4.ex1: She prefers interactive apps to traditional textbooks.
p4.ex2: The museum's interactive displays made learning fun.
p4.example: The interactive lesson kept students engaged throughout.

p4.en: To disappoint someone by failing to do what was expected.
p4.ex1: He let her down by forgetting their important meeting.
p4.ex2: She promised not to let him down again.
p4.example: Don't let your team down — do your part properly.

p4.en: Extremely impressive or surprising.
p4.ex1: The special effects in the film were mind-blowing.
p4.ex2: Learning how the brain works is truly mind-blowing.
p4.example: The view from the top of the mountain was mind-blowing.

p4.en: A formal or polite asking for something.
p4.ex1: The manager received many requests for flexible hours.
p4.ex2: Your request has been received and will be reviewed shortly.
p4.example: She made a request for extra time during the exam.

p4.en: A slow, relaxed walk.
p4.ex1: A morning stroll helps clear your mind.
p4.ex2: She took a stroll through the park to enjoy the sunshine.
p4.example: They went for a stroll along the river after dinner.

p4.en: Used to introduce a new topic or change the subject.
p4.ex1: As for the cost, we can discuss that later.
p4.ex2: As for me, I prefer to work in the mornings.
p4.example: As for the homework, it's due next Monday.

p4.en: Used to say you want to join or take part in something.
p4.ex1: If you're organising a study group, count me in!
p4.ex2: She heard about the volunteering event and said, 'Count me in!'
p4.example: A trip to the seaside? Count me in!

p1.ru: как гром среди ясного неба, неожиданно
p1.en: Happening suddenly and without any warning.
p1.ex1: He called me out of the blue after years of silence.
p1.ex2: The news came completely out of the blue and shocked everyone.
p1.example: Out of the blue, she received a job offer from abroad.

p2.en: To heat a liquid until it reaches 100°C and starts to bubble.
p2.ex1: She boiled the pasta for ten minutes.
p2.ex2: Make sure the water is boiling before you add the vegetables.
p2.example: Boil the kettle before making tea.

p2.en: A dark mark on your skin caused by an injury.
p2.ex1: She put ice on the bruise to reduce the swelling.
p2.ex2: The bruise faded after a few days.
p2.example: He had a large bruise on his arm after the fall.

p2.en: A hard covering placed around a broken bone to protect it while it heals.
p2.ex1: Everyone at school signed his cast when he broke his arm.
p2.ex2: The doctor put a cast on her wrist after the injury.
p2.example: She had a cast on her leg for six weeks.

p2.en: Having a pattern of squares, like a chessboard.
p2.ex1: She bought a checked skirt at the market.
p2.ex2: A checked pattern is very popular in autumn fashion.
p2.example: He wore a checked shirt to the casual meeting.

p2.en: The joint in the middle of your arm where it bends.
p2.ex1: He banged his elbow on the doorframe.
p2.ex2: The sleeve was torn at the elbow.
p2.example: She rested her elbow on the table while reading.

p2.en: Used to say something is different from what usually happens.
p2.ex1: She ordered soup instead of salad for a change.
p2.ex2: For a change, he decided to cook dinner himself.
p2.example: Let's walk to school today for a change.

p2.en: A slight wound where skin has been scraped off.
p2.ex1: He cleaned the graze with antiseptic before bandaging it.
p2.ex2: It was just a graze — nothing serious.
p2.example: She had a graze on her knee after falling off her bike.

p2.en: A place where roads or railway lines meet.
p2.ex1: There was an accident at the main junction this morning.
p2.ex2: The new shopping centre is near the motorway junction.
p2.example: Turn left at the junction and continue straight ahead.

p2.en: A container used for boiling water, usually electric.
p2.ex1: The kettle boiled and clicked off automatically.
p2.ex2: Always fill the kettle with fresh water before using it.
p2.example: She switched the kettle on to make tea.

p2.en: Describing clothing with sleeves that reach the wrists.
p2.ex1: He chose a long-sleeved shirt for the formal event.
p2.ex2: Long-sleeved clothes offer better sun protection.
p2.example: She wore a long-sleeved top because it was cold.

p2.en: A repeated design on fabric or a surface.
p2.ex1: She prefers plain clothes to ones with a loud pattern.
p2.ex2: The pattern on the wallpaper matched the curtains.
p2.example: The dress had a floral pattern on a white background.

p2.en: To put something carefully in a particular position.
p2.ex1: He placed the books neatly on the shelf.
p2.ex2: Place the cast iron pan over medium heat.
p2.example: She placed the kettle on the counter.

p2.en: Simple in appearance, without pattern or decoration.
p2.ex1: He prefers plain food without too many spices.
p2.ex2: A plain background makes the text easier to read.
p2.example: She wore a plain white shirt to the interview.

p2.en: To connect an electrical device to a power supply.
p2.ex1: He plugged his phone in to charge it overnight.
p2.ex2: She plugged in the kettle and waited for it to boil.
p2.example: Don't forget to plug the toaster in before using it.

p2.en: To appear suddenly or unexpectedly.
p2.ex1: New coffee shops keep popping up all over the city.
p2.ex2: He popped up at the party when no one expected him.
p2.example: A notification popped up on her screen.

p2.en: A circular road junction where traffic goes around a central island.
p2.ex1: There is a large roundabout at the entrance to the town.
p2.ex2: She got confused at the roundabout and took the wrong exit.
p2.example: Take the second exit at the roundabout.

p2.en: Describing clothing with sleeves that end above the elbow.
p2.ex1: She packed a few short-sleeved tops for the holiday.
p2.ex2: A short-sleeved dress is perfect for warm weather.
p2.example: He wore a short-sleeved shirt in the summer heat.

p2.en: A basin with a tap, used for washing hands or dishes.
p2.ex1: Don't leave dirty dishes in the sink.
p2.ex2: He fixed the leaking tap over the bathroom sink.
p2.example: She washed the vegetables in the kitchen sink.

p2.en: Small in degree; not serious or significant.
p2.ex1: She felt a slight pain in her wrist after typing all day.
p2.ex2: He made a slight mistake in the calculation.
p2.example: There was a slight delay on the train this morning.

p2.en: To move or travel very fast, often too fast.
p2.ex1: He was caught speeding on the motorway.
p2.ex2: An ambulance sped past the roundabout with its siren on.
p2.example: The car was speeding when it went through the junction.

p2.en: To extend over a wide area, or to apply something thinly over a surface.
p2.ex1: The news spread quickly through the school.
p2.ex2: He spread the map out on the table to find the junction.
p2.example: She spread butter on the toast.

p2.en: Having a pattern of parallel lines of different colours.
p2.ex1: He bought a striped tie for the office.
p2.ex2: A striped pattern is a classic wardrobe choice.
p2.example: She wore a striped blue and white top.

p2.en: Larger than normal due to injury or illness.
p2.ex1: He had a swollen lip after the accident.
p2.ex2: The doctor said the swollen joint needed rest and ice.
p2.example: Her ankle was swollen after she twisted it.

p2.en: Fitting very closely to the body; not loose.
p2.ex1: She found a tight cast around her wrist quite uncomfortable.
p2.ex2: He wore a tight shirt that showed off his athletic build.
p2.example: The jeans were too tight to be comfortable.

p2.en: A kitchen appliance used to toast bread.
p2.ex1: The toaster stopped working after a power cut.
p2.ex2: He dropped his toast trying to get it out of the toaster.
p2.example: She plugged in the toaster and made breakfast.

p2.en: A tool or implement used for cooking or eating.
p2.ex1: A spatula is a very useful cooking utensil.
p2.ex2: Keep utensils clean and dry after each use.
p2.example: She bought new kitchen utensils for the new flat.

p2.en: The joint connecting the hand to the arm.
p2.ex1: He sprained his wrist during football practice.
p2.ex2: The doctor put a cast on her wrist after the X-ray.
p2.example: She wore a watch on her left wrist.

p2.en: A fastener with two rows of teeth that lock together, used on clothing or bags.
p2.ex1: He struggled to zip up his bag because it was too full.
p2.ex2: Make sure the zip is fully closed before going out in the rain.
p2.example: The zip on her jacket was broken.

p2.en: Used to express surprise or disbelief at something.
p2.ex1: Are you kidding me? That film was terrible!
p2.ex2: He said he won the prize — I said, 'Are you kidding?'
p2.example: Are you kidding? She finished the marathon in under three hours!

p2.en: Used to ask if someone is joking or teasing you.
p2.ex1: She told me she got the job — I asked if she was pulling my leg.
p2.ex2: He said the class was cancelled. Are you pulling my leg?
p2.example: Are you pulling my leg? There's no way that actually happened!

p2.ru: быть на ногах, стоять/работать весь день
p2.en: To be standing or working for a long period without rest.
p2.ex1: After a twelve-hour shift, he was glad to finally sit down — he'd been on his feet all day.
p2.ex2: She's been on her feet since six in the morning.
p2.example: Nurses are on their feet for most of the working day.

p2.en: Used to say you have no idea about something.
p2.ex1: How does she manage to do it all? Beats me!
p2.ex2: I don't know why the toaster stopped working. Beats me!
p2.example: Why did he leave so early? Beats me!

p2.en: Used to strongly agree with what someone has just said.
p2.ex1: 'The exam was really hard.' 'You can say that again!'
p2.ex2: She said the traffic was awful, and he replied, 'You can say that again!'
p2.example: 'This weather is terrible.' 'You can say that again!'

p2.ru: Живёшь и учишься. Век живи — век учись.
p2.en: Said when you discover something surprising you did not know before.
p2.ex1: She burned the toast by accident. You live and learn.
p2.ex2: He found out the shortcut after driving the long way for years — you live and learn.
p2.example: I had no idea the roundabout had five exits. You live and learn!

p3.en: Something you have done successfully, especially through hard work.
p3.ex1: He listed his achievements on his CV.
p3.ex2: Building a business from scratch is a remarkable achievement.
p3.example: Passing the B2 exam was her greatest achievement of the year.

p3.en: A sudden feeling of excitement and energy caused by danger or thrill.
p3.ex1: She got an adrenaline rush before going on stage.
p3.ex2: He loves extreme sports because of the adrenaline rush they give.
p3.example: Skydiving gives you an incredible adrenaline rush.

p3.en: The mood or feeling of a place or situation.
p3.ex1: The atmosphere at the concert was electric.
p3.ex2: A peaceful atmosphere helps students focus during exams.
p3.example: The old city had a magical atmosphere at night.

p3.en: To show or describe something in a picture, book, or film.
p3.ex1: The film depicts the hustle and bustle of city life.
p3.ex2: She depicted her feelings through abstract art.
p3.example: The painting depicts a busy market in the old city.

p3.en: Not interesting or exciting; boring.
p3.ex1: He found the monotonous routine extremely dull.
p3.ex2: Without friends, city life can feel surprisingly dull.
p3.example: The lecture was so dull that several students fell asleep.

p3.en: A feeling of happiness and satisfaction from achieving something meaningful.
p3.ex1: Helping others can bring a deep sense of fulfilment.
p3.ex2: He changed careers in search of greater personal fulfilment.
p3.example: She found great fulfilment in working with young children.

p3.en: To recover from something unpleasant, such as an illness or disappointment.
p3.ex1: He couldn't get over how thrilling the experience was.
p3.ex2: She got over her fear of heights by going climbing.
p3.example: It took her a while to get over the shock of the accident.

p3.en: The busy, noisy activity of a place full of people.
p3.ex1: After years in the countryside, he found the hustle and bustle exhausting.
p3.ex2: The hustle and bustle of the train station made it hard to think.
p3.example: She loved the hustle and bustle of the city market.

p3.en: Dull and repetitive, without any variety or change.
p3.ex1: She found the monotonous routine of office life unfulfilling.
p3.ex2: His monotonous voice made the presentation hard to sit through.
p3.example: Working on a factory line can be very monotonous.

p3.en: Calm, quiet, and free from disturbance.
p3.ex1: She took a peaceful stroll along the river at sunrise.
p3.ex2: He found the quiet library a peaceful place to study.
p3.example: The countryside was peaceful compared to the city.

p3.en: To make pain, stress, or a problem less severe.
p3.ex1: The medication helped relieve her back pain.
p3.ex2: Talking to a friend can relieve feelings of loneliness.
p3.example: Exercise can relieve stress after a long day.

p3.en: Involving the possibility of something going wrong or causing harm.
p3.ex1: It's risky to speed on a wet road.
p3.ex2: She knew it was risky, but she took the chance anyway.
p3.example: Investing all your money in one place is risky.

p3.en: The quality of being alike or resembling something else.
p3.ex1: She noticed many similarities between city and rural life.
p3.ex2: Despite their differences, there is a strong similarity in their values.
p3.example: There is a striking similarity between the two paintings.

p3.en: Causing great excitement and pleasure.
p3.ex1: She found skydiving a thrilling experience.
p3.ex2: It was thrilling to watch the team score in the final minute.
p3.example: The roller coaster was absolutely thrilling.

p3.ru: тогда как, в то время как
p3.en: Used to contrast two different facts or situations.
p3.ex1: City life is fast-paced, whereas rural life tends to be more relaxed.
p3.ex2: He finds extreme sports thrilling, whereas she finds them too risky.
p3.example: She loves the hustle of the city, whereas her sister prefers the countryside.

p1.en: To come near or nearer to someone or something.
p1.ex1: He approached the shore slowly, not wanting to make a sound.
p1.ex2: A strange shadow approached them from the darkness.
p1.example: She approached the cottage carefully in the moonlight.

p1.en: Completely calm and relaxed, even in a stressful situation.
p1.ex1: He gave his speech as cool as a cucumber, without any nerves.
p1.ex2: While everyone panicked, she stood there as cool as a cucumber.
p1.example: Despite the emergency, she remained as cool as a cucumber.

p1.en: Knowing that something exists or is happening.
p1.ex1: Are you aware of the emergency services number?
p1.ex2: He became aware of someone watching him in silence.
p1.example: She was aware of the strange shadow drifting near the shore.

p1.en: Completely confused and unable to understand something.
p1.ex1: The police were baffled by the lack of evidence.
p1.ex2: He looked baffled when she pointed to the rope near the oar.
p1.example: She was baffled by the peculiar noise coming from the cottage.

p1.en: To feel relieved after a stressful or worrying situation ends.
p1.ex1: He breathed a sigh of relief after confirming everyone was safe.
p1.ex2: They breathed a sigh of relief when the emergency services arrived.
p1.example: She breathed a sigh of relief when she finally reached the shore.

p1.en: To find or meet something or someone by chance.
p1.ex1: She came across a peculiar seal near the rocks.
p1.ex2: They came across a remote village while drifting along the coast.
p1.example: He came across an old rope and lifebelt near the cottage.

p1.en: To make sure that something is definitely true or correct.
p1.ex1: He confirmed the identity of the person by the moonlight.
p1.ex2: Can you confirm what you saw near the shore?
p1.example: She called to confirm that the emergency services were on their way.

p1.en: Unable to understand something clearly.
p1.ex1: She felt confused when she saw the rope untied.
p1.ex2: The baffled and confused crew muttered to each other in silence.
p1.example: He was confused by the shadow drifting silently past the oar.

p1.en: A small, simple house, usually in the countryside.
p1.ex1: She gazed at the moonlit cottage from the water.
p1.ex2: The pale light coming from the cottage guided them to safety.
p1.example: They found shelter in a remote cottage near the shore.

p1.en: The ability to do something difficult or dangerous without fear.
p1.ex1: She showed great courage by diving into the cold water.
p1.ex2: He summoned all his courage before approaching the shadow.
p1.example: It took a lot of courage to drift alone in the dark.

p1.en: To shout or call out loudly.
p1.ex1: He cried for help, but nobody heard him in the silence.
p1.ex2: They cried out when they saw the lifebelt floating near the shore.
p1.example: She cried out as the boat began to slide toward the rocks.

p1.en: The time of day when light first appears in the sky.
p1.ex1: They waited in silence until dawn before making a move.
p1.ex2: The pale light of dawn revealed the remote cottage on the hill.
p1.example: By dawn, the boat had drifted far from the shore.

p1.en: To be carried slowly by water or wind.
p1.ex1: He watched the oar drift silently away in the moonlight.
p1.ex2: They drifted out without realising how far they had gone.
p1.example: The boat began to drift out toward the open sea.

p1.en: Police, fire brigade, and ambulance services that respond to crises.
p1.ex1: The emergency services arrived within minutes of the call.
p1.ex2: He confirmed that the emergency services had been contacted.
p1.example: She called the emergency services as soon as she saw the danger.

p1.en: To rest or move on the surface of water without sinking.
p1.ex1: She watched the rope float away as the boat drifted out.
p1.ex2: A pale shadow floated silently across the surface of the water.
p1.example: The lifebelt floated near the shore in the moonlight.

p1.en: To look steadily at something for a long time.
p1.ex1: He stood on the shore, gazing at the distant cottage.
p1.ex2: They gazed in silence as the seal disappeared into the water.
p1.example: She gazed at the moonlight reflecting on the water.

p1.en: To recognise and name someone or something.
p1.ex1: He identified the rope as the one they had untied earlier.
p1.ex2: The emergency services were able to identify the drifting boat.
p1.example: She struggled to identify the shadow in the pale moonlight.

p1.en: Without making any sound; quietly.
p1.ex1: She sat in silence, gazing at the moonlit shore.
p1.ex2: He approached the cottage in silence so as not to be heard.
p1.example: They rowed in silence, listening for any strange sound.

p1.en: A curved piece of glass used in cameras or glasses to focus light.
p1.ex1: He looked through the lens to identify the shape on the shore.
p1.ex2: The camera lens captured the moonlight reflecting on the water.
p1.example: She pressed the lens of her camera against the window.

p1.en: A ring-shaped device thrown to someone in water to help them float.
p1.ex1: A lifebelt was tied to the rope near the shore.
p1.ex2: She was relieved to see the lifebelt floating close by.
p1.example: He grabbed the lifebelt and threw it toward the drifting boat.

p1.en: The light from the moon at night.
p1.ex1: She could just make out the oar in the moonlight.
p1.ex2: By moonlight, they could see a shadow drifting near the shore.
p1.example: The cottage looked eerie in the pale moonlight.

p1.en: To speak quietly and unclearly, often when annoyed or thinking.
p1.ex1: She muttered to herself as she untied the rope in the dark.
p1.ex2: They muttered to each other in silence, unsure what to do.
p1.example: He muttered something confused under his breath.

p1.en: A long pole with a flat blade used to row a boat.
p1.ex1: She gripped the oar tightly as the boat drifted out.
p1.ex2: He used the oar to push away from the shore.
p1.example: One of the oars had slipped into the water during the night.

p1.en: Light in colour; or looking white due to illness or shock.
p1.ex1: The pale moonlight made the shore look ghostly.
p1.ex2: He looked pale and tense as the boat drifted further out.
p1.example: Her face went pale when she saw the shadow near the cottage.

p1.en: Strange or unusual in a way that is hard to explain.
p1.ex1: She noticed a peculiar shape floating near the lifebelt.
p1.ex2: He had a peculiar feeling that someone was watching them.
p1.example: There was a peculiar silence over the water at dawn.

p1.en: To look carefully at something, especially when it is hard to see.
p1.ex1: He peered into the darkness, trying to identify the shape.
p1.ex2: They peered through the fog, searching for the cottage.
p1.example: She peered through the lens at the shadow on the shore.

p1.en: To convince someone to do something through reasoning or argument.
p1.ex1: He persuaded the others not to drift any further out.
p1.ex2: It took courage to persuade the group to call the emergency services.
p1.example: She persuaded him to stay close to the shore.

p1.en: To show that something is definitely true.
p1.ex1: He proved that the rope had been deliberately untied.
p1.ex2: It was hard to prove what had happened in the darkness.
p1.example: She had to prove that the shadow near the shore was real.

p1.en: Far away from towns and other people; isolated.
p1.ex1: They found themselves on a remote part of the shore.
p1.ex2: Help was hard to reach in such a remote place.
p1.example: The cottage was in a remote location, far from any road.

p1.en: A thick, strong cord made of twisted fibres.
p1.ex1: She used the rope to pull the lifebelt toward the shore.
p1.ex2: He held the rope tightly as the boat began to drift out.
p1.example: The rope that had tied the boat had been untied.

p1.en: To move or act very quickly.
p1.ex1: He rushed to call the emergency services.
p1.ex2: They rushed out of the cottage when they heard the cry.
p1.example: She rushed to the shore as soon as she saw the boat drifting.

p1.en: A large sea animal with flippers that lives near coasts.
p1.ex1: She peered through the lens and saw a seal floating nearby.
p1.ex2: The pale shape turned out to be a seal, not a shadow.
p1.example: A seal was resting silently on the rocks near the shore.

p1.en: A dark shape made when something blocks light.
p1.ex1: She peered at the shadow near the cottage but couldn't identify it.
p1.ex2: The shadow gave her a tense, uneasy feeling.
p1.example: A large shadow drifted across the moonlit water.

p1.en: To shake slightly because of cold or fear.
p1.ex1: He shivered as the cold air drifted in from the shore.
p1.ex2: They shivered in silence, listening for any strange sound.
p1.example: She shivered in the pale moonlight, gripping the oar.

p1.en: The land along the edge of a sea, lake, or river.
p1.ex1: She could see the pale outline of the cottage from the shore.
p1.ex2: The lifebelt washed up on the shore at dawn.
p1.example: They rowed toward the shore as quickly as they could.

p1.en: To move smoothly along a surface.
p1.ex1: She slid the rope carefully under the lifebelt.
p1.ex2: The boat began to slide toward the rocks in the darkness.
p1.example: The oar slid off the side of the boat into the water.

p1.en: To lose balance and slide accidentally.
p1.ex1: The rope slipped out of his hands as the boat drifted out.
p1.ex2: He slipped trying to tiptoe away from the cottage.
p1.example: She slipped on the wet rocks near the shore.

p1.en: To look at something for a long time without moving your eyes.
p1.ex1: He stared in silence at the moonlight on the water.
p1.ex2: They stared at the drifting boat, baffled by what was happening.
p1.example: She stared at the shadow near the shore, unable to identify it.

p1.en: Feeling nervous or unable to relax because of worry.
p1.ex1: She felt tense as the shadow drifted closer.
p1.ex2: He looked pale and tense, clutching the rope tightly.
p1.example: The atmosphere in the cottage was tense and silent.

p1.en: To walk quietly on the tips of your toes to avoid making noise.
p1.ex1: He tiptoed to the shore, trying not to slip on the wet rocks.
p1.ex2: They tiptoed in silence, unsure what lay ahead.
p1.example: She tiptoed past the cottage to avoid waking anyone.

p1.en: To catch your foot on something and nearly fall.
p1.ex1: She tripped trying to rush toward the shore.
p1.ex2: Be careful not to trip on the oar lying on the deck.
p1.example: He tripped over the rope in the dark and nearly fell.

p1.en: To undo a knot or release something that was tied.
p1.ex1: She untied the lifebelt from the side of the boat.
p1.ex2: He untied the rope and let the boat drift out slowly.
p1.example: Someone had untied the rope during the night.

p1.en: Able to be seen.
p1.ex1: The shadow was barely visible in the moonlight.
p1.ex2: By dawn, the shore was clearly visible from the boat.
p1.example: The pale cottage was just visible through the fog.

p1.en: To speak very quietly so only the person next to you can hear.
p1.ex1: He whispered to confirm that the rope had been untied.
p1.ex2: They whispered to each other as they tiptoed past the cottage.
p1.example: She whispered his name so as not to disturb the silence.

p1.en: To shout very loudly.
p1.ex1: She yelled at him to grab the lifebelt.
p1.ex2: They yelled into the darkness but heard no reply.
p1.example: He yelled for help when the boat began to drift out.

p2.en: To have difficulty breathing after physical effort.
p2.ex1: He was out of breath after rushing to call the emergency services.
p2.ex2: They were out of breath by the time they reached the cottage.
p2.example: She arrived at the shore out of breath after running.

p2.en: Awake and aware of your surroundings; not unconscious.
p2.ex1: She remained conscious throughout, despite the shock.
p2.ex2: The researcher confirmed the patient was fully conscious.
p2.example: He was conscious but pale after the accident on the shore.

p2.en: To look at something carefully or check it thoroughly.
p2.ex1: She examined the rope carefully to see if it had been cut.
p2.ex2: He examined the scene in silence before speaking.
p2.example: The doctor examined his injured leg after the fall.

p2.en: To suddenly lose consciousness for a short time.
p2.ex1: He nearly fainted from exhaustion after the long swim.
p2.ex2: The tense atmosphere made her feel like she might faint.
p2.example: She fainted when she saw the blood on the shore.

p2.en: To look quickly at something.
p2.ex1: He glanced at the shore and then back at the drifting boat.
p2.ex2: She glanced at him and raised her eyebrows in surprise.
p2.example: She glanced at the rope and immediately knew something was wrong.

p2.en: To move your head up and down to show agreement or acknowledgement.
p2.ex1: She nodded slowly, confirming she understood.
p2.ex2: The researcher nodded and made a note in his book.
p2.example: He nodded when she asked if he had seen the shadow.

p2.en: To watch something carefully or notice it.
p2.ex1: He observed that the rope had been untied from the boat.
p2.ex2: The researcher spent hours observing behaviour near the shore.
p2.example: She observed the seal from a distance through the lens.

p2.en: To happen, especially unexpectedly.
p2.ex1: It never occurred to her that someone had untied the rope.
p2.ex2: Strange events had been occurring near the remote cottage.
p2.example: The accident occurred just as dawn was breaking.

p2.en: A liquid fuel used in cars and other vehicles.
p2.ex1: She could smell petrol near the overturned vehicle.
p2.ex2: He shrugged his shoulders when asked why they had no petrol.
p2.example: They ran out of petrol far from the nearest town.

p2.en: To move your eyebrows upward to show surprise or disbelief.
p2.ex1: He raised his eyebrows at the mention of the remote cottage.
p2.ex2: The researcher raised his eyebrows at the unexpected results.
p2.example: She raised her eyebrows when he described the peculiar shadow.

p2.en: A person who studies something in detail to find out new information.
p2.ex1: The researcher examined the evidence carefully.
p2.ex2: She had worked as a researcher for many years before the expedition.
p2.example: A researcher was observing wildlife near the shore.

p2.en: The natural features of a landscape, especially when beautiful.
p2.ex1: She paused to take in the dramatic scenery at dawn.
p2.ex2: The remote cottage was surrounded by stunning mountain scenery.
p2.example: The scenery along the coast was absolutely breathtaking.

p2.en: To move your head from side to side to show disagreement or disbelief.
p2.ex1: She shook her head and muttered something under her breath.
p2.ex2: The researcher shook his head at the confusing data.
p2.example: He shook his head when asked if he had heard the yell.

p2.en: To raise and then lower your shoulders to show you don't know or don't care.
p2.ex1: She shrugged her shoulders and glanced at the shore.
p2.ex2: The baffled researcher shrugged his shoulders at the peculiar result.
p2.example: He shrugged his shoulders when asked about the untied rope.

p2.en: To breathe out slowly and audibly, showing tiredness, relief, or sadness.
p2.ex1: He sighed and shook his head at the confusing scene.
p2.ex2: They both sighed when they finally saw the shore in the distance.
p2.example: She sighed with relief when the emergency services arrived.

p2.en: To walk in a slow and relaxed way.
p2.ex1: She strolled past the cottage without stopping.
p2.ex2: He strolled toward the trail, observing the landscape.
p2.example: They strolled along the shore at dawn, taking in the scenery.

p2.en: A path through countryside or a series of marks left by someone.
p2.ex1: A researcher was following the trail left by the animal.
p2.ex2: The trail led down to the shore where the lifebelt had been found.
p2.example: They followed the trail through the forest toward the remote cottage.

p2.en: To move from a higher to a lower place; or for prices/levels to fall.
p2.ex1: Temperatures came down sharply at dawn.
p2.ex2: She came down the slope toward the shore carefully.
p2.example: The fog came down quickly, making the shore almost invisible.

p2.en: To become ill with something.
p2.ex1: She came down with fever the day after the accident.
p2.ex2: Half the crew came down with food poisoning.
p2.example: He came down with a cold after drifting in the cold water.

p2.en: To appear or become known.
p2.ex1: The sun came out just as they reached the shore.
p2.ex2: Details of the accident came out slowly over the following days.
p2.example: The truth came out when the researcher examined the rope.
