p2.en: To regain consciousness; or to change your opinion.
p2.ex1: It took a while but he finally came round to the idea.
p2.ex2: The doctor was relieved when the patient came round.
p2.example: She came round a few minutes after fainting on the shore.

p2.en: To arise or be mentioned; to move upward.
p2.ex1: An unexpected problem came up just as they reached the shore.
p2.ex2: His name came up when the researcher examined the evidence.
p2.example: The issue of the untied rope came up during the investigation.

p2.en: Extremely brave and courageous.
p2.ex1: Despite his fear, he acted as brave as a lion.
p2.ex2: The rescue swimmer was as brave as a lion during the emergency.
p2.example: She was as brave as a lion when she dived into the dark water.

p2.en: Extremely busy and active.
p2.ex1: He is always as busy as a bee — never a moment to rest.
p2.ex2: The researcher was as busy as a bee gathering data.
p2.example: She was as busy as a bee preparing for the expedition.

p2.en: Completely free, with no restrictions or worries.
p2.ex1: He strolled along the shore feeling as free as a bird.
p2.ex2: Children on summer holidays feel as free as a bird.
p2.example: After finishing the project, she felt as free as a bird.

p2.en: Extremely hungry.
p2.ex1: He arrived home as hungry as a wolf after the long trail.
p2.ex2: She skipped lunch and was as hungry as a wolf by evening.
p2.example: After drifting for hours, they were as hungry as wolves.

p2.en: Very light in weight.
p2.ex1: She carried the bag as if it were as light as a feather.
p2.ex2: He was exhausted but said the pack felt as light as a feather.
p2.example: The lifebelt felt as light as a feather when he threw it.

p2.en: Making no noise at all; very quiet.
p2.ex1: The children sat as quiet as mice during the story.
p2.ex2: He tiptoed along the trail, as quiet as a mouse.
p2.example: She crept past the cottage as quiet as a mouse.

p3.en: To have an influence on someone or something.
p3.ex1: Severe weather can affect travel plans significantly.
p3.ex2: The heatwave affected the entire country for weeks.
p3.example: The drought affected crop production across the region.

p3.en: Attractive or interesting.
p3.ex1: A warm shower after a freezing cold walk is very appealing.
p3.ex2: She found the idea of a peaceful holiday extremely appealing.
p3.example: The cosy cottage in the misty landscape looked very appealing.

p3.en: A large mass of snow and ice falling rapidly down a mountain.
p3.ex1: Hikers were warned about the risk of an avalanche.
p3.ex2: A severe blizzard can trigger an avalanche on steep slopes.
p3.example: The avalanche blocked the entire slope below the village.

p3.en: A severe snowstorm with strong winds.
p3.ex1: They were stuck indoors for days during the blizzard.
p3.ex2: The blizzard caused a breakdown in road transport.
p3.example: A blizzard made the entire landscape invisible.

p3.en: Extremely hot.
p3.ex1: She stayed in the shade because it was boiling hot outside.
p3.ex2: The cosy cottage felt boiling hot in the summer sun.
p3.example: It was boiling hot during the heatwave.

p3.en: The process of forming a close emotional connection with others.
p3.ex1: Family bonding is important during shared experiences.
p3.ex2: Surviving the blizzard together created a strong sense of bonding.
p3.example: The camping trip was great for bonding with the team.

p3.en: A failure of a vehicle, machine, or system to work.
p3.ex1: A breakdown in communication caused the delay.
p3.ex2: The severe fog led to a breakdown in transport services.
p3.example: Their car had a breakdown in the middle of a downpour.

p3.en: Comfortable, warm, and relaxing.
p3.ex1: The warm fire made the room feel cosy and inviting.
p3.ex2: She found the small cafe very cosy on a damp day.
p3.example: They sat in the cosy cottage while the blizzard raged outside.

p3.en: Slightly wet, often in an unpleasant way.
p3.ex1: Her clothes were damp after walking through the mist.
p3.ex2: The damp air near the shore made the cold feel worse.
p3.example: The damp fog made everything feel cold and heavy.

p3.en: A heavy and sudden fall of rain.
p3.ex1: They ran for shelter as the downpour began.
p3.ex2: The downpour lasted for hours, causing flooding in low areas.
p3.example: A sudden downpour ruined their outdoor plans.

p3.en: A long period of time with very little or no rain.
p3.ex1: Farmers struggled to grow crops during the severe drought.
p3.ex2: A heatwave often leads to a drought in warmer regions.
p3.example: The drought left the entire landscape dry and dusty.

p3.en: Including everything or everyone; whole.
p3.ex1: She spent the entire day inside because of the downpour.
p3.ex2: The drought affected the entire region for months.
p3.example: The entire landscape was covered in snow after the blizzard.

p3.en: Thick cloud at ground level that makes it hard to see.
p3.ex1: The fog was so thick that the cottage was barely visible.
p3.ex2: Drivers were warned to slow down due to the morning fog.
p3.example: Dense fog covered the entire slope, making it dangerous.

p3.en: Extremely cold.
p3.ex1: She shivered in the freezing cold air outside the cottage.
p3.ex2: The swimmers emerged from the freezing cold water.
p3.example: It was freezing cold after the blizzard passed through.

p3.en: Feeling annoyed or upset because you cannot achieve something.
p3.ex1: He was frustrated when the breakdown left them stranded.
p3.ex2: They were frustrated by the drought that ruined their plans.
p3.example: She felt frustrated by the fog that blocked the entire trail.

p3.en: A substance in the air that has no fixed shape; also fuel for cooking.
p3.ex1: She cooked on a gas stove in the cosy cottage.
p3.ex2: A gas leak was discovered after the breakdown.
p3.example: The heatwave increased the demand for gas and air conditioning.

p3.en: Small balls of ice that fall from the sky like rain.
p3.ex1: The hail left dents in the roof of the cottage.
p3.ex2: They were caught in hail on the way down the slope.
p3.example: A sudden hail shower hit the slope during the hike.

p3.en: A period of unusually hot weather.
p3.ex1: Water supplies dropped during the severe heatwave.
p3.ex2: The heatwave followed months of drought across the region.
p3.example: The heatwave made the entire country boiling hot for weeks.

p3.en: Warm and damp in a way that feels uncomfortable.
p3.ex1: It was so humid that even the shade felt uncomfortable.
p3.ex2: Tropical climates tend to be hot and humid.
p3.example: The humid air after the downpour felt sticky and heavy.

p3.en: An extremely powerful tropical storm with strong winds.
p3.ex1: The entire town was evacuated before the hurricane arrived.
p3.ex2: A hurricane is far more severe than a typical downpour.
p3.example: The hurricane caused widespread damage to the coastal landscape.

p3.en: Perfect for a particular purpose.
p3.ex1: A cool breeze made the conditions ideal for hiking.
p3.ex2: This spot in the shade is ideal for relaxing on a hot day.
p3.example: The cosy cottage was ideal for a winter holiday.

p3.en: A feeling of great happiness.
p3.ex1: There was a sense of joy and bonding around the campfire.
p3.ex2: Seeing the sun after days of fog filled him with joy.
p3.example: The first snow of winter brought her great joy.

p3.en: The visible features of an area of land.
p3.ex1: A drought can turn a green landscape into a dusty wasteland.
p3.ex2: The entire landscape was covered in mist at dawn.
p3.example: The snowy landscape after the blizzard was stunning.

p3.en: A light form of fog; very small water droplets in the air.
p3.ex1: She could barely make out the cottage through the mist.
p3.ex2: The mist lifted by mid-morning, revealing the beautiful landscape.
p3.example: A thin mist covered the valley in the early morning.

p3.en: The act of moving from one place to another.
p3.ex1: There was no movement in the fog — everything was still.
p3.ex2: The movement of the clouds signalled an incoming downpour.
p3.example: She noticed a sudden movement in the mist near the slope.

p3.en: Very serious, extreme, or harsh.
p3.ex1: A severe drought can lead to widespread food shortages.
p3.ex2: She suffered a severe headache after the humid, boiling hot day.
p3.example: The severe blizzard blocked roads across the entire region.

p3.en: A cool, dark area sheltered from the sun.
p3.ex1: She rested in the shade of the cottage after the long hike.
p3.ex2: The trees provided ideal shade on the humid summer day.
p3.example: They sat in the shade during the boiling hot heatwave.

p3.en: A short period of rain; also a device for washing.
p3.ex1: A sudden shower interrupted their stroll through the landscape.
p3.ex2: The shower lasted only minutes but left everything damp.
p3.example: A brief shower of hail hit the slope unexpectedly.

p3.en: A surface that goes upward or downward at an angle.
p3.ex1: They skied carefully down the icy slope after the blizzard.
p3.ex2: The fog made it hard to see the bottom of the slope.
p3.example: The avalanche swept down the entire slope within seconds.

p3.en: Feeling hot and damp; unpleasant to touch.
p3.ex1: It was sticky and boiling hot even in the shade.
p3.ex2: After the downpour, the ground was muddy and sticky.
p3.example: The humid air made her skin feel sticky all day.

p3.en: A very large and destructive ocean wave caused by an earthquake.
p3.ex1: Emergency services responded immediately after the tsunami warning.
p3.ex2: The tsunami caused a breakdown in infrastructure across the region.
p3.example: The tsunami flooded the entire coastal landscape.

p3.en: When a volcano suddenly throws out lava, ash, and gas.
p3.ex1: The island was evacuated before the volcanic eruption.
p3.ex2: A volcanic eruption can affect the climate for months.
p3.example: The volcanic eruption covered the entire landscape in ash.

p3.en: The quality of being warm; also a feeling of kindness.
p3.ex1: She was grateful for the warmth of the fire after the freezing cold day.
p3.ex2: The warmth of the summer sun lifted everyone's mood.
p3.example: The warmth of the cosy cottage was a relief after the blizzard.

p4.en: Completely or totally; used to emphasise something.
p4.ex1: She was absolutely exhausted after the long trail.
p4.ex2: Without a doubt, it was absolutely the right decision.
p4.example: The scenery was absolutely breathtaking at dawn.

p4.en: After a short period of time; soon.
p4.ex1: He set off at dawn and before long reached the cottage.
p4.ex2: Before long, the downpour had turned into a blizzard.
p4.example: Before long, the mist had covered the entire slope.

p4.ru: в конечном итоге, в конце концов
p4.en: After a long time or series of events.
p4.ex1: She eventually came round after fainting.
p4.ex2: The drought eventually ended after months of no rainfall.
p4.example: They eventually reached the shore after drifting for hours.

p4.en: Slowly and steadily over a period of time.
p4.ex1: She gradually became aware of the movement in the mist.
p4.ex2: The temperature gradually dropped as the blizzard approached.
p4.example: The fog gradually lifted to reveal the stunning landscape.

p4.en: Far away, but still visible.
p4.ex1: She spotted the trail in the distance through the mist.
p4.ex2: The sound of the emergency services could be heard in the distance.
p4.example: In the distance, they could see the outline of the cottage.

p4.en: In the period of time between two events.
p4.ex1: In the meantime, she observed the changing landscape.
p4.ex2: The blizzard was getting worse; in the meantime, they waited.
p4.example: Help was coming; in the meantime, they stayed in the cosy cottage.

p4.en: At the beginning; at first.
p4.ex1: She was initially baffled by the peculiar noise.
p4.ex2: He was initially frustrated but eventually came round.
p4.example: Initially, the fog made it impossible to see the slope.

p4.ru: в тот самый момент, когда; точно так же
p4.en: At exactly the same moment; or in exactly the same way.
p4.ex1: Just as the mist cleared, the sun came out.
p4.ex2: Just as she reached the shore, the blizzard hit.
p4.example: Just as they set off, a sudden downpour began.

p4.en: Very large in size or amount.
p4.ex1: The tsunami caused massive destruction along the coast.
p4.ex2: There was a massive downpour that flooded the entire road.
p4.example: A massive avalanche covered the entire slope below the village.

p4.en: At the same time as something else is happening.
p4.ex1: She set off along the trail; meanwhile, he called for help.
p4.ex2: The heatwave continued; meanwhile, the drought worsened.
p4.example: The blizzard intensified; meanwhile, they searched for shelter.

p4.en: Sometimes, but not often.
p4.ex1: She occasionally glanced back at the cottage in the distance.
p4.ex2: A blizzard occasionally hits this region in early spring.
p4.example: They occasionally saw movement in the mist near the shore.

p4.en: To turn upside down or cause something to fall over.
p4.ex1: The hurricane overturned several vehicles near the shore.
p4.ex2: She watched in horror as the boat overturned in the downpour.
p4.example: The massive wave caused the boat to overturn.

p4.en: To arrive at a place or achieve a goal.
p4.ex1: She reached the cottage before the blizzard got worse.
p4.ex2: Eventually, they reached the top of the slope.
p4.example: They finally reached the shore just as dawn was breaking.

p4.en: To meet someone by chance; or to encounter a problem.
p4.ex1: They ran into trouble when the blizzard hit the slope.
p4.ex2: He ran into the journalist just as he set off along the trail.
p4.example: She ran into her researcher friend while strolling near the shore.

p4.en: To begin a journey.
p4.ex1: She set off along the trail with no idea of what lay ahead.
p4.ex2: Just as they set off, the downpour started.
p4.example: They set off at dawn before the heatwave began.

p4.en: Without any problems or difficulties; in a calm, even way.
p4.ex1: Everything went smoothly until the breakdown occurred.
p4.ex2: The rescue operation was carried out smoothly by the emergency services.
p4.example: Despite the fog, the journey went smoothly.

p4.en: Physical or mental power; the ability to do difficult things.
p4.ex1: It took all his strength to row against the current.
p4.ex2: The bonding experience gave the team great emotional strength.
p4.example: She showed incredible strength during the hurricane.

p4.en: To suddenly start laughing or crying.
p4.ex1: She burst into tears when she finally reached the shore safely.
p4.ex2: He burst out laughing at the peculiar situation they were in.
p4.word: I burst out laughing / into tears.
p4.example: I burst out laughing when he slipped on the wet rocks.

p4.en: Used when you are so surprised you cannot speak.
p4.ex1: She was speechless when the emergency services arrived so quickly.
p4.ex2: He was left speechless by the stunning landscape at dawn.
p4.example: I was left speechless when I saw the massive tsunami wave.

p4.en: Used to say something happened unexpectedly and surprised you.
p4.ex1: She was taken by surprise by the seal near the shore.
p4.ex2: He was taken by surprise when the boat began to overturn.
p4.example: I was taken by surprise when the blizzard hit so suddenly.

p4.en: Used to say something frightened or startled you suddenly.
p4.ex1: The loud crack of thunder made everyone jump.
p4.ex2: It made me jump when the shadow appeared out of the mist.
p4.example: The sudden yell in the silence made me jump.

p4.en: Used to say something was irritating or annoying you.
p4.ex1: The constant fog was getting on everyone's nerves.
p4.ex2: His muttering in silence was getting on my nerves.
p4.word: It was getting on my nerves.
p4.example: The damp, humid weather was getting on my nerves.

p4.en: Used to describe extreme excitement, fear, or nervousness.
p4.ex1: My heart was beating furiously when the shadow appeared.
p4.ex2: She admitted her heart was beating furiously as the avalanche approached.
p4.example: My heart was beating furiously as the boat began to drift out.

p4.en: Used to say something is completely certain.
p4.ex1: Without a doubt, the scenery was absolutely stunning.
p4.ex2: Without a doubt, the blizzard was the most severe in years.
p4.example: Without a doubt, it was the most thrilling experience of her life.

p1.en: To be able to reach, enter, or use something.
p1.ex1: She accessed the city council's findings online.
p1.ex2: Not everyone can access affordable healthcare easily.
p1.example: Residents can now access the new pedestrian area by footpath.

p1.en: Easy to reach, use, or understand.
p1.ex1: Public transport should be affordable and accessible.
p1.ex2: The city council aimed to make all pedestrian areas accessible.
p1.example: The new footpath made the park accessible to all residents.

p1.en: To start using a new method, plan, or way of living.
p1.ex1: Many residents adopted eco-friendly lifestyles to help the environment.
p1.ex2: The council voted to adopt the extension proposal.
p1.example: The city council adopted a workable plan to reduce traffic congestion.

p1.en: Not too expensive; within reach of most people.
p1.ex1: Affordable public transport helps reduce traffic congestion.
p1.ex2: She looked for an affordable alternative to driving to work.
p1.example: The city council proposed affordable housing along with new footpaths.

p1.en: Similar or in the same way.
p1.ex1: Urban and rural communities alike face environmental challenges.
p1.ex2: Young and old alike benefited from the new pedestrian area.
p1.example: The plan was supported by residents and officials alike.

p1.en: In addition to; together with.
p1.ex1: The findings, along with residents' feedback, were published online.
p1.ex2: She adopted a healthy lifestyle along with regular exercise.
p1.example: Along with the new footpath, the council added cycling lanes.

p1.en: Another option that can be chosen instead.
p1.ex1: The council proposed several alternatives to the controversial plan.
p1.ex2: She found an affordable alternative to taking the car.
p1.example: Cycling is a good alternative to driving in urban areas.

p1.en: To officially say something is not allowed.
p1.ex1: Several cities have banned diesel cars to reduce emissions.
p1.ex2: They proposed banning construction during peak traffic hours.
p1.example: The city council voted to ban private vehicles from the pedestrian area.

p1.en: To gain an advantage from something; an advantage or positive effect.
p1.ex1: The extension of the footpath will benefit numerous commuters.
p1.ex2: Clean air is one of the key benefits of reducing traffic congestion.
p1.example: Residents benefit from having a pedestrian area in the city centre.

p1.en: The reason something happens; also a goal worth fighting for.
p1.ex1: She volunteered for a cause she truly believed in.
p1.ex2: Reducing emissions is a cause that the city council strongly supports.
p1.example: Traffic congestion is a major cause of air pollution in urban areas.

p1.en: The group of elected people responsible for running a city.
p1.ex1: Residents were invited to inquire about the council's findings.
p1.ex2: The city council proposed a ban on vehicles in the urban centre.
p1.example: The city council approved the construction of a new pedestrian area.

p1.en: The act of finishing something.
p1.ex1: Upon completion, the new pedestrian area will serve thousands of residents.
p1.ex2: The construction project is close to completion.
p1.example: The completion of the footpath extension was delayed by bad weather.

p1.en: The process of building something.
p1.ex1: The construction caused traffic congestion for several weeks.
p1.ex2: Residents complained about noise during the construction phase.
p1.example: Construction of the new pedestrian area begins next month.

p1.en: To include something; or to keep something under control.
p1.ex1: Measures were put in place to contain emissions from vehicles.
p1.ex2: The pack contained leaflets about the new urban pedestrian area.
p1.example: The report contained the council's findings on traffic congestion.

p1.en: Causing strong disagreement or debate.
p1.ex1: The controversial construction plan divided local residents.
p1.ex2: Numerous residents protested the controversial extension proposal.
p1.example: The ban on private vehicles was a controversial decision.

p1.en: To deal successfully with a difficult situation.
p1.ex1: She found it hard to cope with the noise from the construction site.
p1.ex2: Volunteers helped residents cope with the impact of the controversial changes.
p1.example: Urban infrastructure often struggles to cope with heavy traffic congestion.

p1.en: Working well without wasting time or resources.
p1.ex1: The city council proposed a more efficient alternative to the current plan.
p1.ex2: Solar panels are an efficient and affordable source of energy.
p1.example: An efficient public transport system can reduce traffic congestion significantly.

p1.en: Gas or other substances released into the air, often harmful.
p1.ex1: Electric buses produce far fewer emissions than diesel ones.
p1.ex2: Numerous measures were proposed to cut emissions from construction vehicles.
p1.example: The council aimed to reduce vehicle emissions in the urban centre.

p1.en: To make certain that something will happen.
p1.ex1: She worked to ensure that the findings were published quickly.
p1.ex2: The extension was designed to ensure smooth traffic flow.
p1.example: The city council ensured that all footpaths were safe and accessible.

p1.en: To make something longer, larger, or cover more.
p1.ex1: They planned to extend the footpath to include the urban park.
p1.ex2: The deadline for the construction was extended by two weeks.
p1.example: The council voted to extend the pedestrian area along the riverside.

p1.en: An addition that makes something longer or bigger.
p1.ex1: She applied for an extension to complete the findings report.
p1.ex2: The extension of the pedestrian area was welcomed by volunteers.
p1.example: The extension of the footpath will benefit numerous residents.

p1.en: Something that contributes to a result or situation.
p1.ex1: The council considered numerous factors before adopting the plan.
p1.ex2: Affordability is an important factor when choosing an alternative lifestyle.
p1.example: Traffic congestion is a key factor in urban air pollution.

p1.en: The results or conclusions of a study or investigation.
p1.ex1: Her findings confirmed that the pedestrian area had improved well-being.
p1.ex2: Residents were invited to inquire about the findings at a public meeting.
p1.example: The council published its findings on traffic congestion and emissions.

p1.en: A narrow path for walking, often through countryside or a park.
p1.ex1: The footpath extension made the park accessible to all residents.
p1.ex2: She took the footpath through the urban park to avoid congestion.
p1.example: A new footpath was constructed along the river to reduce traffic.

p1.en: A single person, considered separately from a group.
p1.ex1: The plan benefits every individual who lives in the urban area.
p1.ex2: Volunteers were praised as individuals committed to a worthy cause.
p1.example: Each individual in the community can make a difference.

p1.en: To ask for information about something.
p1.ex1: She inquired about the findings from the urban traffic study.
p1.ex2: He called to inquire about affordable alternatives to driving.
p1.example: Residents can inquire about the construction timeline at the city council.

p1.en: To include or require something as part of a process.
p1.ex1: The project involved numerous volunteers from across the city.
p1.ex2: Reducing emissions involves adopting a more sustainable lifestyle.
p1.example: The plan involved banning private vehicles from the pedestrian area.

p1.en: The way a person or group lives, including habits and activities.
p1.ex1: A healthy lifestyle can significantly improve your well-being.
p1.ex2: She changed her lifestyle to reduce her impact on the environment.
p1.example: Adopting an urban lifestyle often means relying more on public transport.

p1.en: Connected to or associated with something else.
p1.ex1: Poor well-being is often linked to a lack of green spaces.
p1.ex2: The construction delays were linked to funding issues.
p1.example: Traffic congestion is directly linked to increased emissions.

p1.en: To have a positive effect on a situation.
p1.ex1: Even small changes in lifestyle can make a difference to the environment.
p1.ex2: She believed that every individual could make a difference.
p1.example: Volunteers make a real difference to the quality of urban spaces.

p1.en: A large number of.
p1.ex1: There are numerous benefits to having pedestrian areas in cities.
p1.ex2: She reviewed numerous findings before writing her report.
p1.example: Numerous residents attended the city council meeting.

p1.en: A set of items together; or a group.
p1.ex1: She received a pack containing the findings and the proposal.
p1.ex2: A pack of volunteers helped with the construction of the footpath.
p1.example: The council distributed a pack of information to all residents.

p1.en: A zone in a town or city where vehicles are not allowed.
p1.ex1: Numerous residents supported the extension of the pedestrian area.
p1.ex2: The controversial ban on cars created a vibrant pedestrian area.
p1.example: The new pedestrian area reduced traffic congestion in the city centre.

p1.en: Before a particular time or event.
p1.ex1: The council had previously published findings on urban emissions.
p1.ex2: She had previously volunteered for the same cause.
p1.example: The footpath had previously been used only by cyclists.

p1.en: To continue doing something or move forward with a plan.
p1.ex1: She was unsure whether to proceed with the controversial proposal.
p1.ex2: They proceeded with the extension despite numerous objections.
p1.example: The council voted to proceed with the construction of the footpath.

p1.en: To officially forbid something by law or rule.
p1.ex1: Emissions above a certain level are now prohibited in the urban zone.
p1.ex2: Construction at night is prohibited to protect residents' well-being.
p1.example: The city council prohibited vehicles from entering the pedestrian area.

p1.en: To make something known to the public.
p1.ex1: She volunteered to help publicise the cause on social media.
p1.ex2: The new pedestrian area was widely publicised before its completion.
p1.example: The council worked hard to publicise its findings on traffic congestion.

p1.en: How good or bad something is; a high standard.
p1.ex1: Reducing emissions is essential for air quality in cities.
p1.ex2: The well-being of residents depends on the quality of their environment.
p1.example: The extension of green footpaths improved the quality of urban life.

p1.en: The act of making something smaller in size, amount, or degree.
p1.ex1: A reduction in emissions is one of the key goals of the city council.
p1.ex2: There has been a notable reduction in construction noise this month.
p1.example: The new plan led to a significant reduction in traffic congestion.

p1.en: Concerning or on the subject of something.
p1.ex1: He inquired about the findings regarding emissions in the urban area.
p1.ex2: Residents had numerous concerns regarding the proposed ban.
p1.example: She wrote to the city council regarding the controversial construction plan.

p1.en: A person who lives in a particular place.
p1.ex1: Numerous residents supported the extension of the pedestrian area.
p1.ex2: The city council consulted residents before proceeding with the ban.
p1.example: Residents of the urban area were invited to comment on the findings.

p1.en: The top layer of the earth in which plants grow.
p1.ex1: Pollution threatens the quality of soil in urban areas.
p1.ex2: She planted trees to improve the soil and well-being of the community.
p1.example: Construction in the urban park damaged the soil and nearby footpaths.

p1.en: The act of continuing to live or exist, especially in difficult conditions.
p1.ex1: Volunteers worked to ensure the survival of the community garden.
p1.ex2: The survival of the pedestrian area project required strong public support.
p1.example: The survival of green urban spaces depends on reducing emissions.

p1.en: To be likely to cause harm or damage to something.
p1.ex1: The controversial construction plan threatened the survival of the footpath.
p1.ex2: Pollution threatens the quality of soil in numerous urban areas.
p1.example: Traffic congestion and emissions threaten the well-being of urban residents.

p1.en: A situation where roads are so full of vehicles that traffic moves slowly.
p1.ex1: Traffic congestion is linked to increased emissions in urban areas.
p1.ex2: The pedestrian area was created to ease traffic congestion in the centre.
p1.example: The city council introduced a ban to reduce traffic congestion.

p1.en: Related to a town or city.
p1.ex1: The city council aimed to improve urban well-being through green spaces.
p1.ex2: An urban lifestyle involves numerous challenges and benefits alike.
p1.example: Urban residents often cope with high levels of traffic congestion.

p1.en: A person who does work without being paid, usually to help others.
p1.ex1: The cause attracted numerous volunteers from the local community.
p1.ex2: She became a volunteer to make a difference in her urban neighbourhood.
p1.example: Volunteers helped with the construction of the new footpath.

p1.en: The state of being healthy, comfortable, and happy.
p1.ex1: The city council's findings linked traffic congestion to poor well-being.
p1.ex2: Reducing emissions is essential for the well-being of the community.
p1.example: Green spaces contribute significantly to the well-being of urban residents.

p1.en: Practical and able to be done successfully.
p1.ex1: She proposed a workable plan to extend the footpath network.
p1.ex2: Not all suggestions are workable, but this one has real potential.
p1.example: The council needed a workable alternative to the controversial ban.

p2.en: To separate from something or stop being connected, especially from technology.
p2.ex1: A holiday in a remote area helps you truly disconnect from work.
p2.ex2: He felt a growing disconnect between urban life and his well-being.
p2.example: She needed to disconnect from social media to enjoy quality time outdoors.

p2.en: The system of trade, industry, and money in a country or region.
p2.ex1: The city council considered the economic benefits of the pedestrian area.
p2.ex2: A strong economy can make leisure more affordable for residents.
p2.example: Recreational tourism plays an important role in the local economy.

p2.en: Free time when you are not working, used for relaxation or enjoyment.
p2.ex1: She enjoys leisure activities like cycling and hiking.
p2.ex2: The new recreational area gave residents more leisure options.
p2.example: People are spending more leisure time in urban parks and green spaces.

p2.en: The gas in the air that living things need to breathe.
p2.ex1: Reducing emissions helps maintain healthy oxygen levels in the atmosphere.
p2.ex2: Green footpaths surrounded by trees provide clean oxygen for residents.
p2.example: Trees in urban areas produce oxygen and improve air quality.

p2.en: A calm and quiet environment, free from noise or disturbance.
p2.ex1: The new pedestrian area gave residents a place to enjoy peace and quiet.
p2.ex2: After the construction, they finally had peace and quiet.
p2.example: She moved away from the urban centre in search of peace and quiet.

p2.en: The advantages and disadvantages of something.
p2.ex1: She listed the pros and cons before deciding to volunteer.
p2.ex2: There are pros and cons to both urban and rural lifestyles.
p2.example: The city council weighed up the pros and cons of the controversial ban.

p2.en: Time spent doing meaningful activities, especially with family or friends.
p2.ex1: She valued quality time with her children over a busy social schedule.
p2.ex2: Disconnecting from technology helps people enjoy quality time.
p2.example: The new recreational park gives families quality time together outdoors.

p2.en: Activities done for enjoyment or relaxation during free time.
p2.ex1: Recreation in green spaces is linked to improved well-being.
p2.ex2: The city council invested in recreation facilities for all residents.
p2.example: The footpath was designed for recreation as well as commuting.

p2.en: Relating to activities done for fun or relaxation.
p2.ex1: Recreational cycling is a popular alternative to urban driving.
p2.ex2: She used the recreational footpath every weekend to disconnect and relax.
p2.example: The recreational area attracted numerous volunteers and residents alike.

p2.en: The state of being free from stress; rest and enjoyment.
p2.ex1: Quality time in nature is one of the best forms of relaxation.
p2.ex2: The recreational park was created to offer residents a space for relaxation.
p2.example: She found relaxation by walking along the new footpath by the river.

p2.en: Difficult to make or deal with.
p2.ex1: It was a tough decision to proceed with the controversial construction plan.
p2.ex2: She admitted it was tough to balance economic growth with well-being.
p2.example: Banning vehicles from the urban centre was a tough decision for the council.

p1.en: Something done to achieve a goal or deal with a situation.
p1.ex1: Crucial action is needed to reduce emissions in urban areas.
p1.ex2: She responded to the request by taking immediate action.
p1.example: The community took action to support less fortunate residents.

p1.en: Help or support given to someone who needs it.
p1.ex1: She offered her assistance at the fundraising event.
p1.ex2: Volunteers gave assistance to less fortunate members of the community.
p1.example: The organisation provided assistance to people in need.

p1.en: Without any particular plan, pattern, or purpose.
p1.ex1: She picked a purchase at random from the reusable bag.
p1.ex2: Items were given away at random to highlight the cause.
p1.example: Winners were chosen at random from all the donations received.

p1.en: Only just; almost not at all.
p1.ex1: He barely had time to take a sip before the event started.
p1.ex2: The organisation barely covered costs despite a large percentage of donations.
p1.example: She could barely underestimate how much the community had grown.

p1.en: Very strange or unusual.
p1.ex1: He had a bizarre instinct to give away his purchase to a stranger.
p1.ex2: The community came up with a bizarre but effective way to promote the cause.
p1.example: It seemed bizarre that such a small action could make such a big difference.

p1.en: A group of people living in the same area or sharing a common interest.
p1.ex1: She volunteered to highlight the issues facing her local community.
p1.ex2: A strong community responds to requests for assistance quickly.
p1.example: The community came together to support those in need.

p1.en: Extremely important or necessary.
p1.ex1: It is crucial to take action before the situation worsens.
p1.ex2: Spreading awareness is a crucial part of any fundraising campaign.
p1.example: Empathy is crucial when working with less fortunate individuals.

p1.en: A reduction in the usual price of something.
p1.ex1: She received a discount on her purchase as part of the promotion.
p1.ex2: A percentage of the discount was donated to the community fund.
p1.example: The shop offered a discount to encourage people to buy reusable bags.

p1.en: Money or goods given to help people or a cause.
p1.ex1: The fundraising event raised a large percentage of its target through donations.
p1.ex2: Every donation, no matter how small, can make a crucial difference.
p1.example: She made a generous donation to support those in need.

p1.en: Showing the ability to understand and share the feelings of others.
p1.ex1: She was empathetic toward less fortunate members of the community.
p1.ex2: An empathetic approach is crucial when responding to requests for assistance.
p1.example: A good volunteer should be empathetic and respond to people in need.

p1.en: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another person.
p1.ex1: She showed great empathy when responding to the needs of others.
p1.ex2: Empathy is a soft skill that is crucial in any community-based organisation.
p1.example: Empathy motivates many people to give back to their communities.

p1.en: To give something to others for free.
p1.ex1: She gave away a percentage of her profit to those in need.
p1.ex2: They gave away purchases at random to highlight the cause.
p1.example: The organisation gave away reusable bags to promote sustainability.

p1.en: To return something; or to do something to help others in return for what you have received.
p1.ex1: He gave back by donating a percentage of his profit to charity.
p1.ex2: Volunteering is a great way to give back and respond to those in need.
p1.example: She wanted to give back to the community that had supported her.

p1.en: To draw attention to something important.
p1.ex1: She used social media to highlight the community's request for donations.
p1.ex2: The event was designed to highlight the crucial role of empathy.
p1.example: The campaign highlighted the struggles of less fortunate people.

p1.en: Requiring something; lacking the necessities of life.
p1.ex1: She donated reusable bags to families in need.
p1.ex2: Communities in need of support benefit greatly from volunteer action.
p1.example: The organisation responds to those most in need of assistance.

p1.en: As a reaction or reply to something.
p1.ex1: She gave back to the charity in response to the request for assistance.
p1.ex2: In response to the campaign, numerous residents donated their purchases.
p1.example: In response to the donation drive, the community raised a record amount.

p1.en: A natural tendency to behave in a certain way without thinking.
p1.ex1: He acted on instinct when he decided to give away his profit.
p1.ex2: A bizarre instinct led him to take a sip and then share the rest.
p1.example: Her instinct was to respond immediately to those in need.

p1.en: To bring something new into use or present someone formally.
p1.ex1: The community introduced a donation scheme to help less fortunate residents.
p1.ex2: He was introduced at the event as the key motivation behind the campaign.
p1.example: She introduced a reusable packaging option to promote sustainability.

p1.en: People who have fewer advantages or are in a worse situation than others.
p1.ex1: She donated a percentage of her profit to help less fortunate families.
p1.ex2: Empathy motivates many people to assist those less fortunate than themselves.
p1.example: The campaign aimed to support less fortunate members of the community.

p1.en: Very comfortable and expensive.
p1.ex1: The event was held at a luxurious venue to attract large donations.
p1.ex2: He felt bizarre spending money on luxurious purchases while others were in need.
p1.example: She gave up her luxurious lifestyle to volunteer in a less fortunate community.

p1.en: Something very expensive that is pleasant but not essential.
p1.ex1: She pointed out that luxury items were given away at random to raise funds.
p1.ex2: He considered quality time outdoors a luxury in his busy lifestyle.
p1.example: For many, a reusable product is a luxury they cannot afford.

p1.en: The reason or desire that causes someone to do something.
p1.ex1: The campaign gave the community motivation to take crucial action.
p1.ex2: Seeing the impact of donations was motivation enough to continue giving back.
p1.example: Her motivation for volunteering was a deep sense of empathy.

p1.en: An amount expressed as a fraction of 100.
p1.ex1: She pointed out that a large percentage of the community had responded.
p1.ex2: The organisation gave away a percentage of its profit to local charities.
p1.example: A percentage of all purchases was donated to those in need.

p1.en: To draw attention to a fact or piece of information.
p1.ex1: He pointed out the bizarre inconsistency in the donation figures.
p1.ex2: The report pointed out that a large percentage of residents were in need.
p1.example: She pointed out that empathy is a crucial soft skill for volunteers.

p1.en: Money gained after costs have been paid.
p1.ex1: She reinvested her profit into promoting reusable products.
p1.ex2: The fundraising event made a significant profit for those in need.
p1.example: The company donated a percentage of its profit to community causes.

p1.en: To support or encourage something; to raise awareness of it.
p1.ex1: She used social media to promote the donation drive.
p1.ex2: The organisation promoted reusable alternatives to single-use products.
p1.example: The campaign promoted empathy and giving back within the community.

p1.en: Something that has been bought.
p1.ex1: She gave away her purchase at random to someone in need.
p1.ex2: Choosing reusable products is a purchase that benefits the environment.
p1.example: A percentage of every purchase was donated to a community fund.

p1.en: To ask for something formally or politely.
p1.ex1: The organisation requested a percentage of profits from local businesses.
p1.ex2: He requested that volunteers respond as quickly as possible.
p1.example: She requested assistance from the community to support the donation drive.

p1.en: To say or do something as a reaction to something.
p1.ex1: She responded to those in need with empathy and action.
p1.ex2: He was moved to respond after seeing the highlight of the campaign.
p1.example: The community responded to the request with an overwhelming number of donations.

p1.en: Able to be used more than once.
p1.ex1: The organisation gave away reusable bottles to highlight the cause.
p1.ex2: Switching to reusable products is a crucial action for reducing waste.
p1.example: She promoted reusable bags as a sustainable alternative to single-use ones.

p1.en: A personal quality such as communication or empathy that helps you work with others.
p1.ex1: She highlighted soft skills as crucial for community work.
p1.ex2: Employers increasingly value soft skills alongside technical knowledge.
p1.example: Empathy is one of the most valuable soft skills a volunteer can have.

p1.en: To cause something to reach more people or cover a wider area.
p1.ex1: She spread the message by sharing the donation request on social media.
p1.ex2: Word spread quickly about the bizarre but effective promotion.
p1.example: The campaign spread awareness about the needs of less fortunate communities.

p1.en: To drink a small amount of a liquid.
p1.ex1: He took a sip and then passed the bottle to someone in need.
p1.ex2: Take a sip and consider how many people lack access to clean water.
p1.example: She took a sip of water before responding to the crowd at the fundraiser.

p1.en: To make an effort to do something carefully and without rushing.
p1.ex1: He took the time to point out the crucial role of empathy.
p1.ex2: Taking the time to give back makes a crucial difference to a community.
p1.example: She took the time to respond personally to every donation request.

p1.en: To think something is smaller or less important than it really is.
p1.ex1: She underestimated how much motivation the community would show.
p1.ex2: People often underestimate the value of soft skills like empathy.
p1.example: Don't underestimate the impact of a small donation on those in need.

p1.en: To see something happen, especially something important or unusual.
p1.ex1: He witnessed a bizarre act of kindness that motivated him to give back.
p1.ex2: Volunteers witnessed the crucial difference their assistance made.
p1.example: She witnessed the community's response to the donation drive firsthand.

p1.en: Used to introduce a topic you are about to discuss.
p1.ex1: When it comes to donations, every percentage counts.
p1.ex2: When it comes to soft skills, empathy is the most crucial of all.
p1.example: When it comes to empathy, actions speak louder than words.

p2.en: To succeed in doing or completing something.
p2.ex1: He accomplished the task despite numerous obstacles.
p2.ex2: Together, they accomplished something truly meaningful.
p2.example: She accomplished her goal of raising enough donations for the community.

p2.en: Something that has been done successfully; a skill or achievement.
p2.ex1: She listed her accomplishments confidently in the application.
p2.ex2: Every small action is an accomplishment worth celebrating.
p2.example: Organising the fundraising event was a major accomplishment.

p2.en: The way someone or something looks.
p2.ex1: She made a strong first impression with her professional appearance.
p2.ex2: The appearance of the community space improved after the renovation.
p2.example: Don't judge people by their appearance — focus on their soft skills.

p2.en: A formal written request for something, such as a job or place.
p2.ex1: His application stood out because of his accomplishments and soft skills.
p2.ex2: The deadline for the application is the end of this month.
p2.example: She submitted her application to volunteer at the non-profit organisation.

p2.en: To make a formal request for something; or to be relevant to something.
p2.ex1: These rules apply to all residents, without exception.
p2.ex2: He applied to the organisation to volunteer at their next fundraising event.
p2.example: She decided to apply for the role of community coordinator.

p2.en: The act of going to or being present at a place or event.
p2.ex1: Regular attendance at events helps build a sense of community.
p2.ex2: She confirmed her attendance at the fundraising event in response to the request.
p2.example: Attendance at the community meeting was higher than expected.

p2.en: A mixture of two or more things together.
p2.ex1: She used a combination of soft skills and technical knowledge.
p2.ex2: The success was down to a combination of hard work and motivation.
p2.example: A combination of empathy and action is crucial for community work.

p2.en: To put two or more things together.
p2.ex1: He combined volunteering with his studies to develop soft skills.
p2.ex2: Empathy combined with action makes a crucial difference.
p2.example: She combined her donation drive with a community awareness campaign.

p2.en: To focus your attention on something.
p2.ex1: He concentrated on his application to make the best impression.
p2.ex2: The campaign concentrated on highlighting the crucial role of donations.
p2.example: She concentrated on spreading the message to less fortunate communities.

p2.en: To mistake one thing or person for another.
p2.ex1: She confused the date of the fundraising event with the donation deadline.
p2.ex2: People often confuse accomplishment with luck.
p2.example: Don't confuse empathy with sympathy — they have different meanings.

p2.en: To express pleasure at someone's success or good fortune.
p2.ex1: He congratulated her on her successful application.
p2.ex2: The organisation congratulated volunteers on their crucial contributions.
p2.example: She was congratulated on her accomplishments at the community event.

p2.en: To rely on someone or something; to be determined by.
p2.ex1: Her motivation depended on witnessing the impact of her actions.
p2.ex2: A good impression at interview depends on your appearance and soft skills.
p2.example: The success of the donation drive depends on community participation.

p2.en: To give money, goods, or time to help a cause or organisation.
p2.ex1: He donated reusable items to those in need after the fundraising event.
p2.ex2: The organisation asked residents to donate whatever they could afford.
p2.example: She donated a percentage of her profit to the community fund.

p2.en: A formal test; or a careful inspection of something.
p2.ex1: A thorough examination of the application revealed impressive accomplishments.
p2.ex2: The doctor carried out a brief examination before confirming the diagnosis.
p2.example: She passed the examination and was accepted to the volunteer programme.

p2.en: The particular taste of a food or drink.
p2.ex1: The event offered a combination of flavours from different cultures.
p2.ex2: Every flavour of the reusable packaging had a different design.
p2.example: She took a sip of each flavour before choosing her favourite.

p2.en: To accidentally reveal something that was meant to be secret.
p2.ex1: He tried not to give away any hints about the surprise donation.
p2.ex2: Her smile gave away the fact that she had accomplished her goal.
p2.example: Her appearance gave away how nervous she was about the application.

p2.en: To stop doing something; or to stop trying to guess.
p2.ex1: He gave up trying to guess and asked directly.
p2.ex2: Don't give up — your accomplishments speak for themselves.
p2.word: give up (=stop doing sth / stop guessing)
p2.example: She refused to give up on her application despite the setbacks.

p2.en: To make someone feel admiration or respect.
p2.ex1: His accomplishments impressed everyone at the fundraising event.
p2.ex2: A strong application will impress potential employers or organisations.
p2.example: She impressed the panel with her empathy and soft skills.

p2.en: The effect or feeling that someone or something creates.
p2.ex1: His appearance and motivation left a lasting impression on the panel.
p2.ex2: A confident application creates a strong impression of your accomplishments.
p2.example: She made an excellent first impression at the community volunteer interview.

p2.en: To demand something firmly and refuse to accept otherwise.
p2.ex1: He insisted on attending the fundraising event despite his busy schedule.
p2.ex2: The organisation insisted on reusable packaging for all purchases.
p2.example: She insisted on donating a percentage of all profits to charity.

p2.en: To put money, time, or effort into something for a future benefit.
p2.ex1: The organisation invested in reusable equipment to reduce costs.
p2.ex2: Investing in community projects gives back long-term benefits.
p2.example: She invested in developing her soft skills to improve her application.

p2.en: The act of taking part in something.
p2.ex1: He showed strong involvement in spreading awareness about the cause.
p2.ex2: Involvement in volunteer work builds empathy and soft skills.
p2.example: Her involvement in the community fundraiser was crucial to its success.

p2.en: Official or formal agreement to do something.
p2.ex1: Permission to proceed was granted by the organisation.
p2.ex2: He applied for permission to organise the community fundraising event.
p2.example: She asked for permission to give away donated items at the event.

p2.en: To allow someone to do something.
p2.ex1: She was permitted to apply for the role despite her lack of experience.
p2.ex2: The rules do not permit giving away items without prior permission.
p2.example: The council permitted volunteers to use the pedestrian area for the event.

p2.en: A formal party or gathering; or the area where visitors are welcomed.
p2.ex1: She introduced herself at reception before the application interview.
p2.ex2: The warm reception from the community motivated her to give back more.
p2.example: The fundraising event ended with a reception for all volunteers.

p2.en: To mention or speak about something; or to look at something for information.
p2.ex1: He referred to the organisation's guidelines before donating.
p2.ex2: Please refer to the findings report for more information.
p2.example: She referred to her accomplishments when completing the application.

p2.en: The feeling of pleasure when you have done or achieved something.
p2.ex1: Accomplishing her goal gave her a deep sense of satisfaction.
p2.ex2: Volunteering brings a satisfaction that no luxurious purchase can match.
p2.example: She felt great satisfaction from giving back to those in need.

p2.en: To fulfil a need or desire; to make someone pleased.
p2.ex1: The application failed to satisfy the key requirements.
p2.ex2: Nothing satisfied her motivation quite like witnessing her impact.
p2.example: Helping others satisfied her need to give back to the community.

p3.en: Rain that is made acidic by pollution and is harmful to the environment.
p3.ex1: The effects of acid rain on marine life are severe.
p3.ex2: Reducing fossil fuel use is crucial to preventing acid rain.
p3.example: Acid rain caused by exhaust fumes damages forests and soil.

p3.en: A person who takes part in civic life and works to improve their community.
p3.ex1: She became an active citizen after volunteering at the non-profit organisation.
p3.ex2: Active citizens draw society's attention to issues like acid rain and oil spills.
p3.example: Every active citizen can raise awareness about global warming.

p3.en: A state where different things are equal or in the right proportions.
p3.ex1: She tried to maintain a balance between fundraising and her studies.
p3.ex2: Active citizens work to restore the balance between development and nature.
p3.example: A good balance between work and leisure is essential for well-being.

p3.en: An organised series of activities to achieve a goal, especially a social or political one.
p3.ex1: The non-profit organisation launched a campaign to raise money for marine conservation.
p3.ex2: An effective campaign can motivate senior citizens and young people alike.
p3.example: She led a campaign to raise awareness about the greenhouse effect.

p3.en: To supply a battery or device with electricity.
p3.ex1: She charged her device using renewable energy at the community centre.
p3.ex2: Always charge your device before attending an in-person fundraising event.
p3.example: He forgot to charge his phone and was left with a dead battery.

p3.en: To ask someone to pay a particular amount of money.
p3.ex1: They charged a small fee to cover the cost of reusable materials.
p3.ex2: She was surprised by how much they charged for the fundraiser ticket.
p3.example: The non-profit organisation did not charge for attendance at the event.

p3.en: A hard black fossil fuel burned for energy, which produces high emissions.
p3.ex1: Many countries are replacing coal with renewable energy sources.
p3.ex2: She drew attention to the dangers of coal in her fundraising campaign.
p3.example: Burning coal is one of the leading causes of the greenhouse effect.

p3.en: A battery that has no remaining charge and cannot power a device.
p3.ex1: He arrived at the event with a dead battery and no way to reach anyone.
p3.ex2: Always check for a dead battery before setting off on a long trip.
p3.example: She was unable to call for help because of a dead battery.

p3.en: To make someone notice something important.
p3.ex1: She drew the audience's attention to the impact of fossil fuels.
p3.ex2: He drew the senior citizens' attention to the rising effects of global warming.
p3.example: The campaign drew people's attention to the dangers of oil spills.

p3.en: To pull curtains across a window to block light.
p3.ex1: He drew the curtains before the in-person presentation began.
p3.ex2: Drawing the curtains helps maintain warmth and reduce heating costs.
p3.example: She drew the curtains to keep the room cool during the heatwave.

p3.en: Poisonous gases produced by vehicles burning fossil fuels.
p3.ex1: The campaign aimed to reduce exhaust fumes in urban pedestrian areas.
p3.ex2: She raised awareness about the impact of exhaust fumes on marine life.
p3.example: Exhaust fumes from vehicles are a major cause of acid rain.

p3.en: Very severe or intense; going beyond what is normal.
p3.ex1: She took extreme measures to raise money for the environmental campaign.
p3.ex2: The drought was so extreme that it threatened the entire region's water supply.
p3.example: Extreme weather events are becoming more frequent due to global warming.

p3.en: A natural fuel such as coal, oil, or gas formed from ancient organic material.
p3.ex1: The campaign promoted renewable energy as an alternative to fossil fuels.
p3.ex2: Reducing dependence on fossil fuels is crucial to slowing global warming.
p3.example: Burning fossil fuels is the main cause of the greenhouse effect.

p3.en: Making you feel happy and satisfied because of what you are doing.
p3.ex1: Raising awareness about global warming was a fulfilling experience.
p3.ex2: He described fundraising as one of the most fulfilling things he had done.
p3.example: She found volunteering for the non-profit organisation deeply fulfilling.

p3.en: A person who raises money for a cause; or an event held to collect funds.
p3.ex1: The fundraiser attracted senior citizens and young people alike.
p3.ex2: He organised a fundraiser to raise money for renewable energy projects.
p3.example: She became a fundraiser for the marine conservation campaign.

p3.en: An organised event held to collect money for a cause or charity.
p3.ex1: Attendance at the fundraising event exceeded all expectations.
p3.ex2: She combined the in-person campaign with an online fundraising event.
p3.example: The non-profit organisation held a fundraising event to raise awareness about oil spills.

p3.en: The gradual increase in Earth's temperature caused by greenhouse gas emissions.
p3.ex1: The campaign aimed to draw people's attention to the effects of global warming.
p3.ex2: Senior citizens recalled how much the climate had changed due to global warming.
p3.example: Global warming is linked to the burning of fossil fuels.

p3.en: The trapping of the sun's heat in Earth's atmosphere by gases such as CO2.
p3.ex1: She explained the greenhouse effect at the school fundraising event.
p3.ex2: Reducing exhaust fumes is one way to slow down the greenhouse effect.
p3.example: Coal and fossil fuels accelerate the greenhouse effect.

p3.en: Done by being physically present, not online.
p3.ex1: She preferred in-person meetings to discuss the campaign strategy.
p3.ex2: An in-person fundraiser draws more attention than an online campaign.
p3.example: The fundraising event was held in-person for the first time in three years.

p3.en: Relating to the sea and the creatures that live in it.
p3.ex1: The non-profit organisation focused on protecting marine ecosystems.
p3.ex2: She raised money to fund a marine conservation campaign.
p3.example: Oil spills are extremely harmful to marine life.

p3.en: Having no purpose, value, or meaning.
p3.ex1: She argued that extreme measures without public support were meaningless.
p3.ex2: A campaign becomes meaningless if it fails to draw people's attention.
p3.example: Without empathy, fundraising efforts can feel meaningless.

p3.en: Making you feel enthusiastic and ready to take action.
p3.ex1: She found the campaign slogan extremely motivating.
p3.ex2: Hearing about global warming can be terrifying, but also motivating.
p3.example: Witnessing the impact of donations was deeply motivating for the team.

p3.en: An organisation that uses money for its cause rather than making a profit.
p3.ex1: The non-profit organisation hosted a fundraising event about fossil fuels.
p3.ex2: Donations allow non-profit organisations to run campaigns without charging fees.
p3.example: She volunteered for a non-profit organisation focused on renewable energy.

p3.en: An accident in which oil leaks into the sea or environment.
p3.ex1: The fundraising campaign raised money to clean up the oil spill.
p3.ex2: An oil spill can take decades to fully recover from.
p3.example: The oil spill caused extreme damage to the marine ecosystem.

p3.en: All the people living in a particular area or country.
p3.ex1: The campaign aimed to raise awareness among the entire population.
p3.ex2: Senior citizens make up a significant part of the urban population.
p3.example: A growing population places more demand on fossil fuels and resources.

p3.en: To care for and bring up a child until they are an adult.
p3.ex1: She raised her children to be empathetic and aware of global issues.
p3.ex2: Raising a child in an urban area involves unique challenges.
p3.example: Raising a child with good values helps create active citizens.

p3.en: To help people learn about and understand an important issue.
p3.ex1: She used social media to raise awareness about marine oil spills.
p3.ex2: Active citizens raise awareness so that others can take action.
p3.example: The campaign aimed to raise awareness about the greenhouse effect.

p3.en: To collect money, especially for a charity or good cause.
p3.ex1: She raised money to support the renewable energy campaign.
p3.ex2: Every donation helps raise money for those most in need.
p3.example: The non-profit organisation held a fundraising event to raise money.

p3.en: Energy from sources that are naturally replenished, such as sun or wind.
p3.ex1: The campaign promoted renewable energy as an alternative to coal.
p3.ex2: She raised money to fund a renewable energy project in her community.
p3.example: Switching to renewable energy is crucial to reducing the greenhouse effect.

p3.en: To use all of something so that none is left.
p3.ex1: She ran out of motivation until she witnessed the campaign's impact.
p3.ex2: Many regions are running out of affordable fossil fuels.
p3.example: The fundraiser ran out of reusable bags before the event ended.

p3.en: An older person, usually retired.
p3.ex1: The non-profit organisation provided assistance to senior citizens in need.
p3.ex2: She drew attention to the impact of global warming on senior citizens.
p3.example: Senior citizens attended the in-person fundraising event in large numbers.

p3.en: To take action to deal with a problem or situation.
p3.ex1: She took measures to raise awareness about fossil fuels in her community.
p3.ex2: The government must take extreme measures to address global warming.
p3.example: The city council took measures to reduce exhaust fumes in the urban area.

p3.en: A machine used for transporting people or goods.
p3.ex1: Electric vehicles produce fewer emissions than those powered by fossil fuels.
p3.ex2: She used a bicycle rather than a vehicle to reduce her environmental impact.
p3.example: The council banned vehicles from the pedestrian area to reduce exhaust fumes.

p4.en: A feeling of worry or nervousness about something uncertain.
p4.ex1: Anxiety about global warming motivates many people to become active citizens.
p4.ex2: He managed his anxiety by focusing on the fulfilling aspects of the campaign.
p4.example: She felt anxiety before making her first in-person speech at the fundraiser.

p4.en: A part of a road set aside for cyclists.
p4.ex1: She cycled to the fundraising event using the new bicycle lane.
p4.ex2: More bicycle lanes encourage people to use vehicles less and reduce emissions.
p4.example: The city council extended the bicycle lane to reduce vehicle exhaust fumes.

p4.en: To travel regularly between home and work; the journey itself.
p4.ex1: A long daily commute can increase anxiety and affect well-being.
p4.ex2: The new bicycle lane made his commute faster and more fulfilling.
p4.example: She commuted by bicycle rather than car to reduce her emissions.

p4.en: The act of getting rid of something, especially waste.
p4.ex1: The non-profit organisation campaigned for better disposal of vehicle exhaust waste.
p4.ex2: Reusable products reduce the need for disposal of single-use packaging.
p4.example: Proper disposal of fossil fuel waste is crucial for marine health.

p4.en: To make something possible; to give someone the ability to do something.
p4.ex1: The bicycle lane enabled more residents to commute without a vehicle.
p4.ex2: Education enables active citizens to take measures against global warming.
p4.example: Renewable energy enables communities to reduce dependence on fossil fuels.

p4.en: Not looked after or given attention.
p4.ex1: She raised awareness about uncared marine habitats damaged by oil spills.
p4.ex2: The campaign highlighted uncared bicycle lanes that were unsafe to use.
p4.example: Uncared green spaces contribute to anxiety and reduced well-being.

p4.uz: E'tibor qaratish lozim bo'lgan yana bir narsa...
p4.en: Used to add an extra important point to an argument.
p4.ex1: Another point worth mentioning is that bicycle lanes reduce traffic congestion.
p4.ex2: Another point worth mentioning is the anxiety caused by uncared urban spaces.
p4.example: Another point worth mentioning is the impact of exhaust fumes on senior citizens.

p4.en: Used to introduce a conclusion or result that follows logically.
p4.ex1: Fossil fuels are running out; therefore, investing in renewable energy is crucial.
p4.ex2: She raised awareness; therefore, attendance at the fundraising event increased.
p4.example: Global warming is accelerating; therefore, we must take extreme measures now.

p4.en: Used to introduce the final point or summary of an argument.
p4.ex1: To conclude, switching to renewable energy is the most fulfilling action we can take.
p4.ex2: To conclude, raising awareness is the first step toward meaningful change.
p4.example: To conclude, every active citizen has a role to play in reducing global warming.

p1.en: A place where someone lives or stays, especially temporarily.
p1.ex1: The travel package included flights and accommodation.
p1.ex2: Finding affordable accommodation in the city centre can be difficult.
p1.example: She booked accommodation near the university campus for the conference.

p1.en: The reason or principle on which something is based.
p1.ex1: She volunteers on a regular basis to give back to her community.
p1.ex2: The decisions were made on the basis of the council's findings.
p1.example: Rooms were allocated on a first come, first served basis.

p1.en: To arrange in advance to have or use something.
p1.ex1: He booked a brief stay at a hotel near the university campus.
p1.ex2: All rooms must be booked on a first come, first served basis.
p1.example: She booked accommodation for the trip well in advance.

p1.en: Short in time or length.
p1.ex1: Keep your message short and sweet — brief and to the point.
p1.ex2: The meeting was brief, but it fulfilled its objective.
p1.example: She gave a brief but detailed overview of the accommodation options.

p1.en: To increase your knowledge or experience by trying new things.
p1.ex1: She enrolled on the course to broaden her horizons beyond her comfort zone.
p1.ex2: Living on a university campus helps students broaden their horizons.
p1.example: Travelling abroad is a great way to broaden your horizons.

p1.en: A pleasant feeling of being relaxed and free from pain or worry.
p1.ex1: The hotel offered every comfort at a satisfactory price.
p1.ex2: Living within your comfort zone can prevent you from broadening your horizons.
p1.example: She preferred the comfort of her own accommodation to staying on campus.

p1.en: Without stopping or interruption.
p1.ex1: The continuous noise from the construction put her off studying.
p1.ex2: He showed continuous improvement, which fulfilled his teacher's expectations.
p1.example: She made continuous progress toward fulfilling her objective.

p1.en: To communicate or express a meaning, feeling, or message.
p1.ex1: She struggled to convey her regret in a brief email.
p1.ex2: The campaign conveyed its objective clearly and to the point.
p1.example: A short and sweet message often conveys more than a detailed one.

p1.en: Including many facts or small pieces of information.
p1.ex1: The report was detailed and fulfilling to read.
p1.ex2: He preferred detailed instructions rather than vague ones.
p1.example: She gave a detailed account of her stay at the accommodation.

p1.en: Used to say that something sounds easy but is actually difficult to do.
p1.ex1: Booking affordable accommodation on short notice is easier said than done.
p1.ex2: Broadening your horizons sounds great — but it's easier said than done.
p1.example: Fulfilling all expectations is easier said than done.

p1.ru: кто первым пришёл, тот первым обслужен
p1.en: Describes a system where people are helped in the order they arrive.
p1.ex1: Tickets are available on a first come, first served basis — book early.
p1.ex2: She arrived early to ensure she got a room — first come, first served.
p1.example: Accommodation was allocated on a first come, first served basis.

p1.en: To carry out a duty, promise, or requirement completely.
p1.ex1: He fulfilled his potential by broadening his horizons abroad.
p1.ex2: The accommodation failed to fulfil the requirements listed in the brochure.
p1.example: She worked hard to fulfil all the objectives set for her.

p1.en: To give something to a person in authority.
p1.ex1: Please hand in your detailed report by the end of the week.
p1.ex2: He handed in his notice and left the job without regret.
p1.example: She handed in her application for accommodation on time.

p1.en: Regarding a particular aspect of something.
p1.ex1: In terms of cost, the all-inclusive option was more affordable.
p1.ex2: She evaluated the university campus in terms of location and facilities.
p1.example: In terms of comfort, the accommodation was satisfactory.

p1.en: To be as good as expected or hoped.
p1.ex1: He worked continuously to live up to the high expectations set for him.
p1.ex2: The university campus lived up to every expectation she had.
p1.example: The accommodation failed to live up to her expectations.

p1.en: Not anymore; used to say something has stopped.
p1.ex1: The accommodation is no longer available on a first come, first served basis.
p1.ex2: He no longer felt put off by the detailed requirements of the course.
p1.example: She no longer felt regret about her decision to study abroad.

p1.en: A goal or aim that you are working towards.
p1.ex1: The campaign's objective was to broaden awareness of the issue.
p1.ex2: She set clear objectives for her stay at the university campus.
p1.example: Her main objective was to fulfil all course requirements by the deadline.

p1.en: Suddenly and unexpectedly, as if in a single night.
p1.ex1: Success rarely comes overnight — it requires continuous effort.
p1.ex2: The decision to book accommodation was made overnight.
p1.example: Her attitude changed overnight after she decided to broaden her horizons.

p1.en: To make someone lose interest in or enthusiasm for something.
p1.ex1: His continuous complaints put everyone off the idea.
p1.ex2: Don't let one bad experience put you off broadening your horizons.
p1.example: The lack of comfort in the accommodation put her off staying longer.

p1.en: A feeling of sadness or disappointment about something that happened.
p1.ex1: He expressed regret that the accommodation had not lived up to expectations.
p1.ex2: Short and sweet is better than detailed and full of regret.
p1.example: She had no regret about her decision to fulfil her dream of studying abroad.

p1.en: To arrange for something to be kept for your use at a later time.
p1.ex1: He reserved a brief slot to convey his objective to the committee.
p1.ex2: Rooms are reserved on a first come, first served basis.
p1.example: She reserved accommodation at the university campus in advance.

p1.en: Good enough to meet a requirement, but not excellent.
p1.ex1: Her progress was satisfactory but she aimed to fulfil more objectives.
p1.ex2: The detailed report received a satisfactory review from the committee.
p1.example: The accommodation was satisfactory, though it lacked comfort.

p1.en: Brief but effective; saying what is needed without wasting words.
p1.ex1: Her brief speech was short and sweet, but it fulfilled its objective.
p1.ex2: He replied in a short and sweet email that conveyed his regret clearly.
p1.example: Keep your message short and sweet — to the point and easy to convey.

p1.en: Saying only what is necessary and relevant.
p1.ex1: Try to keep your message brief and to the point.
p1.ex2: She conveyed her objective in a short and sweet, to the point summary.
p1.example: Her detailed report was also to the point — nothing unnecessary.

p2.en: Including everything; especially a holiday where all costs are covered.
p2.ex1: In terms of value, the all-inclusive option lived up to her expectations.
p2.ex2: The all-inclusive deal was satisfactory, though it lacked some comforts.
p2.example: She booked an all-inclusive package that covered accommodation and meals.

p2.en: Pleasing in appearance or interesting and appealing.
p2.ex1: She found the all-inclusive offer very attractive in terms of price.
p2.ex2: An attractive accommodation option is one that is both comfortable and affordable.
p2.example: The university campus was attractive and well-maintained.

p2.en: To be going to do something very soon.
p2.ex1: He was about to book the all-inclusive package when he noticed the unattractive reviews.
p2.ex2: They were about to depart when the port was unexpectedly closed.
p2.example: She was about to hand in her accommodation application when she changed her mind.

p2.en: Certain or very likely to happen.
p2.ex1: If you fulfil your objectives continuously, you are bound to succeed.
p2.ex2: An all-inclusive deal is bound to be more satisfactory for first-time travellers.
p2.example: Travelling abroad is bound to broaden your horizons.

p2.en: About to do something at a particular moment.
p2.ex1: He was on the point of handing in his application when he noticed the error.
p2.ex2: They were on the point of departing when the port closed overnight.
p2.example: She was on the point of cancelling her accommodation when the issue was resolved.

p2.en: To leave a place, especially to start a journey.
p2.ex1: She was about to depart when she realised she had left her detailed itinerary behind.
p2.ex2: The group departed on a first come, first served basis.
p2.example: They departed from the port early in the morning.

p2.en: A town or city with a harbour where ships arrive and depart.
p2.ex1: The port was unattractive but functional.
p2.ex2: She reserved accommodation near the port to make departure easier.
p2.example: They arrived at the port just as the ferry was about to depart.

p2.en: A good or bad feature of something.
p2.ex1: She evaluated the positive and negative aspects of the all-inclusive deal.
p2.ex2: One negative aspect of the university campus was the lack of affordable dining.
p2.example: In terms of positive aspects, the accommodation was comfortable and well-located.

p2.en: To try to find or obtain something.
p2.ex1: He sought to fulfil his objective of broadening his horizons abroad.
p2.ex2: Many students seek all-inclusive deals to avoid unexpected costs.
p2.example: She sought affordable accommodation near the university campus.

p2.en: To delay or avoid doing something; or to stop making progress.
p2.ex1: He stalled on booking accommodation, hoping for a more attractive deal.
p2.ex2: Don't stall — suitable accommodation is allocated on a first come, first served basis.
p2.example: She stalled before handing in her application, unsure about her objective.

p2.en: Not pleasing in appearance or not interesting.
p2.ex1: She found the university campus unattractive compared to her expectations.
p2.ex2: The all-inclusive deal seemed unattractive at first but lived up to expectations.
p2.example: The accommodation was unattractive but satisfactory in terms of comfort.

p2.en: The grounds and buildings of a university.
p2.ex1: The university campus was attractive and fulfilling to study on.
p2.ex2: In terms of location, the university campus was to the point — central and accessible.
p2.example: She reserved accommodation on the university campus for her first year.

p2.en: Not right or appropriate for a particular purpose.
p2.ex1: The all-inclusive deal proved unsuitable because it no longer covered transport.
p2.ex2: She found the university campus unsuitable after a brief visit.
p2.example: The accommodation was unsuitable for her needs in terms of comfort.

p2.en: Used to give an overall summary after thinking about all the facts.
p2.ex1: All things considered, the university campus lived up to her expectations.
p2.ex2: All things considered, broadening your horizons is never something you will regret.
p2.example: All things considered, the all-inclusive package was the most satisfactory option.

p2.ru: Что касается меня, по моему мнению...
p2.en: Used to give your personal opinion on something.
p2.ex1: As far as I'm concerned, all-inclusive holidays are bound to be more satisfying.
p2.ex2: As far as I'm concerned, living up to expectations is easier said than done.
p2.example: As far as I'm concerned, short and sweet messages convey more than detailed ones.

p2.en: Used to express your personal perspective.
p2.ex1: From my point of view, the negative aspects outweigh the positive ones.
p2.ex2: From my point of view, seeking all-inclusive accommodation is always worthwhile.
p2.example: From my point of view, the university campus is the most attractive option.

p2.en: Used to suggest moving to the next topic or item in a discussion.
p2.ex1: Shall we move on to the next aspect — positive or negative?
p2.ex2: All things considered, shall we move on to the next objective?
p2.word: Shall we move on to the next...?
p2.example: Shall we move on to the next point? We have covered the accommodation options.

p2.en: Used to confirm that a decision or plan has been agreed.
p2.ex1: So we're settled, then. She will hand in the application by Friday.
p2.ex2: All things considered, so we're settled, then — first come, first served.
p2.example: So we're settled, then — we book the all-inclusive accommodation.

p2.en: Used to give your personal view or interpretation of something.
p2.ex1: The way I see it, the positive aspects of the all-inclusive deal outweigh the negative.
p2.ex2: The way I see it, fulfilling your objectives overnight is easier said than done.
p2.example: The way I see it, broadening your horizons is never unsuitable.

p2.ru: Вы правы, в этом есть смысл.
p2.en: Used to agree that someone's argument is valid or correct.
p2.ex1: You have a point there. The accommodation was unattractive but satisfactory.
p2.ex2: You have a point there — seeking comfort is not always bound to be affordable.
p2.example: You have a point there — the all-inclusive option does live up to expectations.

p1.en: To change your behaviour or approach to suit a new situation.
p1.ex1: Travelling solo helps you adapt to unexpected challenges.
p1.ex2: He adapted his comfort zone by going on an independent expedition.
p1.example: She had to adapt quickly to life in the middle of nowhere.

p1.en: To have a particular goal or intention.
p1.ex1: He aimed to get across his message about the vibrant local culture.
p1.ex2: The expedition aimed to demonstrate that independent travel is possible anywhere.
p1.example: She aimed to soak up every experience during her solo expedition.

p1.en: Recognition of the value or quality of something.
p1.ex1: She expressed her appreciation for the locals who helped her.
p1.ex2: Living in the middle of nowhere gave her a deep appreciation for simplicity.
p1.example: Solo travel deepens your appreciation for different cultures and landmarks.

p1.en: Something that prevents progress or communication.
p1.ex1: Stepping out of your comfort zone helps break down intimidating barriers.
p1.ex2: Consequently, the barrier between locals and travellers was simply one of language.
p1.example: Language was the main barrier she encountered on her solo expedition.

p1.en: To be completely certain about something.
p1.ex1: He was in no doubt that solo travel was out of the ordinary.
p1.ex2: Be in no doubt — soaking up a vibrant culture changes you deeply.
p1.example: She was in no doubt that the expedition would define her decade.

p1.en: Full of busy, noisy activity.
p1.ex1: The bustling market on the outskirts of the town was vibrant and colourful.
