p1.ex2: After a decade in a bustling city, she craved something out of the ordinary.
p1.example: She left her bustling city for a cabin in the middle of nowhere.

p1.en: A small simple shelter or house; or a room on a ship or plane.
p1.ex1: The cabin was within walking distance of a dramatic landmark.
p1.ex2: She was simply grateful for the cabin after days in the middle of nowhere.
p1.example: He spent the first night of his expedition in a remote cabin.

p1.en: Having the ability or skill to do something.
p1.ex1: He demonstrated he was capable of adapting to life on the outskirts.
p1.ex2: Consequently, she was in no doubt she was capable of anything.
p1.example: She proved she was capable of completing a solo expedition.

p1.en: The range of situations where you feel safe and at ease.
p1.ex1: Stepping out of your comfort zone defines who you truly are.
p1.ex2: He had never left his comfort zone — the bustling city felt endless.
p1.example: Travelling solo forced her out of her comfort zone in the best way.

p1.en: As a result; therefore.
p1.ex1: He left his comfort zone; consequently, his appreciation for life deepened.
p1.ex2: They were on the outskirts of town; consequently, the landmark was within walking distance.
p1.example: She encountered a language barrier; consequently, she had to adapt quickly.

p1.en: A period of ten years.
p1.ex1: In the last decade, independent travel has become far more accessible.
p1.ex2: A decade of bustling city life made her crave something out of the ordinary.
p1.example: She had spent a decade in her comfort zone before her solo expedition.

p1.en: Very much; in a thorough or intense way.
p1.ex1: She was deeply moved by the vibrant culture of the locals.
p1.ex2: He was deeply in no doubt that the solo journey had defined his decade.
p1.example: The expedition deeply changed her appreciation for the world.

p1.en: To describe or explain the meaning of something; or to give shape to something.
p1.ex1: Her encounter with locals deeply defined her appreciation for independence.
p1.ex2: She aimed to define herself outside her comfort zone.
p1.example: The solo expedition would define her decade as a traveller.

p1.en: To show or prove something clearly.
p1.ex1: He demonstrated his appreciation by helping the locals in return.
p1.ex2: The vibrant culture of the inhabitants demonstrated something out of the ordinary.
p1.example: She aimed to demonstrate that a solo expedition was not intimidating.

p1.en: Striking, exciting, or impressive.
p1.ex1: She encountered a dramatic landmark in the middle of nowhere.
p1.ex2: The view from the outskirts was dramatic — endless and vibrant.
p1.example: The landscape around the cabin was dramatic and deeply inspiring.

p1.en: To meet or experience something, especially unexpectedly.
p1.ex1: He encountered locals who helped him get across the message.
p1.ex2: On the outskirts of the town, they encountered a dramatic landmark.
p1.example: She encountered a language barrier that was initially intimidating.

p1.en: Having no end or limit; continuing for a very long time.
p1.ex1: She had endless appreciation for the vibrant culture she soaked up.
p1.ex2: He was deeply inspired by the endless dramatic landscape around the cabin.
p1.example: The expedition felt endless as they crossed the middle of nowhere.

p1.en: A journey made for a particular purpose, often to a remote place.
p1.ex1: The expedition took them to a landmark in the middle of nowhere.
p1.ex2: He demonstrated he was capable of leading an independent expedition.
p1.example: She set off on a solo expedition that would define her decade.

p1.en: To communicate an idea or message successfully.
p1.ex1: He aimed to get across the message that solo travel is not intimidating.
p1.ex2: Consequently, she found it hard to get across simple requests in a foreign language.
p1.example: She struggled to get across her appreciation to the locals.

p1.en: To move in a particular direction.
p1.ex1: She headed for the cabin in the middle of nowhere after a bustling week.
p1.ex2: He headed out solo, deeply determined to broaden his horizons.
p1.example: They headed toward the landmark on the outskirts of the town.

p1.en: Far from any town or city; in a very remote place.
p1.ex1: She encountered a local in the middle of nowhere who showed her the landmark.
p1.ex2: He was in no doubt he was in the middle of nowhere when he left the outskirts.
p1.example: The cabin was in the middle of nowhere — dramatic and deeply peaceful.

p1.en: Not relying on others; able to do things for yourself.
p1.ex1: She was deeply proud of her independent approach to the expedition.
p1.ex2: An independent traveller soaks up culture in a way that defines the experience.
p1.example: Solo travel made her more independent and capable.

p1.en: A person or animal that lives in a particular place.
p1.ex1: She soaked up the culture by spending time with local inhabitants.
p1.ex2: Consequently, the inhabitants on the outskirts had a deeply unique way of life.
p1.example: The inhabitants of the remote village were vibrant and welcoming.

p1.en: Making you feel nervous or frightened.
p1.ex1: She was in no doubt that the language barrier would be intimidating.
p1.ex2: Stepping out of your comfort zone can feel intimidating but is deeply rewarding.
p1.example: The idea of a solo expedition was intimidating at first.

p1.en: A recognisable feature of a landscape; or an important building or place.
p1.ex1: She soaked up the history of every landmark on her expedition.
p1.ex2: He headed toward the landmark in the middle of nowhere as the sun set.
p1.example: The dramatic landmark was visible from within walking distance of the cabin.

p1.en: A person who lives in a particular area.
p1.ex1: She soaked up the vibrant culture by talking to locals.
p1.ex2: He demonstrated his appreciation to the locals who guided his expedition.
p1.example: A local helped her navigate the outskirts of the bustling town.

p1.en: When you reach a place.
p1.ex1: On arrival at the landmark, they were in no doubt it was out of the ordinary.
p1.ex2: He soaked up the vibrant atmosphere immediately on arrival.
p1.example: On arrival, she headed straight for the cabin in the middle of nowhere.

p1.en: In the outer areas of a town or city, away from the centre.
p1.ex1: She encountered an intimidating barrier on the outskirts of the village.
p1.ex2: Consequently, the landmark on the outskirts was within walking distance.
p1.example: The cabin was on the outskirts of the bustling town.

p1.en: Unusual or different from what is normal.
p1.ex1: Every encounter with local inhabitants was out of the ordinary.
p1.ex2: She was in no doubt that life in the middle of nowhere was out of the ordinary.
p1.example: The solo expedition was deeply out of the ordinary — and she loved it.

p1.en: A part of something larger; or a single item.
p1.ex1: She soaked up every piece of vibrant culture she encountered.
p1.ex2: The cabin was simply a piece of the dramatic landscape she explored.
p1.example: Each encounter was a piece of her expedition that defined her decade.

p1.en: Used to emphasise how easy or basic something is; or just.
p1.ex1: He was simply capable of adapting to life in the middle of nowhere.
p1.ex2: It was simply out of the ordinary — a deeply vibrant encounter.
p1.example: She was simply in no doubt that the expedition would define her.

p1.en: To absorb or enjoy something fully.
p1.ex1: He aimed to soak up the endless dramatic landscape on his expedition.
p1.ex2: On arrival, she simply soaked up the atmosphere of the bustling market.
p1.example: She soaked up the vibrant culture of every local inhabitant she met.

p1.en: Done alone, without others.
p1.ex1: Travelling solo is intimidating at first but deeply rewarding.
p1.ex2: He headed solo into the middle of nowhere with nothing but a cabin address.
p1.example: She set off on a solo expedition to define her decade.

p1.en: In a way that is not known or certain.
p1.ex1: He somehow ended up in the middle of nowhere after leaving the outskirts.
p1.ex2: Somehow, the solo expedition was less intimidating than she had expected.
p1.example: Somehow, she managed to get across her message despite the language barrier.

p1.en: Done without planning; happening naturally.
p1.ex1: She was deeply spontaneous — heading solo into the middle of nowhere.
p1.ex2: A spontaneous decision to leave her comfort zone defined her decade.
p1.example: The most memorable encounters on the expedition were completely spontaneous.

p1.en: To try hard to do something difficult.
p1.ex1: He struggled to adapt to life in the middle of nowhere.
p1.ex2: Consequently, she struggled but demonstrated she was capable of adapting.
p1.example: She struggled to get across basic requests without the local language.

p1.en: A large amount of something (informal).
p1.ex1: There were tons of out of the ordinary encounters on the solo trip.
p1.ex2: He soaked up tons of vibrant culture in just a decade of travel.
p1.example: She had tons of appreciation for the locals who helped her expedition.

p1.en: Full of energy and life.
p1.ex1: She soaked up the vibrant culture of every local community she visited.
p1.ex2: On arrival, the outskirts came to life with vibrant, spontaneous activity.
p1.example: The bustling market was vibrant and deeply inspiring.

p1.en: Close enough to reach on foot.
p1.ex1: She was deeply pleased that the market was within walking distance.
p1.ex2: On the outskirts, tons of local landmarks were within walking distance.
p1.example: The dramatic landmark was within walking distance of the cabin.

p1.en: Used to explain or restate something more clearly.
p1.ex1: In other words, she was simply in no doubt about her solo expedition.
p1.ex2: In other words, the vibrant encounter was deeply out of the ordinary.
p1.example: In other words, stepping out of your comfort zone defines your decade.

p2.en: To go somewhere with someone.
p2.ex1: He accompanied his family on a scenic excursion to ancient ruins.
p2.ex2: A detailed itinerary accompanied them throughout the voyage.
p2.example: She was accompanied by a local guide to the archaeological site.

p2.en: The remains of very old buildings or structures.
p2.ex1: She postponed her excursion to the ancient ruins due to jet lag.
p2.ex2: The ancient ruins were a must-see on every scenic route in the region.
p2.example: The highlight of the itinerary was visiting the ancient ruins.

p2.en: A place where objects or structures from the past are excavated and studied.
p2.ex1: She accompanied the researcher to the archaeological site on the outskirts.
p2.ex2: Jet lag made it hard to fully appreciate the archaeological site on arrival.
p2.example: The excursion to the archaeological site was the highlight of the voyage.

p2.en: A society that has developed organised culture, government, and technology.
p2.ex1: She soaked up the history of every civilisation she encountered on the route.
p2.ex2: The must-see monument was a symbol of the region's ancient civilisation.
p2.example: The ancient ruins gave a glimpse into a long-lost civilisation.

p2.en: A short trip, usually for pleasure or education.
p2.ex1: She called off the excursion to the archaeological site due to bad weather.
p2.ex2: The itinerary included a must-see excursion to a historic monument.
p2.example: The highlight of her trip was the scenic excursion to the ancient ruins.

p2.en: The most interesting or enjoyable part of something.
p2.ex1: She dropped off her luggage and headed straight for the highlight of the itinerary.
p2.ex2: The must-see monument was, without doubt, the highlight of the route.
p2.example: The highlight of the voyage was visiting the ancient civilisation's ruins.

p2.en: A planned route or schedule for a journey.
p2.ex1: The itinerary included stops at ancient ruins and a scenic archaeological site.
p2.ex2: He called off one excursion and replaced it with a must-see monument.
p2.example: She put off finalising the itinerary until she had recovered from jet lag.

p2.en: Tiredness and disorientation caused by travelling across time zones.
p2.ex1: Jet lag made it hard to fully appreciate the highlight of the itinerary.
p2.ex2: He stopped over to recover from jet lag before heading to the archaeological site.
p2.example: She suffered from jet lag and postponed her first excursion.

p2.en: A structure built to remember a person or event.
p2.ex1: She accompanied a guide to the monument on the outskirts of the city.
p2.ex2: The monument was the highlight of the itinerary and drew tons of visitors.
p2.example: The ancient monument was a must-see on every scenic route.

p2.en: Something that is so good or interesting that you should experience it.
p2.ex1: Every itinerary should include at least one must-see archaeological site.
p2.ex2: She called the monument a must-see and accompanied her friend on the excursion.
p2.example: The ancient ruins were a must-see that she had put off for years.

p2.en: Visually attractive, especially in a quaint or charming way.
p2.ex1: She soaked up the picturesque scenery on the scenic excursion.
p2.ex2: The itinerary took them through a picturesque landscape of monuments and ruins.
p2.example: The route passed through a picturesque village near ancient ruins.

p2.en: To arrange for something to happen at a later time than planned.
p2.ex1: He put off the voyage and eventually postponed it by a full week.
p2.ex2: The highlight of the itinerary was postponed due to bad weather.
p2.example: She postponed the excursion to the archaeological site due to jet lag.

p2.en: The path or direction taken to get from one place to another.
p2.ex1: She accompanied a local guide who knew the best route to the archaeological site.
p2.ex2: He called off one route and replaced it with a more picturesque alternative.
p2.example: The scenic route passed by ancient ruins and a must-see monument.

p2.en: Relating to the countryside rather than a town or city.
p2.ex1: She soaked up the rural atmosphere far from the bustling city.
p2.ex2: The archaeological site was in a rural area, within walking distance of the cabin.
p2.example: The excursion took them through a picturesque rural landscape.

p2.en: Having beautiful natural scenery.
p2.ex1: She accompanied the group on a scenic excursion along the coastline.
p2.ex2: Jet lag aside, she soaked up every moment of the scenic voyage.
p2.example: The scenic route through the rural landscape was the highlight of the itinerary.

p2.en: To experience pain, illness, or a difficult situation.
p2.ex1: He suffered from the intimidating language barrier throughout the excursion.
p2.ex2: Many travellers suffer from anxiety when visiting a must-see site alone.
p2.example: She suffered from jet lag for the first two days of the voyage.

p2.en: Being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else.
p2.ex1: Every archaeological site on the route offered a unique perspective.
p2.ex2: The highlight of the voyage was a unique excursion to ancient ruins.
p2.example: The ancient civilisation had a unique and deeply picturesque culture.

p2.en: A long journey, especially by sea or in space.
p2.ex1: She put off the voyage until she had finalised the itinerary.
p2.ex2: The highlight of the voyage was an excursion to a must-see archaeological site.
p2.example: The scenic voyage along the coast included stops at ancient ruins.

p2.en: To cancel something that was planned.
p2.ex1: He called off the scenic route and chose a more direct one.
p2.ex2: The must-see monument visit was called off when the weather turned.
p2.example: She called off the excursion to the archaeological site due to jet lag.

p2.en: To take someone to a place and leave them there.
p2.ex1: He dropped off the group at the archaeological site and headed back.
p2.ex2: She was dropped off within walking distance of the must-see monument.
p2.example: The guide dropped her off near the ancient ruins.

p2.en: To leave a place or escape from a routine.
p2.ex1: He got away for a week and soaked up the scenic rural landscape.
p2.ex2: Getting away from your comfort zone can define your decade.
p2.example: She finally got away from her bustling life and set off on a solo voyage.

p2.en: To move in the direction of somewhere.
p2.ex1: She headed for the must-see monument at the start of the itinerary.
p2.ex2: He headed for the archaeological site accompanied by a local guide.
p2.example: They headed for the ancient ruins as soon as jet lag passed.

p2.en: To provide someone with a place to stay.
p2.ex1: He put up his travelling companion near the archaeological site.
p2.ex2: She was grateful to be put up by locals during her solo voyage.
p2.example: A local put her up for the night when the cabin was fully booked.

p2.en: To delay doing something.
p2.ex1: He kept putting off the voyage, but eventually he set off solo.
p2.ex2: Don't put off a must-see excursion — you may not get another chance.
p2.example: She put off the excursion to the ancient ruins until her jet lag passed.

p2.en: To go to the place where someone is leaving from to say goodbye.
p2.ex1: He saw off his travelling companion at the airport.
p2.ex2: She was seen off by locals who had put her up during the excursion.
p2.example: Her family saw her off at the port before the voyage.

p2.en: To stay somewhere for a short time during a longer journey.
p2.ex1: They stopped over near the ancient ruins before heading for the coast.
p2.ex2: He stopped over at a must-see archaeological site on the route.
p2.example: She stopped over in a picturesque rural town to recover from jet lag.

p3.en: A seat next to the walkway in a plane, train, or theatre.
p3.ex1: He preferred an aisle seat to avoid climbing over other passengers.
p3.ex2: On arrival at the departure gate, she confirmed her aisle seat booking.
p3.example: She always books an aisle seat to stretch her legs on long voyages.

p3.en: To recognise the value or quality of something.
p3.ex1: He appreciated the first-hand experience of visiting ancient ruins.
p3.ex2: Travelling independently helps you appreciate diversity and culture.
p3.example: She deeply appreciated the authentic cuisine she encountered on the route.

p3.en: An object made by humans, especially one of historical interest.
p3.ex1: The museum preserved artefacts from an ancient civilisation.
p3.ex2: Each artefact represented a unique era of the region's history.
p3.example: She photographed every artefact on display at the archaeological site.

p3.en: Real, genuine, and not a copy or imitation.
p3.ex1: The artefacts on display were authentic and from an ancient era.
p3.ex2: He appreciated the authentic narrative the local guide conveyed.
p3.example: She soaked up the authentic culture and cuisine on her solo voyage.

p3.en: A document that allows you to board a plane.
p3.ex1: He lost his boarding pass and had to request a replacement.
p3.ex2: The boarding pass confirmed her aisle seat for the long-haul voyage.
p3.example: She checked her boarding pass at the departure gate.

p3.en: Money you pay if you cancel a booking.
p3.ex1: The cancellation fee was higher than expected, so she kept her booking.
p3.ex2: He decided to stop over rather than cancel and pay the cancellation fee.
p3.example: She put off cancelling her excursion to avoid the cancellation fee.

p3.en: A style of cooking associated with a particular country or region.
p3.ex1: The highlight of the excursion was trying the unique regional cuisine.
p3.ex2: He appreciated the diversity of cuisine he encountered on the voyage.
p3.example: She soaked up the authentic local cuisine on every stop of the route.

p3.en: A traditional way of behaving in a particular society.
p3.ex1: Learning about customs first-hand deepens your appreciation of a civilisation.
p3.ex2: Each era of the ancient civilisation had its own unique customs on display.
p3.example: She respected every local custom she encountered on her solo voyage.

p3.en: The area in an airport where passengers board their plane.
p3.ex1: He checked the overhead compartment and sat in his aisle seat at the departure gate.
p3.ex2: The cancellation fee notice was posted at the departure gate.
p3.example: She arrived at the departure gate just in time with her boarding pass.

p3.en: A range of different things, people, or ideas.
p3.ex1: The archaeological site represented the diversity of an ancient civilisation.
p3.ex2: Travelling independently exposes you to the diversity of global culture.
p3.example: She appreciated the diversity of cuisine and customs on the voyage.

p3.en: To give special importance to something.
p3.ex1: She emphasised the need to respect local customs on every excursion.
p3.ex2: He emphasised that the boarding pass must be checked at the departure gate.
p3.example: The guide emphasised the significance of each artefact on display.

p3.en: A long and distinct period of history.
p3.ex1: The ancient ruins dated back to an era of remarkable cultural diversity.
p3.ex2: She soaked up knowledge of each era during the archaeological site visit.
p3.example: Each artefact on display represented a different era of the civilisation.

p3.en: To include or have as an important part.
p3.ex1: The museum featured artefacts from every era of the ancient civilisation.
p3.ex2: The route featured scenic geographical features and a picturesque rural landscape.
p3.example: The itinerary featured a must-see excursion to an archaeological site.

p3.en: Experienced or learned directly, not from someone else.
p3.ex1: He got first-hand experience of the ancient era at the archaeological site.
p3.ex2: First-hand encounters with diversity define a truly authentic voyage.
p3.example: She gained a first-hand appreciation of local customs on the voyage.

p3.en: A cart pushed down a plane aisle to serve food and drinks.
p3.ex1: He was in his aisle seat when the food trolley came past.
p3.ex2: The food trolley featured a selection of cuisine from the destination country.
p3.example: She bought authentic snacks from the food trolley during the flight.

p3.en: A natural physical characteristic of a place, such as a mountain or river.
p3.ex1: She photographed each geographical feature from her aisle seat window.
p3.ex2: The itinerary featured geographical features alongside ancient ruins.
p3.example: The scenic route highlighted every major geographical feature of the region.

p3.en: Without help from others; on your own.
p3.ex1: He explored the archaeological site independently, without a guide.
p3.ex2: Travelling independently deepens your first-hand appreciation of diversity.
p3.example: She travelled independently and soaked up every authentic experience.

p3.en: Existing or happening at the beginning.
p3.ex1: Despite initial jet lag, she soaked up every must-see on the itinerary.
p3.ex2: The initial excursion featured an authentic encounter with local customs.
p3.example: Her initial reaction to the ancient ruins was one of deep appreciation.

p3.en: Continuing for the whole of your life.
p3.ex1: He developed a lifelong passion for visiting archaeological sites.
p3.ex2: First-hand encounters with diverse civilisations create lifelong memories.
p3.example: The solo voyage gave her a lifelong appreciation for authentic travel.

p3.en: A spoken or written account of events; a story.
p3.ex1: She soaked up the authentic narrative behind every artefact on display.
p3.ex2: The itinerary featured a narrative connecting each geographical feature.
p3.example: The local guide conveyed a rich narrative about each era of the civilisation.

p3.en: A country or the people of a country considered as a group.
p3.ex1: She appreciated the diversity of every nation she visited on the voyage.
p3.ex2: The artefacts on display represented the heritage of an ancient nation.
p3.example: Each nation on the route had unique customs and authentic cuisine.

p3.en: Being shown to the public.
p3.ex1: The must-see monument had authentic sculptures on display.
p3.ex2: She soaked up every piece of history on display at the archaeological site.
p3.example: Artefacts from every era of the civilisation were on display at the site.

p3.en: Not a copy; existing since the beginning.
p3.ex1: She appreciated the original narrative conveyed by the local guide.
p3.ex2: The original geographical feature had been preserved for centuries.
p3.example: The museum preserved the original artefacts from the ancient era.

p3.en: The storage space above seats on a plane.
p3.ex1: He checked the overhead compartment before sitting down at the departure gate.
p3.ex2: The boarding pass confirmed both the aisle seat and overhead compartment access.
p3.example: She placed her bag in the overhead compartment and took her aisle seat.

p3.en: A device worn over the nose and mouth to supply oxygen, used in planes during emergencies.
p3.ex1: She had never needed an oxygen mask on any of her voyages.
p3.ex2: In case of emergency, the oxygen mask drops from the overhead compartment.
p3.example: The flight attendant demonstrated how to use the oxygen mask.

p3.en: To keep something in its original state or protect it from harm.
p3.ex1: She emphasised the importance of preserving authentic customs and traditions.
p3.ex2: Every era of the nation's history had been carefully preserved on display.
p3.example: The site worked to preserve artefacts from the ancient civilisation.

p3.en: Most important; first in order.
p3.ex1: The primary highlight of the itinerary was the archaeological site.
p3.ex2: She emphasised that diversity was the primary feature of the authentic route.
p3.example: Her primary objective was to soak up first-hand experiences on the voyage.

p3.en: To be a symbol of something; or to act on behalf of someone.
p3.ex1: The monument represented the nation's ancient cultural heritage.
p3.ex2: She appreciated how the local customs represented the authentic identity of the region.
p3.example: Each artefact on display represented a unique era of the civilisation.

p3.en: Something that is necessary or obligatory.
p3.ex1: She checked all requirements before booking her aisle seat.
p3.ex2: The itinerary listed every requirement for visiting the archaeological site.
p3.example: A valid boarding pass is a requirement at every departure gate.

p3.en: A three-dimensional work of art, usually made from stone, metal, or wood.
p3.ex1: She appreciated the authentic detail of each sculpture at the archaeological site.
p3.ex2: The sculpture represented a key figure from the nation's ancient civilisation.
p3.example: The ancient ruins featured sculptures on display from every era.

p3.en: A substance used to flavour food, often with a strong taste or smell.
p3.ex1: Every nation on the route had its own unique combination of spice and custom.
p3.ex2: The food trolley featured dishes with authentic local spice and cuisine.
p3.example: She soaked up the authentic cuisine, rich with local spice and flavour.

p3.en: A small fold-down table attached to the seat in front on a plane.
p3.ex1: He placed his food from the food trolley on the tray table.
p3.ex2: The boarding pass and itinerary were both on the tray table at departure.
p3.example: She unfolded the tray table and checked her itinerary during the flight.

p3.en: Below or beneath something.
p3.ex1: The oxygen mask is located underneath the overhead compartment panel.
p3.ex2: Underneath the ancient ruins, archaeologists found authentic artefacts.
p3.example: She stored her bag underneath the seat in front of her aisle seat.

p4.en: To give reasons for or against something; to have a disagreement.
p4.ex1: He argued that the cancellation fee was a consequence of poor planning.
p4.ex2: It is widely known that travellers argue about the nature of solo versus guided tours.
p4.example: She argued that authentic travel outweighs the frustrating drawbacks.

p4.en: In a genuine and real way.
p4.ex1: He authentically represented the customs of his nation to visitors.
p4.ex2: Travelling authentically means engaging first-hand with diversity.
p4.example: She experienced the local culture authentically, without a guided tour.

p4.en: A heavy load; or something difficult to deal with.
p4.ex1: She argued that the cancellation fee was an unfair burden on travellers.
p4.ex2: The frustrating requirement became an unnecessary burden on the itinerary.
p4.example: Jet lag can be a real burden on a long voyage.

p4.en: To state something as a fact without full proof.
p4.ex1: He claimed that onboard cuisine was not authentically representative.
p4.ex2: It is a well-known fact that travellers claim first-hand experience is irreplaceable.
p4.example: She claimed that the drawbacks of solo travel outweigh the benefits.

p4.en: A result or effect of an action or condition.
p4.ex1: She argued that the cancellation fee was a consequence of poor planning.
p4.ex2: Thus, the consequence of ignoring local customs can be deeply uncomfortable.
p4.example: Jet lag was a frustrating consequence of the long-haul voyage.

p4.en: A disadvantage or problem with something.
p4.ex1: She argued that the frustrating cancellation fee was a major drawback.
p4.ex2: Onboard delays are a common drawback that outweighs minor inconveniences.
p4.example: The main drawback of solo travel is that it can be intimidating.

p4.en: Causing annoyance or disappointment because of obstacles.
p4.ex1: It was frustrating when the cancellation fee outweighed the cost of rebooking.
p4.ex2: She claimed the onboard delays were the most frustrating drawback of the voyage.
p4.example: Jet lag made the initial excursion frustrating rather than fulfilling.

p4.en: More than one; many.
p4.ex1: Multiple artefacts on display represented different eras of the civilisation.
p4.ex2: He made multiple claims about the frustrating nature of the cancellation fee.
p4.example: She encountered multiple drawbacks on the voyage but soaked up every highlight.

p4.en: The basic quality or character of something.
p4.ex1: She argued that the nature of solo voyages outweighs guided tours.
p4.ex2: Thus, the nature of the consequence was frustrating but not unexpected.
p4.example: The nature of authentic travel means embracing frustrating drawbacks.

p4.en: On a ship, plane, or other vehicle.
p4.ex1: She found her boarding pass and headed to the departure gate for the onboard experience.
p4.ex2: Multiple onboard services made the frustrating voyage more satisfactory.
p4.example: The onboard cuisine was not authentically representative of the destination.

p4.en: In a different way; or if not.
p4.ex1: She checked the itinerary; otherwise, the departure gate would have been missed.
p4.ex2: Pay the cancellation fee now; otherwise, the consequence will be worse.
p4.example: Book your aisle seat early; otherwise, you may be left with an unsuitable option.

p4.en: To be greater or more important than something else.
p4.ex1: The frustrating cancellation fee was outweighed by the authentic experience.
p4.ex2: It is a well-known fact that the benefits of travel outweigh the burdens.
p4.example: She argued that the highlights of a voyage outweigh the drawbacks.

p4.en: A greater liking for one thing over another.
p4.ex1: He expressed a preference for independent travel over guided excursions.
p4.ex2: Multiple travellers share a preference for routes that feature must-see landmarks.
p4.example: Her preference was an aisle seat and an authentic onboard cuisine option.

p4.en: Nausea caused by the motion of a boat or ship.
p4.ex1: She suffered from seasickness but argued the highlight outweighed the burden.
p4.ex2: Consequently, seasickness led her to claim the voyage was not worth the cancellation fee.
p4.example: Seasickness was a frustrating drawback of the scenic coastal voyage.

p4.en: To consider something when making a decision.
p4.ex1: He took jet lag into account when planning the initial itinerary.
p4.ex2: Thus, multiple drawbacks must be taken into account before booking a solo voyage.
p4.example: She took the cancellation fee into account before postponing the excursion.

p4.en: As a consequence; therefore.
p4.ex1: She claimed the cancellation fee was avoidable; thus, the drawback was minor.
p4.ex2: Thus, the nature of the voyage outweighed every frustrating consequence.
p4.example: The onboard delay was frustrating; thus, the itinerary had to be adjusted.

p4.en: Used to introduce something widely accepted as true.
p4.ex1: It is a well-known fact that jet lag outweighs most onboard drawbacks.
p4.ex2: It is a well-known fact that first-hand experience is irreplaceable.
p4.word: It is a well-known fact that...
p4.example: It is a well-known fact that authentic travel broadens your horizons.

p4.en: Used to state something that many people accept as true.
p4.ex1: It is widely known that the nature of authentic voyages outweighs the burden of planning.
p4.ex2: It is widely known that multiple drawbacks can be outweighed by a single highlight.
p4.example: It is widely known that solo travel builds independence and appreciation.

p1.en: The act of obtaining or buying something.
p1.ex1: He justified every acquisition by reviewing its value for money.
p1.ex2: Unnecessary acquisition of material goods is a hallmark of consumerist culture.
p1.example: Her latest acquisition was a minimalist outfit from a charity shop.

p1.en: A person who buys and uses goods or services.
p1.ex1: Eye-catching packaging is designed to attract the consumer's attention.
p1.ex2: A minimalist consumer makes the most of what they already own.
p1.example: Consumers are becoming more reluctant to overspend on material possessions.

p1.en: Relating to or promoting the buying of goods as a priority.
p1.ex1: Widespread consumerist culture encourages people to overspend on fake goods.
p1.ex2: Indeed, a consumerist society turns a blind eye to the impact on natural resources.
p1.example: She tried to move away from her consumerist lifestyle and embrace minimalism.

p1.en: The use or purchase of goods and resources.
p1.ex1: She kept a record of her consumption to keep within her budget.
p1.ex2: It goes without saying that reducing consumption makes economic sense.
p1.example: Widespread consumption of material goods puts pressure on natural resources.

p1.en: A statement that explains the meaning of a word or concept.
p1.ex1: The definition of good value for money depends on your priorities.
p1.ex2: She reviewed the definition of consumerist culture for her survey.
p1.example: By definition, a minimalist avoids unnecessary material possessions.

p1.en: To get rid of something or stop using it.
p1.ex1: Many minimalists do away with consumerist habits to embrace simpler living.
p1.ex2: It makes sense to do away with fake goods and stick to reliable brands.
p1.example: She decided to do away with material possessions that added no value.

p1.en: Using no more money or resources than necessary.
p1.ex1: Buying from a charity shop is a more economical alternative to high-street stores.
p1.ex2: An economical approach to consumption helps preserve natural resources.
p1.example: She was economical with her expenses by keeping within a budget.

p1.en: To accept something enthusiastically.
p1.ex1: He was reluctant at first but eventually embraced the minimalist lifestyle.
p1.ex2: Indeed, embracing economical habits makes the most of your expenses.
p1.example: She decided to embrace minimalism and do away with material possessions.

p1.en: The feeling of pleasure from doing something.
p1.ex1: He reviewed his priorities and found enjoyment in experiences over possessions.
p1.ex2: Indeed, enjoyment does not require widespread consumption or overspending.
p1.example: She found genuine enjoyment in making the most of simple material goods.

p1.en: Money spent on something.
p1.ex1: He was reluctant to review his expenses, fearing he had overspent.
p1.ex2: Cutting down on unnecessary expenses makes economic sense.
p1.example: She kept a record of all her expenses to keep within her budget.

p1.en: Immediately noticeable and attractive.
p1.ex1: She ignored the eye-catching display and stuck to her budget.
p1.ex2: Indeed, eye-catching advertising targets consumerist habits.
p1.example: Eye-catching packaging often persuades hesitant consumers to make a purchase.

p1.en: Not genuine; a copy or imitation.
p1.ex1: He turned a blind eye to the fake label and made the acquisition anyway.
p1.ex2: It goes without saying that fake material goods lack reliability.
p1.example: She was reluctant to buy from the market after discovering fake goods.

p1.en: Slow to act or speak because of uncertainty or nervousness.
p1.ex1: He was hesitant to review his expenses after overspending on material goods.
p1.ex2: Consumers are often hesitant when faced with too wide a selection.
p1.example: She was hesitant to embrace minimalism but eventually found enjoyment in it.

p1.en: To pay no attention to something.
p1.ex1: He turned a blind eye to the issue, effectively ignoring it.
p1.ex2: It makes sense not to ignore widespread consumerist habits in your review.
p1.example: She ignored the eye-catching display and stuck to her budget.

p1.en: Used to emphasise something or confirm it is true.
p1.ex1: She was indeed reluctant to overspend, unlike her consumerist friends.
p1.ex2: Indeed, keeping a record of expenses makes the most of your budget.
p1.example: Indeed, it goes without saying that minimalism improves well-being.

p1.en: To write down information so you can refer to it later.
p1.ex1: He kept a record of every acquisition to review later.
p1.ex2: Keeping a record helps you keep within a budget and make sense of your spending.
p1.example: She kept a record of all her expenses to avoid overspending.

p1.en: To avoid spending more money than you have planned.
p1.ex1: He reviewed his expenses weekly to keep within his budget.
p1.ex2: It goes without saying that keeping within a budget requires priorities.
p1.example: She found enjoyment in keeping within a budget rather than overspending.

p1.en: To be logical or easy to understand.
p1.ex1: She reviewed her priorities — embracing minimalism made sense to her.
p1.ex2: Indeed, keeping a record of consumption makes sense for any consumer.
p1.example: It makes sense to do away with material possessions you never use.

p1.en: To use or enjoy something as fully as possible.
p1.ex1: He made the most of his material possessions rather than seeking new acquisitions.
p1.ex2: It goes without saying that a minimalist makes the most of what they already own.
p1.example: She made the most of her budget by shopping at charity shops.

p1.en: Physical objects that can be bought and owned.
p1.ex1: A consumerist society places too much priority on material goods.
p1.ex2: Indeed, material goods rarely bring long-term enjoyment.
p1.example: She chose to do away with unnecessary material goods.

p1.en: Physical things that a person owns.
p1.ex1: He kept a record of his material possessions and donated the surplus.
p1.ex2: Widespread consumerist culture encourages people to value material possessions over experiences.
p1.example: She embraced minimalism by reducing her material possessions.

p1.en: A person who lives with as few possessions as possible; relating to this lifestyle.
p1.ex1: He reviewed his lifestyle and embraced a more minimalist approach.
p1.ex2: A minimalist consumer ignores eye-catching displays and sticks to essentials.
p1.example: As a minimalist, she made the most of a small selection of material goods.

p1.en: Materials found in nature that are used by people, such as water, coal, or wood.
p1.ex1: It goes without saying that production of material goods depletes natural resources.
p1.ex2: A minimalist lifestyle reduces the strain on natural resources.
p1.example: Widespread consumption turns a blind eye to the depletion of natural resources.

p1.en: A set of clothes worn together.
p1.ex1: He reviewed his wardrobe and donated every outfit he never wore.
p1.ex2: A minimalist owns a small selection of outfits and makes the most of each one.
p1.example: She found a stylish outfit at a charity shop without overspending.

p1.en: To spend more money than you planned or can afford.
p1.ex1: He overspent on fake goods and later regretted the acquisition.
p1.ex2: Keeping a record of expenses helps prevent overspending.
p1.example: She was reluctant to overspend on material possessions she didn't need.

p1.en: Something considered more important than other things.
p1.ex1: He reviewed his priorities and decided to embrace a minimalist lifestyle.
p1.ex2: It goes without saying that natural resources should be a global priority.
p1.example: Her priority was to keep within a budget rather than acquire material goods.

p1.en: The process of making goods.
p1.ex1: She reviewed the environmental impact of the production of fake goods.
p1.ex2: Indeed, reducing production waste makes economic sense.
p1.example: Widespread production of material goods consumes natural resources rapidly.

p1.en: Fair and sensible; not excessive.
p1.ex1: He reviewed the expenses and found them reasonable given the quality.
p1.ex2: It makes sense to stick to reasonable priorities when keeping within a budget.
p1.example: The price was reasonable, so she made the acquisition without hesitation.

p1.en: Not willing to do something; hesitant.
p1.ex1: He was reluctant to do away with his material possessions at first.
p1.ex2: Indeed, many consumers are reluctant to embrace minimalism.
p1.example: She was reluctant to overspend but found the eye-catching offer hard to ignore.

p1.en: An assessment or evaluation of something.
p1.ex1: He wrote a detailed review of the charity shop's selection.
p1.ex2: A review of your expenses helps you keep within a budget.
p1.example: She read every review before making a significant acquisition.

p1.en: To continue doing something or not change from it.
p1.ex1: He found it hard to stick to his priorities in a consumerist environment.
p1.ex2: It makes sense to stick to reasonable expenses and avoid overspending.
p1.example: She stuck to her budget and ignored the eye-catching display.

p1.en: A study that collects information from a group of people.
p1.ex1: She conducted a survey on the widespread acquisition of fake goods.
p1.ex2: Indeed, the survey confirmed that material possessions are a top priority for many.
p1.example: A survey found that most consumers are reluctant to review their spending habits.

p1.en: To make good use of an opportunity.
p1.ex1: He took advantage of the widespread discount to make a reasonable acquisition.
p1.ex2: It makes sense to take advantage of good value offers without overspending.
p1.example: She took advantage of the charity shop sale to make the most of her budget.

p1.en: To deliberately ignore something wrong or unpleasant.
p1.ex1: She turned a blind eye to the fake label and made the acquisition anyway.
p1.ex2: Indeed, turning a blind eye to overspending leads to budget problems.
p1.example: Many consumers turn a blind eye to the production impact on natural resources.

p1.en: The quality of being (not) able to be trusted to work or behave as expected.
p1.ex1: The unreliability of fake goods made her reluctant to buy them again.
p1.ex2: It goes without saying that reliability is a priority for any consumer.
p1.example: She reviewed the product's reliability before making the acquisition.

p1.en: Found or happening over a large area or among many people.
p1.ex1: The survey revealed widespread reluctance to review personal spending.
p1.ex2: Indeed, widespread production of fake goods is a global problem.
p1.example: Widespread consumerist habits put pressure on natural resources.

p1.en: Used to say something is so obvious it hardly needs to be mentioned.
p1.ex1: It goes without saying that a consumer should review expenses regularly.
p1.ex2: It goes without saying that widespread consumption depletes natural resources.
p1.example: It goes without saying that minimalism makes more sense than overspending.

p2.en: To feel that you must do something because of a rule or social expectation.
p2.ex1: He was obliged to queue due to the overcrowded charity shop.
p2.ex2: Consumers often feel obliged to take advantage of time-saving packaging deals.
p2.example: She felt obliged to review every purchase before keeping within her budget.

p2.en: A shop that sells donated goods to raise money for a charity.
p2.ex1: He donated his surplus material possessions to a charity shop.
p2.ex2: Buying from a charity shop is an economical alternative to consumerist spending.
p2.example: She found a thoughtful selection of outfits at the charity shop.

p2.en: Required by law or rules; not optional.
p2.ex1: She felt it was almost compulsory to save for a rainy day.
p2.ex2: The survey suggested that compulsory consumption reviews could reduce overspending.
p2.example: It is not compulsory to reuse packaging, but it makes economic sense.

p2.en: The state of being easy and quick to do or use.
p2.ex1: On impulse, he chose convenience over thoughtful selection.
p2.ex2: Indeed, convenience often outweighs the sentimental value of traditional shopping.
p2.example: She valued the convenience of time-saving packaging despite its overcrowded shelves.

p2.en: To reduce the amount of something you do or use.
p2.ex1: He cut down on impulse purchases after reviewing his overspending.
p2.ex2: It makes sense to cut down on packaging waste to preserve natural resources.
p2.example: She decided to cut down on unnecessary expenses and save for a rainy day.

p2.en: The need or desire for something, often in large quantities.
p2.ex1: A survey revealed growing demand for reusable and economical packaging.
p2.ex2: It goes without saying that demand shapes what consumers prioritise.
p2.example: Widespread demand for material goods drives consumerist production.

p2.en: To improve the quality or value of something.
p2.ex1: She enhanced her selection by visiting multiple charity shops.
p2.ex2: Reusing materials enhances the economical value of production.
p2.example: Thoughtful packaging can enhance the sentimental value of a purchase.

p2.en: To officially say that something must not be done.
p2.ex1: She felt it was almost forbidden to buy on impulse after her budget review.
p2.ex2: It goes without saying that forbidding overcrowded queues improves convenience.
p2.example: The policy forbids the sale of fake goods without reliable review.

p2.en: Worth the amount of money paid; offering a fair deal.
p2.ex1: Charity shops offer good value for money without encouraging overspending.
p2.ex2: Indeed, good value for money matters more than eye-catching packaging.
p2.example: She reviewed every acquisition to ensure it was good value for money.

p2.en: Required by law or rules.
p2.ex1: A thoughtful review of packaging is not mandatory but makes sense.
p2.ex2: She felt mandatory reuse of materials was a reasonable priority.
p2.example: It is mandatory to keep a record of expenses for tax purposes.

p2.en: Required as part of a rule or custom; compulsory.
p2.ex1: He considered saving for a rainy day an obligatory financial habit.
p2.ex2: It goes without saying that obligatory consumption reviews reduce overspending.
p2.example: Reviewing expenses monthly felt obligatory to keep within her budget.

p2.en: Without planning; suddenly and without thinking it through.
p2.ex1: He made the acquisition on impulse without reviewing its reliability.
p2.ex2: Indeed, buying on impulse often leads to overspending on material goods.
p2.example: She bought the eye-catching outfit on impulse and later regretted the expense.

p2.en: Having too many people or things in a space.
p2.ex1: An overcrowded store makes it hard to stick to a thoughtful selection.
p2.ex2: She avoided overcrowded shops by saving her visits for quieter times.
p2.example: The charity shop was overcrowded during the sale, so she decided to queue.

p2.en: The materials used to wrap or contain a product.
p2.ex1: Eye-catching packaging often encourages impulse purchases.
p2.ex2: Cutting down on packaging waste is a priority for reducing production impact.
p2.example: She reviewed the packaging to ensure it was reusable and economical.

p2.en: To wait in a line for your turn.
p2.ex1: He queued patiently, reviewing the selection from a distance.
p2.ex2: It makes sense to queue rather than leave — the selection was worth the wait.
p2.example: She had to queue for a long time in the overcrowded charity shop.

p2.en: To use something again instead of throwing it away.
p2.ex1: He made the most of every material by finding ways to reuse it.
p2.ex2: It goes without saying that reusing goods makes economical sense.
p2.example: She chose to reuse packaging rather than add to widespread waste.

p2.en: To keep money for a time when you might need it.
p2.ex1: He reviewed his expenses and set aside funds to save for a rainy day.
p2.ex2: Indeed, saving for a rainy day is a reasonable financial priority.
p2.example: She cut down on impulse purchases to save for a rainy day.

p2.en: A range of things from which to choose.
p2.ex1: She was hesitant at first but found the selection worth the queue.
p2.ex2: A wide selection of reusable goods makes it easier to cut down on packaging waste.
p2.example: The charity shop had a thoughtful selection of outfits at reasonable prices.

p2.en: The personal emotional importance of something, not its monetary worth.
p2.ex1: Material possessions sometimes hold sentimental value beyond their market price.
p2.ex2: A minimalist keeps items of sentimental value while cutting down on the rest.
p2.example: She refused to do away with the outfit because of its sentimental value.

p2.en: Showing care and consideration for others or for a situation.
p2.ex1: A thoughtful consumer reviews expenses and avoids impulse purchases.
p2.ex2: Indeed, a thoughtful approach to consumption helps preserve natural resources.
p2.example: She made a thoughtful selection from the charity shop without overspending.

p2.en: Designed to reduce the amount of time something takes.
p2.ex1: A time-saving approach to shopping helps consumers keep within a budget.
p2.ex2: Indeed, time-saving habits enhance the enjoyment of everyday consumption.
p2.example: She appreciated the time-saving convenience of reusable packaging.

p2.en: Used to introduce the first point in a discussion or list.
p2.ex1: To start off, she reviewed her expenses to identify areas to cut down on.
p2.ex2: To start off, a thoughtful selection from a charity shop makes economic sense.
p2.example: To start off, it goes without saying that keeping within a budget is essential.

p1.en: A person who examines data or information to provide expert conclusions.
p1.ex1: The analyst reflected on the economic term used to describe manufacturing costs.
p1.ex2: She worked as a digital analyst, tracking globally trending brands annually.
p1.example: An analyst presented findings on how fast fashion affects the environment.

p1.en: Once a year or every year.
p1.ex1: The analyst reported that manufacturing costs rise annually.
p1.ex2: Globally, billions of items of cheap cloth are produced annually.
p1.example: Fast fashion brands release new collections virtually every week, not just annually.

p1.en: A way of dealing with or thinking about something.
p1.ex1: The brand's approach to customisation made their process unique.
p1.ex2: Traditionally, a long-lasting approach to clothing was more common.
p1.example: A more environmentally conscious approach to fashion could reduce pollution.

p1.en: A name or label associated with a particular product or company.
p1.ex1: The brand guaranteed long-lasting quality using environmentally conscious techniques.
p1.ex2: Trendy brands potentially cost a fortune due to costly manufacturing processes.
p1.example: She reflected on how digital brands have changed fast fashion globally.

p1.en: To reduce the level or cost of something.
p1.ex1: Globally, fast fashion brands aim to bring down transportation expenses.
p1.ex2: Using inexpensive cloth can bring down the cost of production significantly.
p1.example: The analyst suggested new techniques to bring down manufacturing costs.

p1.en: Material made from fibres used to make clothes or other items.
p1.ex1: Traditionally, long-lasting cloth was sourced locally to reduce transportation impact.
p1.ex2: She reflected on how digitally customised cloth has changed the fashion process.
p1.example: The brand used poor quality cloth to bring down production costs.

p1.en: A worry or issue that is considered important.
p1.ex1: The analyst presented her concern about costly and time-consuming manufacturing.
p1.ex2: Environmentally conscious consumers express concern about globally polluted waterways.
p1.example: A major concern is that fast fashion is potentially damaging to the environment.

p1.en: Expensive; costing a lot of money or resources.
p1.ex1: She reflected on how costly transportation adds to the price of branded cloth.
p1.ex2: Costly customisation is virtually impossible for inexpensive brands to guarantee.
p1.example: Traditional, long-lasting techniques are often more costly than fast fashion processes.

p1.en: The expression of disapproval or judgement of something.
p1.ex1: The analyst reflected on the criticism directed at poor quality manufacturing.
p1.ex2: Environmentally conscious consumers present strong criticism of trendy but costly brands.
p1.example: Fast fashion brands face widespread criticism for producing polluted waste annually.

p1.en: The process of making something to suit individual needs or preferences.
p1.ex1: She valued customisation over trendy, inexpensive fast fashion alternatives.
p1.ex2: The brand's approach to customisation was both long-lasting and environmentally conscious.
p1.example: Digital customisation has made it possible to present unique clothing globally.

p1.en: Made or altered to suit a particular person or purpose.
p1.ex1: The brand presented a customised digital tool to reduce manufacturing time.
p1.ex2: Customised items potentially cost more but are rarely poor quality.
p1.example: She preferred customised, long-lasting cloth over trendy fast fashion.

p1.en: Relating to computers or electronic technology.
p1.ex1: The brand used a digital approach to bring down customisation costs.
p1.ex2: She reflected on how digital techniques have made clothing more accessible annually.
p1.example: Digital tools have transformed the manufacturing process in fast fashion globally.

p1.en: Relating to money, trade, and production of goods.
p1.ex1: Globally, fast fashion has had a significant economic impact on traditional manufacturing.
p1.ex2: An environmentally conscious approach can still be economically sustainable.
p1.example: The analyst presented an economic term for the rising cost of transportation.

p1.en: Aware of and concerned about the impact of actions on the environment.
p1.ex1: She reflected on how being environmentally conscious affects brand choice annually.
p1.ex2: The brand presented a globally recognised, environmentally conscious manufacturing technique.
p1.example: Environmentally conscious consumers prefer long-lasting cloth over fast fashion.

p1.en: The rapid production of large quantities of trendy, cheap clothing.
p1.ex1: The analyst presented criticism of fast fashion's poor quality and costly waste.
p1.ex2: Traditionally, clothing was long-lasting — fast fashion reversed this process.
p1.example: Fast fashion is potentially one of the most polluted industries globally.

p1.en: Throughout the world.
p1.ex1: The analyst reflected on how digital tools have transformed manufacturing globally.
p1.ex2: Annually, millions of tonnes of polluted cloth are discarded globally.
p1.example: Fast fashion brands sell trendy items globally at inexpensive prices.

p1.en: To promise that something will happen or be done.
p1.ex1: She reflected on whether fast fashion could ever guarantee environmentally conscious production.
p1.ex2: Digital customisation techniques can guarantee a more unique and potentially costly product.
p1.example: The brand guaranteed long-lasting quality despite using inexpensive cloth.

p1.en: Not costing much money.
p1.ex1: She brought down her budget by choosing inexpensive but long-lasting cloth.
p1.ex2: Globally, inexpensive manufacturing processes have made fast fashion widespread.
p1.example: Fast fashion presents inexpensive items that are trendy but potentially poor quality.

p1.en: Continuing for a long time; durable.
p1.ex1: An environmentally conscious brand guarantees long-lasting, customised products.
p1.ex2: She reflected that long-lasting items are rarely produced by fast fashion brands.
p1.example: Traditionally, clothing was made using long-lasting techniques and high-quality cloth.

p1.en: The process of making goods on a large scale using machinery.
p1.ex1: Digital techniques have transformed the manufacturing process in fast fashion.
p1.ex2: Bringing down manufacturing costs is a key term in the economic approach to fashion.
p1.example: The analyst presented concern about the polluted impact of global manufacturing.

p1.en: Made dirty or harmful by waste or chemicals.
p1.ex1: The analyst reflected on how globally polluted rivers are linked to cloth manufacturing.
p1.ex2: An environmentally conscious brand avoids potentially polluted production techniques.
p1.example: Fast fashion produces polluted water and fabric waste annually.

p1.en: Not good enough; below standard.
p1.ex1: The criticism of the brand centred on its poor quality and costly returns process.
p1.ex2: She reflected that poor quality items are rarely long-lasting, no matter how trendy.
p1.example: Inexpensive fast fashion is often made from poor quality cloth.

p1.en: Possibly at some future time; in a way that may become real.
p1.ex1: Digital customisation could potentially bring down manufacturing costs annually.
p1.ex2: She reflected that inexpensive cloth is potentially poor quality in the long term.
p1.example: Fast fashion is potentially one of the most environmentally damaging industries globally.

p1.en: To show or introduce something formally.
p1.ex1: She presented a new digital technique to bring down manufacturing costs.
p1.ex2: The brand presented a customised, long-lasting alternative to trendy fast fashion.
p1.example: The analyst presented her findings on the environmental impact of fast fashion.

p1.en: A series of actions or steps taken to achieve a result.
p1.ex1: She reflected on how the digital process has changed customisation globally.
p1.ex2: The analyst presented a concern about the costly transportation process.
p1.example: The manufacturing process of fast fashion is potentially polluted and time-consuming.

p1.en: To think carefully about something; or to show the nature of something.
p1.ex1: The analyst reflected on globally rising manufacturing costs annually.
p1.ex2: A brand's approach to cloth quality reflects its environmentally conscious values.
p1.example: She reflected on how fast fashion reflects wider consumerist values.

p1.en: To place or locate something in a particular position.
p1.ex1: The brand's digital tools were situated globally to guarantee fast delivery.
p1.ex2: She reflected on how fast fashion brands are often situated in polluted industrial zones.
p1.example: The manufacturing plant was situated far from the city to reduce transportation costs.

p1.en: A particular way of doing something, especially one requiring skill.
p1.ex1: The analyst presented a new technique to bring down costs and reduce pollution.
p1.ex2: Traditionally, long-lasting cloth was produced using hand-crafted techniques.
p1.example: Digital techniques have transformed the manufacturing process in fast fashion globally.

p1.en: A word or phrase used to describe something specific.
p1.ex1: In economic terms, bringing down manufacturing costs is a key concern.
p1.ex2: She reflected on the term environmentally conscious and how it applies to the brand.
p1.example: The analyst introduced the economic term used to define fast fashion production.

p1.en: Taking a large amount of time.
p1.ex1: The digital process was designed to make customisation less time-consuming.
p1.ex2: She reflected that environmentally conscious approaches are often more time-consuming but worthwhile.
p1.example: Customised, long-lasting manufacturing is more time-consuming than fast fashion.

p1.en: A device or resource used to do a job or achieve a goal.
p1.ex1: She presented a new tool to bring down transportation costs globally.
p1.ex2: The analyst used a digital tool to reflect on annually rising production trends.
p1.example: Digital tools have made the manufacturing process faster and less costly.

p1.en: In a way that follows long-established customs or practices.
p1.ex1: Traditionally, consumers reflected on value before making a purchase.
p1.ex2: Globally, fast fashion has replaced what was traditionally a slower manufacturing process.
p1.example: Traditionally, clothing was made using long-lasting cloth and time-consuming techniques.

p1.en: The act or system of moving goods or people from one place to another.
p1.ex1: She reflected on how digital approaches could bring down transportation costs annually.
p1.ex2: The analyst presented a concern about the polluted impact of global transportation.
p1.example: Transportation adds a potentially costly element to globally sourced manufacturing.

p1.en: Very fashionable at a particular time.
p1.ex1: She reflected that trendy items rarely stay in style long enough to be long-lasting.
p1.ex2: Globally, digital brands guarantee trendy customised items annually.
p1.example: Fast fashion brands produce trendy items that are inexpensive but potentially poor quality.

p1.en: Almost or nearly; used to say something is almost completely true.
p1.ex1: The digital process has virtually transformed global manufacturing annually.
p1.ex2: She reflected that virtually all trendy fast fashion cloth ends up as waste.
p1.example: Fast fashion items are virtually inexpensive but potentially poor quality.

p2.en: Something that costs much more than it is worth.
p2.ex1: He felt the customised item was a rip-off given its inexpensive manufacturing process.
p2.ex2: Fast fashion items can feel like a rip-off when they fall apart quickly.
p2.example: She said the trendy brand was a complete rip-off for such poor quality cloth.

p2.en: The activity of searching for goods at lower than normal prices.
p2.ex1: Bargain hunting at clearance sales can help you avoid overspending.
p2.ex2: He preferred bargain hunting to shopping sprees at overpriced brand stores.
p2.example: She enjoyed bargain hunting at the flea market every weekend.

p2.en: The place in a shop where you pay for goods.
p2.ex1: He used his debit card at the checkout to avoid withdrawing cash.
p2.ex2: The checkout was understaffed, which led to long queues.
p2.example: She was overcharged at the checkout and had to ask for a correction.

p2.en: A sale where goods are sold cheaply to get rid of them.
p2.ex1: He went bargain hunting during the clearance event at the flea market.
p2.ex2: Clearance prices are often underpriced compared to their original cost.
p2.example: She found a bargain at the clearance sale — not a rip-off at all.

p2.en: To be very expensive.
p2.ex1: She said the overpriced outfit cost a fortune — an absolute rip-off.
p2.ex2: Traditionally crafted, long-lasting items can cost a fortune but are worth it.
p2.example: The customised brand item cost a fortune compared to fast fashion alternatives.

p2.en: To be extremely expensive.
p2.ex1: He said the clearance was fine — the original price cost an arm and a leg.
p2.ex2: Fast fashion is popular because traditional alternatives cost an arm and a leg.
p2.word: cost an arm and a leg
p2.example: The trendy brand coat cost an arm and a leg, but she bought it anyway.

p2.en: A card that takes money directly from your bank account when you pay.
p2.ex1: He was overcharged on his debit card and had to report it.
p2.ex2: A debit card makes bargain hunting easier by tracking what you spend.
p2.example: She used her debit card at the checkout instead of withdrawing cash.

p2.en: An outdoor market where people sell second-hand or inexpensive goods.
p2.ex1: He preferred the flea market to overpriced brand stores.
p2.ex2: Flea markets are a great alternative to fast fashion shopping sprees.
p2.example: She found a one-of-a-kind piece at the flea market during her bargain hunting.

p2.en: To go out shopping.
p2.ex1: He hit the shops on a spending spree and ended up overcharged on his debit card.
p2.ex2: She hit the shops at the flea market rather than overpriced brand stores.
p2.example: She decided to hit the shops during the clearance sale for some bargain hunting.

p2.en: To pack something again, usually differently or more carefully.
p2.ex1: He repacked the clearance items into reusable bags after checkout.
p2.ex2: The understaffed checkout meant items were repacked incorrectly.
p2.example: She had to repack her shopping after the overpriced items were returned.

p2.en: To look at prices in different shops before deciding where to buy.
p2.ex1: He shopped around at the flea market before paying at the checkout.
p2.ex2: Bargain hunting means shopping around to avoid being ripped off.
p2.example: She always shops around before spending a fortune on a trendy brand.

p2.en: A period of buying a lot of things, often impulsively.
p2.ex1: He hit the shops on a spending spree and ended up with overpriced items.
p2.ex2: A shopping spree at a flea market is far less costly than at brand stores.
p2.example: She went on a shopping spree during the clearance and overspent on her debit card.

p2.en: Something bought for a much lower price than its real value (informal).
p2.ex1: She found a long-lasting woollen coat at the flea market — a real steal.
p2.ex2: He shopped around and found a bargain that was practically a steal.
p2.example: That customised jacket at the clearance was a steal — not a rip-off at all.

p2.en: To take money out of a bank account.
p2.ex1: He preferred his debit card over withdrawing cash at the checkout.
p2.ex2: She withdrew the exact amount to avoid overspending on her shopping spree.
p2.example: She withdrew cash before hitting the shops at the flea market.

p2.en: Having more bookings than there are spaces available.
p2.ex1: She arrived to find the fitting room overbooked due to a shopping spree event.
p2.ex2: The understaffed checkout made the overbooked situation worse.
p2.example: The store was overbooked during the clearance and the checkout queue was endless.

p2.en: To charge someone too much money.
p2.ex1: He felt the brand had overcharged him — a complete rip-off.
p2.ex2: Overpriced fast fashion items often overcharge for poor quality cloth.
p2.example: She was overcharged at the checkout and had to return to the customer service desk.

p2.en: To cook food for too long.
p2.ex1: He overcook the meal while distracted by browsing overpriced brand catalogues.
p2.ex2: Overcooking, like overcharging, means going further than necessary.
p2.example: She overcook the food during the shopping spree preparation — a minor mistake.

p2.en: To do something to an excessive degree.
p2.ex1: He overdid his shopping spree and withdrew far too much cash.
p2.ex2: Don't overdo the clearance sales — it's easy to overspend.
p2.example: She overdid the bargain hunting and came home exhausted.

p2.en: To think something is bigger, better, or more important than it actually is.
p2.ex1: He overestimated the value of the clearance items — they were a rip-off.
p2.ex2: Don't overestimate how much you can carry on a shopping spree.
p2.example: She overestimated how much cash she needed to withdraw for the flea market.

p2.en: Extremely happy.
p2.ex1: He was overjoyed when the overpriced brand item went on clearance.
p2.ex2: She was overjoyed that the checkout wasn't overbooked for once.
p2.example: She was overjoyed to find a steal at the flea market during her bargain hunting.

p2.en: Costing more than it is worth.
p2.ex1: He said the item cost an arm and a leg — completely overpriced.
p2.ex2: Overpriced fast fashion items are often a rip-off compared to clearance alternatives.
p2.example: She avoided the overpriced brand store and went bargain hunting at the flea market.

p2.en: To sleep longer than intended.
p2.ex1: He overslept and arrived at the flea market after all the bargains were gone.
p2.ex2: Oversleeping meant she had to hit the shops at the overpriced brand store instead.
p2.example: She overslept and missed the clearance sale she had planned for her shopping spree.

p2.en: Having more workers than necessary.
p2.ex1: The flea market felt overstaffed compared to the clearance sale.
p2.ex2: An overstaffed store can be just as frustrating as an understaffed one.
p2.example: Unlike the understaffed checkout, the brand store was overstaffed and slow.

p2.en: Above the normal or allowed weight.
p2.ex1: He was overweight with shopping from the clearance and couldn't withdraw more cash.
p2.ex2: After bargain hunting at the flea market, her bags were completely overweight.
p2.example: Her bag was overweight after the shopping spree and she had to repack.

p2.en: To charge less than the correct price.
p2.ex1: The checkout screen showed she had been undercharged by mistake.
p2.ex2: He was undercharged at the clearance and felt too awkward to point it out.
p2.example: The flea market seller undercharged her — practically giving her a steal.

p2.en: To cook food for less time than needed.
p2.ex1: Like overcharging, undercooking means failing to meet the right standard.
p2.ex2: He undercooked the food during his shopping spree preparation.
p2.example: She undercooked the meal while distracted during her bargain hunting.

p2.en: Sold for less than the real value.
p2.ex1: Clearance items are often underpriced to bring down stock quickly.
p2.ex2: She found an underpriced, long-lasting item during her bargain hunting.
p2.example: The woollen coat at the flea market was underpriced — a genuine steal.

p2.en: To spend less than the amount available or planned.
p2.ex1: He underspent during the shopping spree by sticking to a budget.
p2.ex2: Bargain hunting helped her underspend and avoid a rip-off.
p2.example: She underspent at the clearance and had cash left to withdraw for the flea market.

p2.en: Not having enough workers.
p2.ex1: An understaffed flea market stall can make bargain hunting frustrating.
p2.ex2: She was overcharged because the understaffed checkout made too many errors.
p2.example: The checkout was understaffed, causing long queues during the clearance.

p2.en: Below the normal or expected weight.
p2.ex1: The parcel was underweight, so shipping was cheaper than expected.
p2.ex2: After the flea market, her bag felt underweight compared to a typical shopping spree.
p2.example: His shopping bag was underweight — he had underspent at the clearance.

p3.en: To look at goods in a shop without necessarily buying anything.
p3.ex1: He browsed the overpriced brand store but left without using his debit card.
p3.ex2: Browsing online before hitting the shops can help avoid rip-offs.
p3.example: She spent an hour browsing the flea market before making any purchase.

p3.en: Having a small piece broken off the edge or surface.
p3.ex1: He returned the chipped mug, claiming it was a rip-off at that price.
p3.ex2: A chipped label or scratched surface can reduce an item's value significantly.
p3.example: She noticed the item was chipped and asked for a discount at the checkout.

p3.en: To appear and disappear repeatedly; to be temporary.
p3.ex1: Peer pressure to keep up with fast fashion comes and goes seasonally.
p3.ex2: Pop-up shops come and go, making bargain hunting an unpredictable activity.
p3.example: Trendy fashion labels come and go — long-lasting style is more valuable.

p3.en: Having a line or break on the surface without falling apart.
p3.ex1: She found the item cracked at the checkout and asked to exchange it.
p3.ex2: A cracked or chipped item should be returned with a receipt.
p3.example: The cracked screen made the price tag seem like a rip-off.

p3.en: To make a hollow mark in a surface by hitting it.
p3.ex1: She dented the price tag argument by showing a receipt from the flea market.
p3.ex2: Shipping damage can dent, scratch or crack an item during transit.
p3.example: The delivery had dented the packaging, making the item look chipped.

p3.en: To prevent someone from concentrating on something.
p3.ex1: She was distracted by a pop-up stall and ended up on an unplanned shopping spree.
p3.ex2: Peer pressure can distract you from keeping up with a sensible budget.
p3.example: Eye-catching displays are designed to distract consumers from the price tag.

p3.en: A person who follows fashion trends too slavishly, often without considering cost or suitability.
p3.ex1: A fashion victim is easily distracted by pop-up shops and impulsive purchases.
p3.ex2: She refused to be a fashion victim and chose long-lasting style over trendy fast fashion.

p1.en: A large amount of money or valuable possessions; also an abundance of something.
