p3.en: Machines or mechanical equipment used in industry or manufacturing.
p3.ex1: The carpenter assessed the working environment for safe lifting and machinery use.
p3.ex2: Work-related insecurity increased when inconsistent machinery caused instability.
p3.example: Irregular machinery maintenance caused interruptions and reduced productivity.

p3.en: Lasting or intended to last indefinitely.
p3.ex1: The carpenter sought a permanent working environment to reduce insecurity.
p3.ex2: Permanent employment provides stability and reduces work-related inconsistency.
p3.example: She left her temporary role for a permanent position offering salary stability.

p3.en: The efficiency with which work is done; how much output is produced.
p3.ex1: Teamwork and stability increased productivity in the carpenter's profession.
p3.ex2: Work-related interruptions and insecurity consistently lower productivity and morale.
p3.example: Irregular machinery and inconsistent lifting reduced productivity in the working environment.

p3.en: A paid job that requires specialised training or education.
p3.ex1: Her profession offered permanent stability despite inconsistent and irregular salary periods.
p3.ex2: Work-related insecurity in the profession increased during irregular machinery interruptions.
p3.example: Carpentry is a profession that requires lifting, teamwork, and machinery expertise.

p3.en: A fixed regular payment for employment, usually paid monthly.
p3.ex1: She sought a permanent profession with a stable and regular salary.
p3.ex2: Work-related insecurity increased when the irregular salary failed to reflect productivity.
p3.example: The temporary salary was inconsistent and caused insecurity in the working environment.

p3.en: The quality of being firm, steady, and not likely to change.
p3.ex1: The carpenter valued stability and teamwork over an inconsistent temporary profession.
p3.ex2: Permanent employment provides stability, productivity, and reduces irregular interruptions.
p3.example: Stability in salary and working environment reduced work-related insecurity.

p3.en: Not likely to change or fail; firmly established.
p3.ex1: She sought a stable profession with consistent machinery and regular lifting routines.
p3.ex2: Teamwork and productivity are stronger in a stable and permanent working environment.
p3.example: A stable salary and permanent working environment reduced the carpenter's insecurity.

p3.en: The ability to work cooperatively with others towards a shared goal.
p3.ex1: The carpenter's profession required stable teamwork and consistent productivity.
p3.ex2: Permanent stability increases teamwork and reduces work-related irregular interruptions.
p3.example: Teamwork in the working environment reduced machinery interruptions and insecurity.

p3.en: Lasting for only a limited time; not permanent.
p3.ex1: The carpenter took a temporary profession while seeking permanent working environment stability.
p3.ex2: Temporary lifting roles increased insecurity and reduced long-term productivity.
p3.example: Her temporary role lacked stability and offered an inconsistent, irregular salary.

p3.en: The conditions and surroundings in which work is carried out.
p3.ex1: The carpenter assessed the working environment for irregular lifting and machinery risks.
p3.ex2: Teamwork and productivity improve when the working environment is permanent and stable.
p3.example: A stable working environment with consistent machinery reduces insecurity and interruptions.

p3.en: Connected to or caused by your job or profession.
p3.ex1: The carpenter reported work-related interruptions from unstable machinery in the environment.
p3.ex2: Permanent stability reduces work-related insecurity and improves productivity.
p3.example: Work-related insecurity increased with irregular salary and inconsistent lifting demands.

p1.en: A person who formally applies for something, such as a job.
p1.ex1: The interviewee stood out as the most straightforward and punctual applicant.
p1.ex2: She was a strong applicant — smartly dressed, with clear job prospects and initiative.
p1.example: Each applicant was assessed for soft skills before being suited to the position.

p1.en: A settled way of thinking or feeling about something.
p1.ex1: The interviewee revealed a confident attitude — suited, punctual, and smartly dressed.
p1.ex2: A straightforward attitude and initiative are key traps applicants must avoid in interviews.
p1.example: Her positive attitude helped her stand out and meet the demands of the occupation.

p1.en: Before a particular event or time.
p1.ex1: The applicant researched the occupation beforehand to stand out in the interview.
p1.ex2: Being smartly dressed and punctual beforehand reveals a straightforward, suited attitude.
p1.example: She ran through the job prospects and specified her experience beforehand.

p1.en: Relating to how a person behaves.
p1.ex1: Behavioural traps in interviews reveal whether applicants can meet the demands of the position.
p1.ex2: She ran through behavioural questions beforehand to stand out as a suited applicant.
p1.example: The interviewee was assessed using behavioural questions to determine her initiative.

p1.en: To talk with excessive pride about something.
p1.ex1: She confessed to boasting about her occupation, which became a trap in the interview.
p1.ex2: Standing out is straightforward — display initiative rather than boast about attitude.
p1.example: The applicant was warned not to boast about job prospects during the interview.

p1.en: To cause a quality or feature to become more noticeable.
p1.ex1: A smartly dressed applicant brings out a suited and punctual first impression.
p1.ex2: Behavioural questions bring out whether an applicant can meet the demands of the position.
p1.example: The interviewee's attitude brought out her initiative and straightforward approach.

p1.en: To admit something, especially something you feel guilty about.
p1.ex1: The applicant confessed beforehand that she was not entirely suited to the occupation.
p1.ex2: A straightforward interviewee confesses honestly rather than revealing a misleading attitude.
p1.example: She confessed to a trap in the interview — she had boasted about her job prospects.

p1.en: To discover or establish something by research or investigation.
p1.ex1: She ran through the questions beforehand to determine how to stand out.
p1.ex2: Determining whether an applicant is suited to the position requires a straightforward approach.
p1.example: The interviewer used behavioural questions to determine the applicant's initiative.

p1.en: To show or make something visible.
p1.ex1: She ran through how to display soft skills without boasting in the interview.
p1.ex2: Displaying a straightforward attitude brings out the best in any interviewee.
p1.example: The smartly dressed applicant displayed initiative and a suited, punctual attitude.

p1.en: To give someone a paid job.
p1.ex1: She was employed after displaying a straightforward attitude and strong job prospects.
p1.ex2: Employing the right applicant requires determining their behavioural attitude beforehand.
p1.example: The company employed the most suited applicant — punctual, smartly dressed, and initiative-driven.

p1.en: The ability to assess situations and take action independently.
p1.ex1: She ran through ways to bring out initiative without boasting in the behavioural interview.
p1.ex2: Applicants suited to the position confess to taking initiative beforehand.
p1.example: The interviewee displayed initiative — a key quality that made her stand out.

p1.en: A person who is being interviewed.
p1.ex1: She confessed beforehand to being nervous — but displayed initiative and a suited attitude.
p1.ex2: A behavioural trap reveals whether the interviewee is genuinely suited to the occupation.
p1.example: The interviewee stood out for being smartly dressed, punctual, and straightforward.

p1.en: The chances of getting a good job or being successful in your career.
p1.ex1: Boasting about job prospects is a trap — display initiative and a suited attitude instead.
p1.ex2: Applicants with strong job prospects stand out when smartly dressed and punctual.
p1.example: She ran through her job prospects and specified her occupation experience beforehand.

p1.en: Without a paid job.
p1.ex1: The jobless applicant confessed to a behavioural trap in her previous position.
p1.ex2: Being jobless motivated her to run through her CV and stand out as a suited interviewee.
p1.example: She became jobless after failing to meet the demands of the occupation.

p1.en: Work that involves using your hands or body rather than your mind.
p1.ex1: She confessed her attitude toward manual labour was not suited to the working environment.
p1.ex2: Applicants for manual labour positions stand out by displaying punctual, straightforward initiative.
p1.example: The occupation required manual labour — specified in the position beforehand.

p1.en: To satisfy requirements or reach a required standard.
p1.ex1: The interviewee displayed initiative and a suited attitude to meet expectations.
p1.ex2: Being smartly dressed and punctual helps applicants meet the demands of the occupation.
p1.example: She ran through her experience to determine if she could meet the demands of the position.

p1.en: A person's job or profession.
p1.ex1: The interviewee confessed that manual labour was not suited to her occupation.
p1.ex2: A behavioural question determines whether the applicant is suited to the occupation.
p1.example: She specified her occupation beforehand to stand out as a suited applicant.

p1.en: A job or role within an organisation.
p1.ex1: The applicant displayed initiative and was employed for the permanent position.
p1.ex2: Behavioural traps reveal whether an interviewee can meet the demands of the position.
p1.example: She ran through the requirements to determine if she was suited to the position.

p1.en: Arriving or doing something at the agreed time.
p1.ex1: She was determined to be punctual and straightforward to meet the demands of the position.
p1.ex2: Being punctual and suited beforehand helps applicants avoid behavioural traps.
p1.example: The smartly dressed, punctual interviewee displayed initiative and stood out.

p1.en: To make something known that was previously hidden.
p1.ex1: She confessed to a trap — she had revealed too much about her job prospects.
p1.ex2: A smartly dressed applicant reveals initiative and a straightforward, punctual attitude.
p1.example: The behavioural interview revealed whether the applicant was suited to the occupation.

p1.en: To practise or go over something quickly.
p1.ex1: The interviewee ran through behavioural traps to avoid boasting in the interview.
p1.ex2: Running through the position requirements determined whether she was suited and punctual.
p1.example: She ran through her CV and specified her occupation beforehand to stand out.

p1.en: Wearing neat, tidy, and appropriate clothes.
p1.ex1: She was determined to be smartly dressed, punctual, and straightforward beforehand.
p1.ex2: Being smartly dressed and suited reveals a positive attitude toward the occupation.
p1.example: The smartly dressed applicant displayed initiative and stood out in the interview.

p1.en: To state something clearly and in detail.
p1.ex1: The applicant specified her initiative and attitude in the behavioural interview.
p1.ex2: Specifying job prospects beforehand helps applicants stand out as suited interviewees.
p1.example: She specified her occupation experience beforehand to meet the demands of the position.

p1.en: To be clearly noticeable or better than others.
p1.ex1: She ran through how to stand out without boasting about her job prospects.
p1.ex2: Displaying a straightforward attitude and initiative helps any applicant stand out.
p1.example: The smartly dressed, punctual applicant stood out and was employed for the position.

p1.en: Simple and easy to understand; honest and direct.
p1.ex1: She ran through the behavioural questions in a straightforward, suited manner.
p1.ex2: Specifying your occupation in a straightforward way helps applicants stand out.
p1.example: A straightforward attitude and initiative helped the interviewee meet the demands of the position.

p1.en: Right or appropriate for a particular purpose or person.
p1.ex1: The smartly dressed applicant displayed initiative and was considered suited for the occupation.
p1.ex2: Behavioural questions reveal whether an interviewee is genuinely suited to the position.
p1.example: She determined she was suited to the position after running through the requirements.

p1.en: A trick or situation designed to catch or trick someone.
p1.ex1: Confessing to a weakness can become a trap if not specified in a straightforward way.
p1.ex2: The interviewee revealed a trap — she had boasted rather than displaying initiative.
p1.example: She ran through behavioural traps beforehand to avoid boasting in the interview.

p2.en: To remember or consider something when making a decision.
p2.ex1: She bore in mind the compensation and pension benefits before deciding to resign.
p2.ex2: Bear in mind that going out of business affects insurance, wages, and medical cover.
p2.example: Bear in mind that expanding a department requires a supervisor and adequate wages.

p2.en: Money given as payment for loss, injury, or as part of a job.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that compensation, pension, and insurance are key workplace benefits.
p2.ex2: The employee resigned after the company refused to offer a fair pay rise or compensation.
p2.example: She received compensation after the supervisor failed to meet the department's demands.

p2.en: A section of a larger organisation dealing with a specific area.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that each department requires a form of medical and pension support.
p2.ex2: She resigned after the department went out of business and compensation was denied.
p2.example: The supervisor expanded the department and set up a new insurance and wage structure.

p2.en: A task or action that you are required to perform as part of a job.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that medical and pension duties are set up by the workplace insurance.
p2.ex2: She resigned because her duty to expand the department was not supported by a pay rise.
p2.example: Her duty as supervisor was to inspire the department and manage compensation fairly.

p2.en: To increase in size, number, or importance.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that expanding too fast can cause the business to go out of business.
p2.ex2: She was inspired to expand her duties after receiving a pay rise and pension benefits.
p2.example: The supervisor expanded the department and set up a new wage and insurance structure.

p2.en: To dismiss someone from their job.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that firing without compensation or a valid form is a legal risk.
p2.ex2: She resigned before the department could fire her — insurance and pension were secured.
p2.example: The supervisor fired the employee after repeated failure to meet workplace duties.

p2.en: An official document with spaces for information.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that a compensation form must be signed before the department can expand.
p2.ex2: The supervisor fired the employee after completing a duty and wage review form.
p2.example: She filled in a form to set up pension and insurance before the supervisor retired.

p2.en: To stop operating as a business.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that going out of business affects all pension, medical, and compensation plans.
p2.ex2: She resigned before the supervisor fired her — the business was about to go out of business.
p2.example: The department went out of business after failing to expand wages and insurance.

p2.en: To fill someone with enthusiasm, motivation, or a desire to act.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that a pay rise and medical benefits inspire employees to expand their duties.
p2.ex2: She resigned because no one in the department inspired her to take on new responsibilities.
p2.example: The supervisor inspired the department by setting up a fair wage and pension structure.

p2.en: An arrangement where you pay regularly to get financial help if something goes wrong.
p2.ex1: She set up insurance and pension forms before the supervisor retired.
p2.ex2: The department went out of business after insurance, wage, and medical funding collapsed.
p2.example: Bear in mind that workplace insurance covers medical, compensation, and wage duties.

p2.en: Relating to the practice of medicine and health.
p2.ex1: The supervisor set up medical and pension cover when the department started to expand.
p2.ex2: She resigned because medical and insurance duties were not included in the wage form.
p2.example: Bear in mind that medical benefits are part of the workplace compensation and insurance.

p2.en: An increase in the amount of money you are paid for your job.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that a pay rise without a pension form is incomplete compensation.
p2.ex2: The supervisor inspired the team by setting up a fair pay rise and insurance structure.
p2.example: She requested a pay rise after expanding her department duties beyond her original wage.

p2.en: A regular payment made to someone who has retired from work.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that pension and medical compensation are critical workplace duties.
p2.ex2: The company went out of business before her pension and wage form could be finalised.
p2.example: She set up a pension and insurance form before the supervisor retired from the department.

p2.en: To voluntarily leave your job.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that resigning without a form may affect your insurance and medical cover.
p2.ex2: The supervisor inspired her to stay — but she resigned when the business went out of business.
p2.example: She resigned after the department failed to offer a pay rise, pension, or compensation.

p2.en: To leave your job permanently, usually because of age.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that retiring early may affect wage, medical, and compensation benefits.
p2.ex2: She inspired the department before retiring — leaving behind a clear pay rise structure.
p2.example: The supervisor retired after setting up pension, insurance, and department forms.

p2.en: To establish or start a new business or system.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that setting up a business requires insurance, wage, and compensation forms.
p2.ex2: The supervisor inspired her to set up a department with fair pension and medical cover.
p2.example: She set up a business after the department went out of business.

p2.en: A person who oversees and directs the work of others.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that a supervisor manages compensation, duty, and medical insurance forms.
p2.ex2: She resigned after the supervisor fired a colleague and refused to offer a pay rise.
p2.example: The supervisor inspired the department to expand and set up fair wages and pension.

p2.en: To gain control of something or assume responsibility from someone else.
p2.ex1: Bear in mind that taking over a department requires updating insurance and compensation forms.
p2.ex2: She was inspired to take over and expand the department with fair wages and pension cover.
p2.example: She took over as supervisor after the previous manager resigned and the business nearly went out of business.

p2.en: A fixed regular payment for work, usually calculated by the hour or week.
p2.ex1: The supervisor set up a wage and insurance form after the department started to expand.
p2.ex2: She resigned because her wage failed to reflect her expanded duties and compensation.
p2.example: Bear in mind that a fair wage alongside pension and medical benefits reduces resignation.

p2.en: The location where someone works.
p2.ex1: The supervisor inspired the department by setting up a fair workplace wage structure.
p2.ex2: She resigned after the workplace went out of business and pension forms were cancelled.
p2.example: Bear in mind that a safe workplace requires insurance, medical, and compensation cover.

p3.en: Feeling satisfied because you have achieved something meaningful.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that feeling fulfilled is not just about wage — it is about meaningful duty.
p3.ex2: She resigned from the low-paid job to find a well-paid, fulfilled workplace role.
p3.example: She felt fulfilled after setting up her own business and inspiring a strong department.

p3.en: Introducing new ideas or methods.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that innovative thinking and soft skills help burn out be avoided.
p3.ex2: She turned down a low-paid offer and accepted a well-paid, innovative position.
p3.example: The supervisor inspired the department with innovative ways to expand and avoid going out of business.

p3.en: Receiving a very small amount of money for work.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that low-paid positions with no pension or insurance lead to burnout.
p3.ex2: Working for peanuts in a low-paid department led her to call it a day and resign.
p3.example: She resigned from her low-paid job to find a well-paid, fulfilled workplace role.

p3.en: An incorrect belief or understanding about something.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that misconceptions about low-paid work can burn out your best applicants.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, the misconception about the wage ruined the workplace morale.
p3.example: A common misconception is that well-paid jobs are always fulfilled and innovative.

p3.en: The feeling of being safe or having stable conditions.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that security, pension, and insurance are key to avoiding burnout.
p3.ex2: Working for peanuts with no security or insurance made her call it a day.
p3.example: She turned down an innovative role for the security of a well-paid, permanent position.

p3.en: Receiving a good amount of money for your work.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that well-paid positions require innovative thinking and no misconceptions.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, she got on the same page and secured a well-paid job.
p3.example: She turned down the low-paid offer and accepted a well-paid, fulfilled supervisor role.

p3.en: To become exhausted from overwork.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that security and well-paid conditions prevent employees from burning out.
p3.ex2: The supervisor called it a day after burning out — there was no misconception about why.
p3.example: She burned out after years of working for peanuts in a low-paid department.

p3.en: To do someone's job or duties while they are absent.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that filling in for a low-paid colleague builds fulfilled workplace trust.
p3.ex2: She showed him the ropes before filling in — there was no misconception about the duty.
p3.example: She filled in for the supervisor to show the department she was on the same page.

p3.en: To manage to survive or cope with a difficult situation.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that getting by on a low-paid wage leads to burnout and misconception.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, she got by until a well-paid innovative role came up.
p3.example: She worked for peanuts but got by — the security of the position made it worthwhile.

p3.en: To review or check something carefully.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that going over the insurance and wage form prevents workplace misconception.
p3.ex2: She showed him the ropes and went over the duty list — they were on the same page.
p3.example: She went over the compensation form with the supervisor before the department expanded.

p3.en: To tell someone about something to get their opinion or approval.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that running innovative ideas by management avoids misconception.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, she ran it by the department and they were all on the same page.
p3.example: She ran the pay rise proposal by the supervisor before going over the compensation form.

p3.en: To refuse an offer or request.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that turning down an innovative offer for security may lead to misconception.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, she turned it down — working for peanuts was not worth it.
p3.example: She turned down a low-paid position and held out for a well-paid, fulfilled role.

p3.en: To develop well or have a positive result; also to exercise.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that things work out when security, innovation, and duty are on the same page.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, it all worked out — no burnout, no misconception.
p3.example: Her decision to resign and set up a business worked out — she felt fulfilled and well paid.

p3.en: To decide to stop doing something for the day.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that burning out means it is time to call it a day and reassess.
p3.ex2: She called it a day — working for peanuts in a low-paid role was a misconception of success.
p3.example: The supervisor called it a day after going over the insurance and wage form.

p3.en: To have just enough money for your basic needs.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that making ends meet on a low wage leads to burnout and misconception.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, she turned down the job — she could not make ends meet.
p3.example: She worked for peanuts and struggled to make ends meet in the low-paid department.

p3.en: To make someone very happy.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that a well-paid offer and pension security can make an applicant's day.
p3.ex2: The supervisor showed her the ropes, and the fulfilled workplace role made her day.
p3.example: The pay rise made her day — she had been working for peanuts in a low-paid role.

p3.ru: быть на одной волне, понимать друг друга
p3.en: To have the same understanding or agreement about something.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that being on the same page avoids burnout and workplace misconception.
p3.ex2: She ran it by the team — they were on the same page about the innovative pay rise.
p3.example: The department and supervisor were on the same page about the wage and insurance form.

p3.en: To function perfectly and smoothly.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that a workplace runs like clockwork when everyone is on the same page.
p3.ex2: She showed him the ropes and the whole department ran like clockwork in no time.
p3.example: After the supervisor set things up, the department ran like clockwork — well paid and fulfilled.

p3.ru: показать как что делается, ввести в курс дела
p3.en: To teach someone how to do a job or task.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that showing someone the ropes prevents misconception and burnout.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, she showed him the ropes and the team ran like clockwork.
p3.example: She showed the new applicant the ropes before filling in for the supervisor.

p3.en: Used to summarise a long story or explanation briefly.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that — to cut a long story short — burnout leads to resignation.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, they were on the same page and the department ran like clockwork.
p3.word: to cut a long story short
p3.example: To cut a long story short, she turned down the low-paid role and set up her own business.

p3.en: To be paid a very small amount of money for work.
p3.ex1: Bear in mind that working for peanuts leads to burnout and inability to make ends meet.
p3.ex2: To cut a long story short, she turned down the offer — she refused to work for peanuts.
p3.example: She worked for peanuts in a low-paid department until she called it a day.

p4.en: The ability to use computers and related technology effectively.
p4.ex1: She turned down the low-paid offer and highlighted her computer literacy in the CV.
p4.ex2: To cut a long story short, computer literacy and fluency are key to workplace innovation.
p4.example: Bear in mind that computer literacy is a key guarantee for a well-paid, fulfilled role.

p4.en: The ability to speak or write a language smoothly and accurately.
p4.ex1: Bear in mind that fluency and computer literacy are key soft skills in any department.
p4.ex2: To cut a long story short, fluency and computer literacy guaranteed her the well-paid role.
p4.example: Fluency in English is a key guarantee for well-paid, innovative workplace positions.

p4.en: A formal promise that something will happen or be provided.
p4.ex1: Bear in mind that no job offers a guarantee — but fluency and innovation help.
p4.ex2: To cut a long story short, her computer literacy was the key guarantee that got her hired.
p4.example: Computer literacy and fluency were a key guarantee of her well-paid, fulfilled position.

p4.en: Most important; essential.
p4.ex1: Bear in mind that key soft skills like fluency and computer literacy prevent burnout.
p4.ex2: To cut a long story short, fluency was the key guarantee that made her application stand out.
p4.example: Computer literacy and fluency are key guarantees for a fulfilled, well-paid career.

p1.en: The quality of being easy to reach, use, or understand.
p1.ex1: The host city approved new regulation to ensure accessibility for all companions.
p1.ex2: Navigation and accessibility were key concerns for runners-up at the ceremony.
p1.example: Accessibility at the prestigious venue was improved for athletes with a disability.

p1.en: Very skilled or proficient at something.
p1.ex1: Adept runners-up overcome disturbing obstacles to prove their fitness.
p1.ex2: The skilled, adept companion tracked routes and secured approval for the ceremony.
p1.example: She was adept at navigation and tracking routes to the prestigious venue.

p1.en: Official agreement or permission for something.
p1.ex1: She received approval from the regulation committee for the accessible ceremony.
p1.ex2: RSVP confirmation served as proof of approval for the runner-up companion.
p1.example: The host city required legal approval before tracking athletes at the prestigious venue.

p1.en: To officially agree to something or think it is acceptable.
p1.ex1: She approved of the legal proof submitted by the skilled, adept companion.
p1.ex2: The committee approved of tracking runners-up at the prestigious ceremony.
p1.example: The host city approved of the regulation ensuring accessibility at the venue.

p1.en: A formal public event or celebration.
p1.ex1: Legal proof of disability accessibility was required before the ceremony RSVP.
p1.ex2: She was glued to the screen tracking the ceremony at the prestigious venue.
p1.example: The runner-up received approval to attend the prestigious ceremony at the host city venue.

p1.en: A person or animal with whom you spend time.
p1.ex1: The adept companion tracked the runner-up to ensure secure approval at the ceremony.
p1.ex2: A skilled companion proves indispensable when overcoming disturbing regulation barriers.
p1.example: Her companion helped navigate accessibility at the prestigious host city venue.

p1.en: A physical or mental condition that limits a person's movements or activities.
p1.ex1: She approved of the legal proof confirming disability accessibility at the ceremony venue.
p1.ex2: Overcoming a disability requires skilled companions, adept navigation, and secure tracking.
p1.example: Accessibility for athletes with a disability was a key regulation at the host city.

p1.en: Causing worry, anxiety, or distress.
p1.ex1: She found the tracking of privacy during the ceremony legally disturbing.
p1.ex2: The runner-up overcame disturbing obstacles to secure approval at the host city.
p1.example: The disturbing lack of accessibility at the prestigious venue was overcome with new regulation.

p1.en: The way something matches or suits a particular purpose or person.
p1.ex1: Her adept navigation skills were a natural fit for tracking the prestigious ceremony.
p1.ex2: A legal and secure fit between regulation and privacy was approved by the host city.
p1.example: The venue's accessibility was a perfect fit for athletes with a disability.

p1.en: Very recently; just made or prepared.
